text_sanskrit:
अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्त: सर्वं प्रवर्तते |
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विता: || 8||
transliteration:
ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate |
iti matvā bhajante māṁ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ ||
translation: I am the origin of all creation. Everything proceeds from Me. The wise who know this perfectly worship Me with great faith and devotion.
commentary_full: Krishna declares Himself as the ultimate cause of all creation. Everything in both material and spiritual realms originates from Him. Those who truly realize this develop deep devotion and worship Him with full faith and understanding.
commentary_summary: God is the ultimate source of all creation, and true realization of this leads to deep devotion.
theme: Supreme source of creation

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्त: परस्परम् |
कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च || 9||
transliteration:
mach-chittā mad-gata-prāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam |
kathayantaśh cha māṁ nityaṁ tuṣhyanti cha ramanti cha ||
translation: With their minds fixed on Me and their lives surrendered to Me, My devotees remain ever content in Me. They derive great satisfaction and bliss in enlightening one another about Me and in conversing about My glories.
commentary_full: Devotees remain deeply absorbed in God through constant remembrance, discussion, and sharing of His glories. Their love expresses through surrender of mind, life, and actions. This devotion brings them lasting joy, satisfaction, and spiritual fulfillment.
commentary_summary: Devotees remain absorbed in God through remembrance and discussion, finding joy and fulfillment in devotion.
theme: Joy of devotion

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
तेषां सततयुक्तानां भजतां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् |
ददामि बुद्धियोगं तं येन मामुपयान्ति ते || 10||
transliteration:
teṣhāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam |
dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ taṁ yena mām upayānti te ||
translation: To those whose minds are always united with Me in loving devotion, I give the divine knowledge by which they can attain Me.
commentary_full: Krishna explains that true knowledge of God is not achieved by intellect alone but through divine grace. He grants spiritual understanding to those who are devoted with love. This divine guidance leads the soul toward realization and union with Him.
commentary_summary: God grants divine knowledge to devoted souls, enabling them to attain Him through His grace.
theme: Divine grace and guidance

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
तेषामेवानुकम्पार्थमहमज्ञानजं तम: |
नाशयाम्यात्मभावस्थो ज्ञानदीपेन भास्वता || 11||
transliteration:
teṣhām evānukampārtham aham ajñāna-jaṁ tamaḥ |
nāśhayāmyātma-bhāva-stho jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā ||
translation: Out of compassion for them, I, dwelling within their hearts, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the luminous lamp of knowledge.
commentary_full: Krishna explains that divine grace actively removes ignorance from the devotee’s heart. This ignorance, symbolized as darkness, is dispelled by the light of divine knowledge granted by Him. Through this grace, the soul’s perception transforms, enabling it to realize God beyond material limitations.
commentary_summary: God removes ignorance through divine knowledge out of compassion for His devotees.
theme: Divine removal of ignorance

speaker: Arjuna
text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
परं ब्रह्म परं धाम पवित्रं परमं भवान् |
पुरुषं शाश्वतं दिव्यमादिदेवमजं विभुम् || 12||
आहुस्त्वामृषय: सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा |
असितो देवलो व्यास: स्वयं चैव ब्रवीषि मे || 13||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha |
paraṁ brahma paraṁ dhāma pavitraṁ paramaṁ bhavān |
puruṣhaṁ śhāśhvataṁ divyam ādi-devam ajaṁ vibhum ||
āhus tvām ṛiṣhayaḥ sarve devarṣhir nāradas tathā |
asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṁ chaiva bravīṣhi me ||
translation: Arjuna said: You are the Supreme Divine Personality, the Supreme Abode, the Supreme Purifier, the Eternal God, the Primal Being, the Unborn, and the Greatest. Great sages like Narad, Asit, Deval, and Vyas affirm this, and now You Yourself declare it to me.
commentary_full: Arjuna affirms Krishna’s supreme position based on both personal realization and authoritative testimony from sages. He rejects the idea of God being impersonal and recognizes Krishna as the ultimate reality. This marks a deep shift from doubt to complete conviction and surrender.
commentary_summary: Arjuna fully स्वीकारs Krishna as the Supreme, supported by both realization and scriptural authority.
theme: Recognition of the Supreme

speaker: Arjuna
text_sanskrit:
सर्वमेतदृतं मन्ये यन्मां वदसि केशव |
न हि ते भगवन्व्यक्तिं विदुर्देवा न दानवा: || 14||
transliteration:
sarvam etad ṛitaṁ manye yan māṁ vadasi keśhava |
na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṁ vidur devā na dānavāḥ ||
translation: O Krishna, I accept everything You have said as truth. Neither the gods nor the demons can understand Your true personality.
commentary_full: Arjuna expresses complete trust in Krishna’s words and acknowledges the limitations of even celestial beings in understanding God. This highlights that divine truth transcends intellectual and cosmic hierarchies.
commentary_summary: God’s true nature is beyond even gods and demons, and is accepted through faith.
theme: Transcendence of divine nature

speaker: Arjuna
text_sanskrit:
स्वयमेवात्मनात्मानं वेत्थ त्वं पुरुषोत्तम |
भूतभावन भूतेश देवदेव जगत्पते || 15||
transliteration:
swayam evātmanātmānaṁ vettha tvaṁ puruṣhottama |
bhūta-bhāvana bhūteśha deva-deva jagat-pate ||
translation: You alone know Yourself, O Supreme Person, Creator of all beings, Lord of all beings, God of gods, and Lord of the universe.
commentary_full: Arjuna emphasizes that only God can fully comprehend Himself, as finite beings cannot grasp the infinite. This reinforces the idea that divine knowledge is granted through grace rather than intellectual effort.
commentary_summary: Only God truly knows Himself; realization comes through His grace.
theme: Divine self-knowledge

speaker: Arjuna
text_sanskrit:
वक्तुमर्हस्यशेषेण दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतय: |
याभिर्विभूतिभिर्लोकानिमांस्त्वं व्याप्य तिष्ठसि || 16||
कथं विद्यामहं योगिंस्त्वां सदा परिचिन्तयन् |
केषु केषु च भावेषु चिन्त्योऽसि भगवन्मया || 17||
transliteration:
vaktum arhasyaśheṣheṇa divyā hyātma-vibhūtayaḥ |
yābhir vibhūtibhir lokān imāṁs tvaṁ vyāpya tiṣhṭhasi ||
kathaṁ vidyām ahaṁ yogins tvāṁ sadā parichintayan |
keṣhu keṣhu cha bhāveṣhu chintyo ’si bhagavan mayā ||
translation: Please describe Your divine glories by which You pervade all worlds. How can I know You and meditate upon You, and in what forms should I think of You?
commentary_full: Arjuna seeks practical guidance for devotion. He wants to understand how to perceive God in everyday life and maintain constant remembrance. This reflects the transition from philosophical understanding to applied spirituality.
commentary_summary: Arjuna seeks ways to perceive and meditate on God in daily life.
theme: Seeking practical devotion

speaker: Arjuna
text_sanskrit:
विस्तरेणात्मनो योगं विभूतिं च जनार्दन |
भूय: कथय तृप्तिर्हि शृण्वतो नास्ति मेऽमृतम् || 18||
transliteration:
vistareṇātmano yogaṁ vibhūtiṁ cha janārdana |
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛiptir hi śhṛiṇvato nāsti me ’mṛitam ||
translation: O Krishna, describe again in detail Your divine glories and manifestations. I can never tire of hearing Your nectar.
commentary_full: Arjuna expresses deep eagerness and joy in hearing about Krishna’s glories. Divine knowledge is described as nectar—satisfying yet increasing the desire for more. This reflects the nature of true devotion, where spiritual engagement brings both fulfillment and longing.
commentary_summary: Hearing about God brings endless joy and deepens the desire for devotion.
theme: Joy of divine knowledge

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतय: |
प्राधान्यत: कुरुश्रेष्ठ नास्त्यन्तो विस्तरस्य मे ||19||
transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha |
hanta te kathayiṣhyāmi divyā hyātma-vibhūtayaḥ |
prādhānyataḥ kuru-śhreṣhṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me ||
translation: The Lord said: I shall now briefly describe My divine glories to you, O best of the Kurus, for there is no end to their detail.
commentary_full: Krishna explains that His divine manifestations are infinite and cannot be fully enumerated. Therefore, He will describe only the most prominent ones. This highlights the boundless nature of divine power, qualities, and expressions.
commentary_summary: God’s glories are infinite; only a few can be described.
theme: Infinite nature of divine glories

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थित: |
अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च || 20||
transliteration:
aham ātmā guḍākeśha sarva-bhūtāśhaya-sthitaḥ |
aham ādiśh cha madhyaṁ cha bhūtānām anta eva cha ||
translation: I am seated in the heart of all beings, O Arjun. I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.
commentary_full: Krishna reveals His immanence—He resides within every being as the inner self. He is also the origin, sustainer, and final destination of all existence. This establishes both His closeness and His supremacy over all life.
commentary_summary: God resides within all beings and is their beginning, sustainer, and end.
theme: God as inner self of all beings

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान् |
मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी || 21||
transliteration:
ādityānām ahaṁ viṣhṇur jyotiṣhāṁ ravir anśhumān |
marīchir marutām asmi nakṣhatrāṇām ahaṁ śhaśhī ||
translation: Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among lights I am the radiant sun. Among the Maruts I am Marichi, and among stars I am the moon.
commentary_full: Krishna begins listing His divine manifestations by identifying Himself with the most prominent and powerful entities in different categories. These representations help devotees perceive His presence throughout creation.
commentary_summary: God is the highest and most radiant presence in all categories of existence.
theme: Divine manifestations in nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासव: |
इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना || 22||
transliteration:
vedānāṁ sāma-vedo ’smi devānām asmi vāsavaḥ |
indriyāṇāṁ manaśh chāsmi bhūtānām asmi chetanā ||
translation: I am the Samaveda among the Vedas and Indra among the gods. Among the senses I am the mind, and among living beings I am consciousness.
commentary_full: Krishna identifies Himself with the most significant elements of knowledge, power, and life. By doing so, He shows that intelligence, authority, and consciousness itself are expressions of His divine energy.
commentary_summary: God is the essence of knowledge, power, mind, and consciousness.
theme: Divine essence in knowledge and consciousness

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
रुद्राणां शङ्करश्चास्मि वित्तेशो यक्षरक्षसाम् |
वसूनां पावकश्चास्मि मेरु: शिखरिणामहम् || 23||
transliteration:
rudrāṇāṁ śhaṅkaraśh chāsmi vitteśho yakṣha-rakṣhasām |
vasūnāṁ pāvakaśh chāsmi meruḥ śhikhariṇām aham ||
translation: Among the Rudras I am Shankar; among Yakshas and Rakshasas I am Kuber. Among the Vasus I am fire, and among mountains I am Meru.
commentary_full: Krishna continues identifying Himself with the most powerful and prominent beings and elements. These examples emphasize that wherever greatness, strength, or excellence is seen, it reflects a fraction of His divine glory.
commentary_summary: All greatness and power in the universe reflect God’s divine glory.
theme: Divine presence in power and greatness

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् |
सेनानीनामहं स्कन्द: सरसामस्मि सागर: || 24||
transliteration:
purodhasāṁ cha mukhyaṁ māṁ viddhi pārtha bṛihaspatim |
senānīnām ahaṁ skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ ||
translation: Among priests I am Brihaspati; among military commanders I am Skanda; among bodies of water I am the ocean.
commentary_full: Krishna highlights His presence in leadership, wisdom, and vastness. The greatest representatives in each category symbolize His divine excellence and supremacy.
commentary_summary: God is reflected in the highest forms of wisdom, leadership, and vastness.
theme: Divine excellence in leadership and scale

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
महर्षीणां भृगुरहं गिरामस्म्येकमक्षरम् |
यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि स्थावराणां हिमालय: || 25||
transliteration:
maharṣhīṇāṁ bhṛigur ahaṁ girām asmyekam akṣharam |
yajñānāṁ japa-yajño ’smi sthāvarāṇāṁ himālayaḥ ||
translation: Among great sages I am Bhrigu; among sounds I am Om. Among sacrifices I am the chanting of the holy names, and among immovable things I am the Himalayas.
commentary_full: Krishna points to spiritual practices and natural wonders as manifestations of His glory. The sacred syllable Om and devotional chanting are highlighted as the most direct means of connecting with Him.
commentary_summary: God is present in sacred sound, devotion, and the grandeur of nature.
theme: Divine presence in spirituality and nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
अश्वत्थ: सर्ववृक्षाणां देवर्षीणां च नारद: |
गन्धर्वाणां चित्ररथ: सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनि: || 26||
transliteration:
aśhvatthaḥ sarva-vṛikṣhāṇāṁ devarṣhīṇāṁ cha nāradaḥ |
gandharvāṇāṁ chitrarathaḥ siddhānāṁ kapilo muniḥ ||
translation: Among trees I am the peepal tree; among celestial sages I am Narad. Among gandharvas I am Chitrarath, and among perfected beings I am Kapil Muni.
commentary_full: Krishna identifies Himself with the most revered and spiritually significant beings and entities. These examples highlight devotion, wisdom, and spiritual excellence as reflections of divine presence.
commentary_summary: God is reflected in the most sacred, wise, and spiritually elevated beings.
theme: Divine presence in spiritual greatness

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
उच्चै:श्रवसमश्वानां विद्धि माममृतोद्भवम् |
ऐरावतं गजेन्द्राणां नराणां च नराधिपम् || 27||
transliteration:
uchchaiḥśhravasam aśhvānāṁ viddhi mām amṛitodbhavam |
airāvataṁ gajendrāṇāṁ narāṇāṁ cha narādhipam ||
translation: Among horses I am Ucchaihshrava, born from nectar; among elephants I am Airavata, and among humans I am the king.
commentary_full: Krishna highlights supreme excellence in strength, majesty, and authority. These symbols represent the highest forms of power and leadership in their respective domains.
commentary_summary: God manifests as the highest power and authority in every category.
theme: Divine excellence in power and authority

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
आयुधानामहं वज्रं धेनूनामस्मि कामधुक् |
प्रजनश्चास्मि कन्दर्प: सर्पाणामस्मि वासुकि: || 28||
transliteration:
āyudhānām ahaṁ vajraṁ dhenūnām asmi kāmadhuk |
prajanaśh chāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ ||
translation: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am Kamadhenu. Among causes of procreation I am Kamdev, and among serpents I am Vasuki.
commentary_full: Krishna identifies Himself with forces that sustain, create, and protect life. Even natural desires, when aligned with dharma, are seen as divine expressions.
commentary_summary: Divine presence exists in power, sustenance, and righteous creation.
theme: Divine role in creation and power

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानां वरुणो यादसामहम् |
पितृणामर्यमा चास्मि यम: संयमतामहम् || 29||
transliteration:
anantaśh chāsmi nāgānāṁ varuṇo yādasām aham |
pitṝīṇām aryamā chāsmi yamaḥ sanyamatām aham ||
translation: Among serpents I am Anant; among aquatics I am Varun. Among ancestors I am Aryama, and among regulators I am Yama.
commentary_full: Krishna reveals His presence in cosmic order, justice, and continuity. Even forces like death and law are expressions of divine balance and governance.
commentary_summary: God manifests in cosmic order, justice, and regulation of life.
theme: Divine law and cosmic order

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां काल: कलयतामहम् |
मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम् || 30||
transliteration:
prahlādaśh chāsmi daityānāṁ kālaḥ kalayatām aham |
mṛigāṇāṁ cha mṛigendro ’haṁ vainateyaśh cha pakṣhiṇām ||
translation: Among demons I am Prahlad; among controllers I am time. Among animals I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda.
commentary_full: Krishna shows that even in opposing or diverse categories, the highest expression reflects divine glory. Time itself is the ultimate controller, emphasizing God’s supreme authority.
commentary_summary: God is present as the highest force even in opposing or powerful domains.
theme: Supreme control and dominance

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
पवन: पवतामस्मि राम: शस्त्रभृतामहम् |
झषाणां मकरश्चास्मि स्रोतसामस्मि जाह्नवी || 31||
transliteration:
pavanaḥ pavatām asmi rāmaḥ śhastra-bhṛitām aham |
jhaṣhāṇāṁ makaraśh chāsmi srotasām asmi jāhnavī ||
translation: Among purifiers I am the wind; among warriors I am Ram. Among aquatic creatures I am the crocodile, and among rivers I am the Ganges.
commentary_full: Krishna identifies with purity, strength, and sacredness. Natural elements and divine personalities alike become symbols of His presence.
commentary_summary: God is reflected in purity, strength, and sacred natural forces.
theme: Divine purity and strength

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
सर्गाणामादिरन्तश्च मध्यं चैवाहमर्जुन |
अध्यात्मविद्या विद्यानां वाद: प्रवदतामहम् || 32||
transliteration:
sargāṇām ādir antaśh cha madhyaṁ chaivāham arjuna |
adhyātma-vidyā vidyānāṁ vādaḥ pravadatām aham ||
translation: I am the beginning, middle, and end of creation. Among sciences I am spiritual knowledge, and among debates I am logical reasoning.
commentary_full: Krishna emphasizes that spiritual knowledge is the highest form of wisdom. Logical reasoning that leads to truth is also a reflection of divine intelligence.
commentary_summary: Spiritual knowledge and true reasoning are the highest expressions of divine wisdom.
theme: Supreme knowledge and truth

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
अक्षराणामकारोऽस्मि द्वन्द्व: सामासिकस्य च |
अहमेवाक्षय: कालो धाताहं विश्वतोमुख: || 33||
transliteration:
akṣharāṇām a-kāro ’smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya cha |
aham evākṣhayaḥ kālo dhātāhaṁ viśhvato-mukhaḥ ||
translation: Among letters I am ‘A’; among compounds I am the dual. I am eternal time, and among creators I am Brahma.
commentary_full: Krishna identifies Himself with foundational elements of language, time, and creation. These are the building blocks of knowledge and existence.
commentary_summary: God is present in the fundamental structures of language, time, and creation.
theme: Divine foundation of existence

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
मृत्यु: सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम् |
कीर्ति: श्रीर्वाक्च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृति: क्षमा || 34||
transliteration:
mṛityuḥ sarva-haraśh chāham udbhavaśh cha bhaviṣhyatām |
kīrtiḥ śhrīr vāk cha nārīṇāṁ smṛitir medhā dhṛitiḥ kṣhamā ||
translation: I am death that destroys all, and the origin of future beings. Among feminine qualities I am fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, courage, and forgiveness.
commentary_full: Krishna shows that both creation and destruction are divine processes. He also highlights noble qualities that uplift human character as manifestations of His energy.
commentary_summary: God is both destruction and creation, and the source of noble human qualities.
theme: Divine role in life cycles and virtues

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
बृहत्साम तथा साम्नां गायत्री छन्दसामहम् |
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽहमृतूनां कुसुमाकर: || 35||
transliteration:
bṛihat-sāma tathā sāmnāṁ gāyatrī chhandasām aham |
māsānāṁ mārga-śhīrṣho ’ham ṛitūnāṁ kusumākaraḥ ||
translation: Among hymns I am the Brihatsama; among meters I am the Gayatri. Among months I am Margashirsha, and among seasons I am spring.
commentary_full: Krishna identifies Himself with harmony, beauty, and balance in time and expression. These manifestations evoke devotion, joy, and aesthetic appreciation.
commentary_summary: God is present in harmony, beauty, and the most balanced aspects of time and expression.
theme: Divine beauty and harmony

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
द्यूतं छलयतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् |
जयोऽस्मि व्यवसायोऽस्मि सत्त्वं सत्त्ववतामहम् || 36||
transliteration:
dyūtaṁ chhalayatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham |
jayo ’smi vyavasāyo ’smi sattvaṁ sattvavatām aham ||
translation: I am the gambling of cheats, the brilliance of the brilliant. I am victory, determination, and the virtue of the virtuous.
commentary_full: Krishna explains that all abilities originate from Him, even those that may be misused. While divine energy empowers all actions, individuals are responsible for how they use it. Virtue, determination, and success are also expressions of divine strength.
commentary_summary: All abilities—good or misused—come from God, but responsibility lies with the individual.
theme: Divine source of abilities and responsibility

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
वृष्णीनां वासुदेवोऽस्मि पाण्डवानां धनञ्जय: |
मुनीनामप्यहं व्यास: कवीनामुशना कवि: || 37||
transliteration:
vṛiṣhṇīnāṁ vāsudevo ’smi pāṇḍavānāṁ dhanañjayaḥ |
munīnām apyahaṁ vyāsaḥ kavīnām uśhanā kaviḥ ||
translation: Among the Vrishnis I am Krishna; among the Pandavas I am Arjun. Among sages I am Vyas, and among thinkers I am Shukracharya.
commentary_full: Krishna identifies Himself with the most distinguished personalities in wisdom, devotion, and intellect. These figures represent excellence in their respective domains.
commentary_summary: God is reflected in the most उत्कृष्ट personalities across domains.
theme: Divine presence in great personalities

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
दण्डो दमयतामस्मि नीतिरस्मि जिगीषताम् |
मौनं चैवास्मि गुह्यानां ज्ञानं ज्ञानवतामहम् || 38||
transliteration:
daṇḍo damayatām asmi nītir asmi jigīṣhatām |
maunaṁ chaivāsmi guhyānāṁ jñānaṁ jñānavatām aham ||
translation: I am just punishment, proper conduct, silence among secrets, and wisdom among the wise.
commentary_full: Krishna emphasizes discipline, ethics, and wisdom as divine tools. Silence protects truth, and wisdom guides life toward higher understanding.
commentary_summary: Discipline, ethics, silence, and wisdom are divine expressions.
theme: Divine order and wisdom

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन |
न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम् || 39||
transliteration:
yach chāpi sarva-bhūtānāṁ bījaṁ tad aham arjuna |
na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṁ charācharam ||
translation: I am the seed of all beings. Nothing moving or non-moving can exist without Me.
commentary_full: Krishna establishes Himself as both the origin and essence of all existence. Every form of life depends on His sustaining power.
commentary_summary: God is the origin and sustaining force of all existence.
theme: God as the source of all existence

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परन्तप |
एष तूद्देशत: प्रोक्तो विभूतेर्विस्तरो मया || 40||
transliteration:
nānto ’sti mama divyānāṁ vibhūtīnāṁ parantapa |
eṣha tūddeśhataḥ prokto vibhūter vistaro mayā ||
translation: There is no end to My divine manifestations. What I have described is only a small sample.
commentary_full: Krishna clarifies that His glories are infinite. The examples given are only to help the mind connect with His presence.
commentary_summary: God’s manifestations are infinite; examples are only illustrative.
theme: Infinite divine glory

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा |
तत्देवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम् || 41||
transliteration:
yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṁ śhrīmad ūrjitam eva vā |
tat tad evāvagachchha tvaṁ mama tejo ’nśha-sambhavam ||
translation: Whatever is glorious, beautiful, or powerful—know it to be a spark of My splendor.
commentary_full: Krishna teaches that all excellence in the world is a reflection of divine energy. Recognizing this leads the mind toward God.
commentary_summary: All beauty and greatness are reflections of divine splendor.
theme: Divine reflection in excellence

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
अथवा बहुनैतेन किं ज्ञातेन तवार्जुन |
विष्टभ्याहमिदं कृत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत् || 42||
transliteration:
atha vā bahunaitena kiṁ jñātena tavārjuna |
viṣhṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛitsnam ekānśhena sthito jagat ||
translation: What need is there for all this knowledge? I sustain the entire universe with just a fraction of My being.
commentary_full: Krishna concludes by revealing His supreme transcendence. The entire universe exists within just a fraction of His infinite reality.
commentary_summary: The entire universe is sustained by just a fraction of God’s infinite power.
theme: Supreme transcendence of God

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
मदनुग्रहाय परमं गुह्यमध्यात्मसञ्ज्ञितम् |
यत्त्वयोक्तं वचस्तेन मोहोऽयं विगतो मम || 1||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
mad-anugrahāya paramaṁ guhyam adhyātma-sanjñitam
yat tvayoktaṁ vachas tena moho ’yaṁ vigato mama
translation: Arjun said: Having heard the supreme confidential spiritual knowledge, my illusion has now been dispelled.
commentary_full: Arjun expresses gratitude for Krishna’s teachings. He acknowledges that the knowledge has removed his ignorance and strengthened his understanding of the divine.
commentary_summary: Spiritual knowledge removes illusion and brings clarity.
theme: Removal of ignorance through divine knowledge

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
भवाप्ययौ हि भूतानां श्रुतौ विस्तरशो मया |
त्वत्त: कमलपत्राक्ष माहात्म्यमपि चाव्ययम् || 2||
transliteration:
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṁ śhrutau vistaraśho mayā
tvattaḥ kamala-patrākṣha māhātmyam api chāvyayam
translation: I have heard from You about the creation and dissolution of beings, and also Your eternal greatness.
commentary_full: Arjun affirms Krishna as the ultimate source of creation and destruction, recognizing His eternal and supreme nature.
commentary_summary: God is the eternal source of creation and dissolution.
theme: Divine supremacy over creation

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर |
द्रष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम || 3||
transliteration:
evam etad yathāttha tvam ātmānaṁ parameśhvara
draṣhṭum ichchhāmi te rūpam aiśhwaraṁ puruṣhottama
translation: O Supreme Lord, I wish to see Your divine cosmic form.
commentary_full: Having understood Krishna’s greatness intellectually, Arjun now desires direct realization through vision of the universal form.
commentary_summary: Desire to experience divine truth directly.
theme: Longing for divine vision

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
मन्यसे यदि तच्छक्यं मया द्रष्टुमिति प्रभो |
योगेश्वर ततो मे त्वं दर्शयात्मानमव्ययम् || 4||
transliteration:
manyase yadi tach chhakyaṁ mayā draṣhṭum iti prabho
yogeśhvara tato me tvaṁ darśhayātmānam avyayam
translation: If You think I am capable, please reveal Your imperishable form to me.
commentary_full: Arjun humbly submits to Krishna, recognizing that divine vision depends on God’s grace, not personal ability.
commentary_summary: Divine realization depends on grace, not ego.
theme: Dependence on divine grace

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
पश्य मे पार्थ रूपाणि शतशोऽथ सहस्रश: |
नानाविधानि दिव्यानि नानावर्णाकृतीनि च || 5||
transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
paśhya me pārtha rūpāṇi śhataśho ’tha sahasraśhaḥ
nānā-vidhāni divyāni nānā-varṇākṛitīni cha
translation: Behold My countless divine forms of various kinds, shapes, and colors.
commentary_full: Krishna begins revealing His universal form, emphasizing its infinite diversity and divine magnificence.
commentary_summary: God’s forms are infinite and diverse.
theme: Infinite forms of God

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
पश्यादित्यान्वसून् रुद्रानश्विनौ मरुतस्तथा |
बहून्यदृष्टपूर्वाणि पश्याश्चर्याणि भारत || 6||
transliteration:
paśhyādityān vasūn rudrān aśhvinau marutas tathā
bahūny adṛiṣhṭa-pūrvāṇi paśhyāśhcharyāṇi bhārata
translation: Behold the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Ashwini Kumars, and many unseen wonders.
commentary_full: Krishna reveals that all celestial beings and unseen marvels exist within His universal form.
commentary_summary: All divine beings exist within God’s universal form.
theme: Universe within God

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा |
दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षु: पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् || 8||
transliteration:
na tu māṁ śhakyase draṣhṭum anenaiva sva-chakṣhuṣhā
divyaṁ dadāmi te chakṣhuḥ paśhya me yogam aiśhwaram
translation: You cannot see Me with your physical eyes. I grant you divine vision to behold My form.
commentary_full: Divine reality cannot be perceived with ordinary senses. Spiritual perception requires divine grace and higher consciousness.
commentary_summary: Divine truth requires divine vision.
theme: Need for divine perception

speaker: Sanjay
text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एवमुक्त्वा ततो राजन्महायोगेश्वरो हरि: |
दर्शयामास पार्थाय परमं रूपमैश्वरम् || 9||
transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
evam uktvā tato rājan mahā-yogeśhvaro hariḥ
darśhayām āsa pārthāya paramaṁ rūpam aiśhwaram
translation: Sanjay said: Krishna then revealed His supreme divine form to Arjun.
commentary_full: The narration shifts to Sanjay, who describes Krishna revealing the universal form through divine grace.
commentary_summary: Krishna reveals His cosmic form through divine power.
theme: Revelation of the universal form

speaker: Sanjay
text_sanskrit:
अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् |
अनेकदिव्याभरणं दिव्यानेकोद्यतायुधम् || 10||
दिव्यमाल्याम्बरधरं दिव्यगन्धानुलेपनम् |
सर्वाश्चर्यमयं देवमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् || 11||
transliteration:
aneka-vaktra-nayanam anekādbhuta-darśhanam
aneka-divyābharaṇaṁ divyānekodyatāyudham
divya-mālyāmbara-dharaṁ divya-gandhānulepanam
sarvāśhcharya-mayaṁ devam anantaṁ viśhvato-mukham
translation: Arjun saw the cosmic form with countless faces and eyes, adorned with divine ornaments, holding many celestial weapons, wearing garlands and fragrant substances—an infinite, wondrous form facing all directions.
commentary_full: Sanjay describes the overwhelming vastness of Krishna’s universal form. It transcends all limitations of space, form, and perception, revealing infinite diversity and divine magnificence in a single unified vision.
commentary_summary: The universal form reveals infinite, all-encompassing divine diversity.
theme: Infinite cosmic manifestation of God

speaker: Sanjay
text_sanskrit:
दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्युगपदुत्थिता |
यदि भा: सदृशी सा स्याद्भासस्तस्य महात्मन: || 12||
transliteration:
divi sūrya-sahasrasya bhaved yugapad utthitā
yadi bhāḥ sadṛiśhī sā syād bhāsas tasya mahātmanaḥ
translation: If a thousand suns were to rise simultaneously in the sky, their radiance would not equal the splendor of that great form.
commentary_full: Sanjay uses a powerful metaphor to convey the unimaginable brilliance of the universal form. The comparison emphasizes that divine radiance far exceeds any known physical light.
commentary_summary: The divine form’s brilliance surpasses all known light.
theme: Unimaginable divine radiance

speaker: Sanjay
text_sanskrit:
तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा |
अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा || 13||
transliteration:
tatraika-sthaṁ jagat kṛitsnaṁ pravibhaktam anekadhā
apaśhyad deva-devasya śharīre pāṇḍavas tadā
translation: Arjun beheld the entire universe, divided in many ways, all situated in one place within the body of the Supreme Lord.
commentary_full: Sanjay describes the astonishing vision where Arjun sees the entirety of creation—countless universes and their divisions—contained within Krishna’s cosmic form. This reveals the non-dual nature of reality, where all multiplicity exists within the One Supreme Being.
commentary_summary: The entire universe exists within the divine form of God.
theme: Unity of all existence within God

speaker: Sanjay
text_sanskrit:
तत: स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जय: |
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत || 14||
transliteration:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣhṭo hṛiṣhṭa-romā dhanañjayaḥ
praṇamya śhirasā devaṁ kṛitāñjalir abhāṣhata
translation: Filled with wonder and awe, Arjun bowed his head to the Lord with folded hands and began to speak.
commentary_full: Arjun experiences intense devotional ecstasy, marked by physical symptoms like hair standing on end. His response reflects deep reverence and surrender before the divine cosmic vision.
commentary_summary: Arjun reacts with awe, devotion, and surrender.
theme: Devotional response to divine revelation

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे...
transliteration: paśhyāmi devāns tava deva dehe...
translation: I see all gods and beings within Your body, including Brahma, Shiva, sages, and divine serpents.
commentary_full: Arjun perceives all divine and cosmic entities within Krishna, affirming Him as the container of all existence.
commentary_summary: All divine beings exist within God.
theme: God as the container of all existence

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं...
transliteration: aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netraṁ...
translation: I see Your infinite form everywhere, without beginning, middle, or end.
commentary_full: Arjun realizes the boundless, infinite nature of the divine form that transcends space and time.
commentary_summary: God is infinite and limitless.
theme: Infinity of the divine

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च...
transliteration: kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ chakriṇaṁ cha...
translation: I see Your radiant form with crown, mace, and discus, shining like blazing suns.
commentary_full: The divine brilliance is overwhelming, symbolizing supreme power and majesty.
commentary_summary: God’s form radiates immense power and brilliance.
theme: Divine splendor

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं...
transliteration: tvam akṣharaṁ paramaṁ veditavyaṁ...
translation: You are the Supreme, eternal truth, the support of all creation and protector of dharma.
commentary_full: Arjun acknowledges Krishna as the ultimate reality described in scriptures.
commentary_summary: God is the supreme eternal truth.
theme: Recognition of supreme divinity

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: अनादिमध्यान्तमनन्तवीर्य...
transliteration: anādi-madhyāntam ananta-vīryam...
translation: You are without beginning, middle, or end, with infinite power, illuminating the universe.
commentary_full: God transcends time and space while sustaining the universe through divine energy.
commentary_summary: God is timeless and all-powerful.
theme: Timeless power of God

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि...
transliteration: dyāv ā-pṛithivyor idam antaraṁ hi...
translation: The entire universe is pervaded by You, and all worlds tremble in fear of Your form.
commentary_full: The cosmic form inspires both awe and fear, reflecting divine authority over all existence.
commentary_summary: God pervades everything and commands awe.
theme: Divine omnipresence and power

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: अमी हि त्वां सुरसङ्घा विशन्ति...
transliteration: amī hi tvāṁ sura-saṅghā viśhanti...
translation: Gods and sages enter You and praise You with devotion and fear.
commentary_full: Even divine beings revere and surrender to the cosmic form of God.
commentary_summary: All beings worship and surrender to God.
theme: Universal surrender to God

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: रुद्रादित्या वसवो ये च साध्या...
transliteration: rudrādityā vasavo ye cha sādhyā...
translation: All celestial beings behold You in wonder.
commentary_full: All classes of beings are amazed by the divine cosmic form.
commentary_summary: All beings are astonished by God.
theme: Universal amazement

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं...
transliteration: rūpaṁ mahat te bahu-vaktra-netraṁ...
translation: Seeing Your terrifying vast form, all worlds and I are filled with fear.
commentary_full: The overwhelming magnitude of God evokes fear alongside awe.
commentary_summary: God’s vast form inspires fear and awe.
theme: Fear of divine magnitude

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: नभ:स्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं...
transliteration: nabhaḥ-spṛiśhaṁ dīptam aneka-varṇaṁ...
translation: Seeing Your blazing form touching the sky, I lose peace and courage.
commentary_full: Arjun’s relationship shifts from friendship to reverence and fear due to divine revelation.
commentary_summary: Divine vision overwhelms Arjun emotionally.
theme: Transformation of devotion

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit: दंष्ट्राकरालानि च ते मुखानि...
transliteration: danṣhṭrā-karālāni cha te mukhāni...
translation: Seeing Your terrifying mouths like fire of destruction, I lose direction and seek Your mercy.
commentary_full: Arjun, overwhelmed by fear, surrenders completely and seeks divine grace.
commentary_summary: Fear leads to surrender and plea for mercy.
theme: Surrender before divine power

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
अमी च त्वां धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रा:
सर्वे सहैवावनिपालसङ्घै: |
भीष्मो द्रोण: सूतपुत्रस्तथासौ
सहास्मदीयैरपि योधमुख्यै: || 26||
वक्त्राणि ते त्वरमाणा विशन्ति
दंष्ट्राकरालानि भयानकानि |
केचिद्विलग्ना दशनान्तरेषु
सन्दृश्यन्ते चूर्णितैरुत्तमाङ्गै: || 27||
transliteration:
amī cha tvāṁ dhṛitarāśhtrasya putrāḥ
sarve sahaivāvani-pāla-saṅghaiḥ
bhīṣhmo droṇaḥ sūta-putras tathāsau
sahāsmadīyair api yodha-mukhyaiḥ
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśhanti
danṣhṭrā-karālāni bhayānakāni
kechid vilagnā daśhanāntareṣhu
sandṛiśhyante chūrṇitair uttamāṅgaiḥ
translation: I see all the sons of Dhritarashtra, along with their allied kings, including Bheeshma, Dronacharya, Karn, and also the generals from our side, rushing headlong into Your fearsome mouths. I see some with their heads smashed between Your terrible teeth.
commentary_full: What are the teeth of God that Arjun is referring to? He mentioned them in the previous verse as well. We use our teeth to grind our food. God's teeth are his force of destruction that grinds everyone to death with the passage of time. Arjun sees the great Kaurava generals—Bheeshma, Dronacharya, and Karn—and also many of the Pandava generals rushing headlong into the mouth of the Lord, to be ground between his teeth. He is beholding the imminent future in the cosmic form of God. Since God is beyond the limits of time, the past, present, and future are visible within him in the present. Bheeshma had continued to support Duryodhan despite knowing he was evil and was usurping the rights of the Pandavas. Thus, he was destined to die in this war of goodness versus evil. Dronacharya was the guru of martial arts for both the Kauravas and the Pandavas, but felt obliged to help Duryodhan because he was financially dependent upon him. Karn was the bosom friend of Duryodhan and so he fought from the Kaurava side. Since Karn had taken the side of Duryodhan in the war, he too was destined to die.
commentary_summary: Arjun beholds Bheeshma, Drona, Karna and other warriors being devoured by God's fearsome cosmic form, symbolizing the inevitable passage of time.
theme: Inevitability of destruction under divine cosmic time

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
यथा नदीनां बहवोऽम्बुवेगा:
समुद्रमेवाभिमुखा द्रवन्ति |
तथा तवामी नरलोकवीरा
विशन्ति वक्त्राण्यभिविज्वलन्ति || 28||
यथा प्रदीप्तं ज्वलनं पतङ्गा
विशन्ति नाशाय समृद्धवेगा: |
तथैव नाशाय विशन्ति लोका-
स्तवापि वक्त्राणि समृद्धवेगा: || 29||
transliteration:
yathā nadīnāṁ bahavo 'mbu-vegāḥ
samudram evābhimukhā dravanti
tathā tavāmī nara-loka-vīrā
viśhanti vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti
yathā pradīptaṁ jvalanaṁ pataṅgā
viśhanti nāśhāya samṛiddha-vegāḥ
tathaiva nāśhāya viśhanti lokās
tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛiddha-vegāḥ
translation: As many waves of the rivers flowing rapidly into the ocean, so are all these great warriors entering into Your blazing mouths. As moths rush with great speed into the fire to perish, so are all these armies entering with great speed into Your mouths.
commentary_full: There were many noble kings and warriors in the war, who fought as their duty and laid down their lives on the battlefield. Arjun compares them to river waves willingly merging into the ocean. There were also many others, who fought out of greed and self-interest. Arjun compares them with moths being lured ignorantly into the incinerating fire. But in both cases, they are marching rapidly toward their imminent death.
commentary_summary: Warriors rushing to their doom are compared to rivers merging into the ocean and moths flying into fire — both inevitable, one noble and one ignorant.
theme: The inexorable march of all beings toward death and divine will

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
लेलिह्यसे ग्रसमान: समन्ता-
ल्लोकान्समग्रान्वदनैर्ज्वलद्भि: |
तेजोभिरापूर्य जगत्समग्रं
भासस्तवोग्रा: प्रतपन्ति विष्णो || 30||
transliteration:
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantāl
lokān samagrān vadanair jvaladbhiḥ
tejobhir āpūrya jagat samagraṁ
bhāsas tavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣhṇo
translation: With Your fiery tongues You are licking up the hosts of living beings on all sides and devouring them with Your blazing mouths. O Vishnu, You are scorching the entire universe with the fierce, all-pervading rays of Your effulgence.
commentary_full: The Lord controls the world with grandiose forces of creation, maintenance, and annihilation. At present, he is being perceived by Arjun in this mode as the all-devouring force that is engulfing his friends and allies from all sides. Viewing the apparition of future destined events in the cosmic form of God, Arjun sees his enemies being wiped out in the imminent battle. He also sees many of his allies in the grip of death. Petrified by the spectacle he is seeing, Arjun supplicates before Shree Krishna in the next verse.
commentary_summary: Arjun sees the cosmic Vishnu devouring all creation with blazing mouths and fierce effulgence, overwhelming him with terror.
theme: God as the all-consuming destroyer of worlds

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
आख्याहि मे को भवानुग्ररूपो
नमोऽस्तु ते देववर प्रसीद |
विज्ञातुमिच्छामि भवन्तमाद्यं
न हि प्रजानामि तव प्रवृत्तिम् || 31||
transliteration:
ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugra-rūpo
namo 'stu te deva-vara prasīda
vijñātum ichchhāmi bhavantam ādyaṁ
na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛittim
translation: Tell me who You are, so fierce of form. O God of gods, I bow before You; please bestow Your mercy on me. You, who existed before all creation, I wish to know who You are, for I do not comprehend Your nature and workings.
commentary_full: Earlier, Arjun had requested to see the universal form. When Shree Krishna exhibited it, Arjun became bewildered and agitated. Having witnessed an almost unbelievable cosmic spectacle, he now wants to know the very heart of God's nature and purpose. Hence, he asks the question, "Who are you and what is your purpose?"
commentary_summary: Overwhelmed by the terrible cosmic form, Arjun humbly implores God to reveal his identity and purpose.
theme: Seeking to understand the nature and purpose of the Supreme

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
कालोऽस्मि लोकक्षयकृत्प्रवृद्धो
लोकान्समाहर्तुमिह प्रवृत्त: |
ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे
येऽवस्थिता: प्रत्यनीकेषु योधा: || 32||
transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
kālo 'smi loka-kṣhaya-kṛit pravṛiddho
lokān samāhartum iha pravṛittaḥ
ṛite 'pi tvāṁ na bhaviṣhyanti sarve
ye 'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣhu yodhāḥ
translation: The Supreme Lord said: I am mighty Time, the source of destruction that comes forth to annihilate the worlds. Even without your participation, the warriors arrayed in the opposing army shall cease to exist.
commentary_full: In response to Arjun's question regarding who he is, Shree Krishna reveals his nature as all-powerful Time, the destroyer of the universe. The word kāla is derived from kalayati, which means 'to take count of.' All events in nature get buried in time. When Oppenheimer witnessed the destruction of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, he quoted this verse: 'Time…I am the destroyer of all the worlds.' Time counts and controls the lifespan of all beings. It will determine when the great personalities like Bheeshma, Dronacharya, and Karn will meet their end. It will destroy the enemy army arrayed on the battlefield even without Arjun participating in the fight, because the Lord wants it to happen as a part of his grand scheme for the world.
commentary_summary: Krishna reveals himself as mighty Time, the inevitable destroyer of worlds, declaring that the opposing warriors are already as good as dead.
theme: God as Time — the ultimate destroyer of all creation

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
तस्मात्त्वमुत्तिष्ठ यशो लभस्व
जित्वा शत्रून्भुङ् क्ष्व राज्यं समृद्धम् |
मयैवैते निहता: पूर्वमेव
निमित्तमात्रं भव सव्यसाचिन् || 33||
transliteration:
tasmāt tvam uttiṣhṭha yaśho labhasva
jitvā śhatrūn bhuṅkṣhva rājyaṁ samṛiddham
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva
nimitta-mātraṁ bhava savya-sāchin
translation: Therefore, arise and attain honor! Conquer your foes and enjoy prosperous rulership. These warriors stand already slain by Me, and you will only be an instrument of My work, O expert archer.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna has revealed to Arjun his will that the Kauravas should perish and the kingdom of Hastinapur should be administered by the Pandavas in accordance with rules of dharma. He has already decided the annihilation of the unrighteous and the victory of the righteous as the outcome of the battle. His grand scheme for the welfare of the world cannot be averted by any means. He now informs Arjun that he wishes him to be the nimitta-mātram, or the instrument of his work. God does not need the help of a human for his work, but humans attain eternal welfare by working to fulfill God's wish. Opportunities that come our way to accomplish something for the pleasure of the Lord are a very special blessing. Shree Krishna encourages Arjun by reminding him of his exceptional skills in archery, addressing him as savya-sāchin, meaning expert archer who is admirably ambidextrous.
commentary_summary: Krishna urges Arjun to arise and fight, for the enemies are already slain by divine will, and Arjun is merely an instrument of God's cosmic design.
theme: Human beings as instruments of divine cosmic purpose

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
द्रोणं च भीष्मं च जयद्रथं च
कर्णं तथान्यानपि योधवीरान् |
मया हतांस्त्वं जहि मा व्यथिष्ठा
युध्यस्व जेतासि रणे सपत्नान् || 34||
transliteration:
droṇaṁ cha bhīṣhmaṁ cha jayadrathaṁ cha
karṇaṁ tathānyān api yodha-vīrān
mayā hatāṁs tvaṁ jahi mā vyathiṣhṭhā
yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān
translation: Dronacharya, Bheeshma, Jayadratha, Karn, and other brave warriors have already been killed by Me. Therefore, slay them without being disturbed. Just fight and you will be victorious over your enemies in battle.
commentary_full: Many of the generals on the side of the Kauravas were heretofore undefeated in combat. Jayadrath had the boon that whoever caused his head to fall on the ground would instantly have his own head burst. Karn had a special weapon called 'Shakti' given by Indra, which would slay anyone against whom it was used. Dronacharya had received the knowledge of all weapons from Parshuram, an Avatara of God. Bheeshma had a boon that he would only die when he chose to. And yet, if God wished them to die in the battle, nothing could save them. Shree Krishna says he has already decided the outcome, but he wishes Arjun to be the medium to accomplish it and receive the glory of the conquest. Just as devotees wish to glorify God, it is God's nature to glorify his devotees. Hence, Shree Krishna wishes people to say, 'Arjun fought so valiantly that he secured victory for the Pandavas.'
commentary_summary: Krishna assures Arjun that all the great Kaurava warriors are already slain by divine decree, urging him to fight without fear and claim victory.
theme: Divine assurance of victory to the righteous warrior

speaker: Sanjay
text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं केशवस्य
कृताञ्जलिर्वेपमान: किरीटी |
नमस्कृत्वा भूय एवाह कृष्णं
सगद्गदं भीतभीत: प्रणम्य || 35||
transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
etach chhrutvā vachanaṁ keśhavasya
kṛitāñjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī
namaskṛitvā bhūya evāha kṛiṣhṇaṁ
sa-gadgadaṁ bhīta-bhītaḥ praṇamya
translation: Sanjay said: Hearing these words of Keshav, Arjun trembled with dread. With palms joined, he bowed before Shree Krishna and spoke in a faltering voice, overwhelmed with fear.
commentary_full: Here, Arjun is referred to as 'the crowned one.' He had once helped Indra kill two demons. As a token of his pleasure, Indra had placed a dazzling crown on his head. Sanjay deliberately uses the word 'kiriti' (crowned one) to hint to the old king Dhritarashtra that his sons, the Kauravas, will lose the throne to the Pandavas in the impending war.
commentary_summary: Sanjay narrates how Arjun, trembling with fear after hearing Krishna's words, bowed and spoke in a faltering voice.
theme: The overwhelming effect of witnessing divine power

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या
जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च |
रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति
सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घा: || 36||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sthāne hṛiṣhīkeśha tava prakīrtyā
jagat prahṛiṣhyaty anurajyate cha
rakṣhānsi bhītāni diśho dravanti
sarve namasyanti cha siddha-saṅghāḥ
translation: Arjun said: O Master of the senses, it is but apt that the universe rejoices in giving You praise and is enamored by You. Demons flee fearfully from You in all directions and hosts of perfected saints bow to You.
commentary_full: In this verse and the next ten, Arjun eulogizes Shree Krishna's glories from various perspectives. He uses the word sthāne, meaning 'it is but apt.' It is but natural that the people of a kingdom who accept the sovereignty of their king delight in glorifying him. It is also natural that those who harbor enmity toward the king fear him and flee from his presence. Arjun draws a parallel, saying that it is only appropriate that the world glorifies their Supreme Lord, the demons become frightened of him, and the saintly personalities offer devotional prayers to him.
commentary_summary: Arjun praises the Lord, saying it is perfectly fitting that the universe rejoices in His glory while demons flee and saints bow in devotion.
theme: The natural response of creation to divine supremacy

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्
गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे |
अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवास
त्वमक्षरं सदसतत्परं यत् || 37||
transliteration:
kasmāch cha te na nameran mahātman
garīyase brahmaṇo 'py ādi-kartre
ananta deveśha jagan-nivāsa
tvam akṣharaṁ sad-asat tat paraṁ yat
translation: O Great One, who are even greater than Brahma, the original creator, why should they not bow to you? O Limitless One, O Lord of the devatās, O Refuge of the universe, You are the imperishable reality beyond both the manifest and the non-manifest.
commentary_full: Justifying why the behavior mentioned in the previous verse is apt, Arjun uses the words 'kasmāchcha tena', meaning 'why should they not.' Why shouldn't all living beings offer their humble respects to the Supreme Lord, when the entire creation emanates from him, is sustained by him, and shall merge back into him? He is everything that is manifest in creation because it is all his energy. He is also everything that remains unmanifest because it is his latent energy. And yet he is beyond both the manifest and the unmanifest. Arjun specifically mentions that Shree Krishna is greater than the secondary creator Brahma. Although Brahma is considered the senior most grandsire of the world, Shree Krishna is Brahma's Grandsire — Brahma was born from the lotus that grew from the navel of Lord Vishnu, who is an expansion of Shree Krishna.
commentary_summary: Arjun justifies universal worship of Krishna, who is greater than Brahma himself — the imperishable source beyond both manifest and unmanifest reality.
theme: Krishna as the supreme cause beyond Brahma and all creation

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
त्वमादिदेव: पुरुष: पुराणस्-
 त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् |
वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धाम
 त्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप || 38||
transliteration:
tvam ādi-devaḥ puruṣhaḥ purāṇas
tvam asya viśhvasya paraṁ nidhānam
vettāsi vedyaṁ cha paraṁ cha dhāma
tvayā tataṁ viśhvam ananta-rūpa
translation: You are the primeval God and the original Divine Personality; You are the sole resting place of this universe. You are both the knower and the object of knowledge; You are the Supreme Abode. O possessor of infinite forms, You alone pervade the entire universe.
commentary_full: Arjun addresses Shree Krishna as the original Divine Person, the cause of all causes. Every object and every personality has a cause, or a source, from which it came into being. Even Lord Vishnu has a cause — he is an expansion of Shree Krishna. However, Shree Krishna is not the expansion of any personality. He is the causeless first cause of everything that exists. Shree Krishna is omniscient—the knower of everything. Further, he is also the object of all knowledge. Jagadguru Shree Kripaluji Maharaj states: 'Whatever work is done in the service of God, know that truly to be karma. Whatever knowledge enhances our love for God, know that to be true jnana.' Hence, Shree Krishna is both the knower and the object of knowledge.
commentary_summary: Arjun praises Krishna as the primeval God, the resting place of the universe, the knower and object of all knowledge, pervading all with infinite forms.
theme: Krishna as the eternal first cause and all-pervading supreme reality

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुण: शशाङ्क:
प्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च |
नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्व:
पुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते || 39||
transliteration:
vāyur yamo 'gnir varuṇaḥ śhaśhāṅkaḥ
prajāpatis tvaṁ prapitāmahaśh cha
namo namas te 'stu sahasra-kṛitvaḥ
punaśh cha bhūyo 'pi namo namas te
translation: You are Vāyu (god of wind), Yamraj (god of death), Agni (god of fire), Varuṇ (god of water), and Chandra (moon-god). You are the creator Brahma, and the Great-grandfather of all beings. I offer my salutations unto You a thousand times, again and yet again!
commentary_full: Experiencing profuse reverence toward Shree Krishna, Arjun is offering repeated obeisances sahasra-kṛitvaḥ (thousands and thousands of times). During Diwali celebrations in India, sugar sweets are made in many shapes — elephant, horse, man, woman, dog, etc. But the ingredient in all of them is the same sugar. Similarly, the celestial gods have their distinct personalities and unique set of duties to discharge in the administration of the world. However, the same one God sitting in all of them manifests the special powers they possess. Just as gold is not an ornament but ornaments are golden, likewise God is all the devatās but the devatās are not God. Hence, Arjun says that Shree Krishna is also Vāyu, Yamrāj, Agni, Varuṇ, Chandra, and Brahma.
commentary_summary: Arjun salutes Krishna as all the cosmic deities — Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, Chandra, Brahma — and as the Great-grandfather of all beings.
theme: God as the underlying reality of all celestial deities

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
नम: पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्ते
नमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व |
अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वं
सर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्व: || 40||
transliteration:
namaḥ purastād atha pṛiṣhṭhatas te
namo 'stu te sarvata eva sarva
ananta-vīryāmita-vikramas tvaṁ
sarvaṁ samāpnoṣhi tato 'si sarvaḥ
translation: O Lord of infinite power, my salutations to You from the front and the rear, indeed from all sides! You possess infinite valor and might and pervade everything, and thus, You are everything.
commentary_full: Arjun continues with his glorification of Shree Krishna by declaring him as ananta-vīrya (possessing infinite strength) and ananta-vikramaḥ (immeasurably powerful). Overcome with awe, he offers his salutations to Shree Krishna from all sides, repeatedly exclaiming Namaḥ! Namaḥ! (I bow down to you again and again).
commentary_summary: Arjun offers salutations to Krishna from all directions, declaring Him to be of infinite power and valor who pervades and is everything.
theme: Surrendering to the all-pervading infinite divine power

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तं
 हे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति |
अजानता महिमानं तवेदं
मया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि || 41||
यच्चावहासार्थमसत्कृतोऽसि
विहारशय्यासनभोजनेषु |
एकोऽथवाप्यच्युत तत्समक्षं
तत्क्षामये त्वामहमप्रमेयम् || 42||
transliteration:
sakheti matvā prasabhaṁ yad uktaṁ
he kṛiṣhṇa he yādava he sakheti
ajānatā mahimānaṁ tavedaṁ
mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi
yach chāvahāsārtham asat-kṛito 'si
vihāra-śhayyāsana-bhojaneṣhu
eko 'tha vāpy achyuta tat-samakṣhaṁ
tat kṣhāmaye tvām aham aprameyam
translation: Thinking of You as my friend, I presumptuously addressed You as, "O Krishna," "O Yadav," "O my dear Friend." I was ignorant of Your majesty, showing negligence and undue affection. And if, jestfully, I treated You with disrespect, while playing, resting, sitting, eating, when alone, or before others—for all that I crave forgiveness.
commentary_full: Having seen the universal form of God, Arjun is now painfully aware that Shree Krishna is not merely his friend and comrade-in-arms, but is also the Supreme Divine Personality, whom even the devatās, gandharvas, siddhas, etc. venerate. Thus, he feels regret for the disrespect he thinks he may have shown toward Shree Krishna by audaciously looking upon him as a mere friend. As an indication of respect, those who are venerated are not called by their first names. He is worried that due to excessive familiarity, he had put himself on equal status with God and had presumptuously addressed him with affectionate vocatives, such as 'My friend,' 'My dear buddy,' and 'O Krishna.' So he implores forgiveness for whatever he may have done in forgetfulness of the divinity of Shree Krishna's personality.
commentary_summary: Arjun apologizes for having addressed Krishna informally as a friend, not knowing His supreme divine majesty, and begs forgiveness for all past disrespect.
theme: The tension between intimate devotion and reverence for divine supremacy

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य
त्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् |
न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिक: कुतोऽन्यो
लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव || 43||
transliteration:
pitāsi lokasya charācharasya
tvam asya pūjyaśh cha gurur garīyān
na tvat-samo 'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto 'nyo
loka-traye 'py apratima-prabhāva
translation: You are the Father of the entire universe, of all moving and non-moving beings. You are the most deserving of worship and the Supreme Spiritual Master. When there is none equal to You in all the three worlds, then who can possibly be greater than You, O Possessor of incomparable power?
commentary_full: Arjun says that Shree Krishna is the greatest and the senior most. The father is always senior to the son. Shree Krishna is the father of the father… of all the fathers that exist. Similarly, he is the spiritual master of the spiritual master of all the spiritual masters that are present. The first spiritual master was the creator Brahma, who passed on the knowledge to his disciple. However, Brahma received the Vedic knowledge from Shree Krishna. The Shrimad Bhagavatam states: 'Shree Krishna imparted Vedic knowledge into the heart of the first-born Brahma.' Thus, he is the supreme spiritual master. The Shwetashvatar Upanishad states: 'Nobody is equal to God, nor is anyone superior to him.' Realizing Shree Krishna to be that same Supreme Lord of the Vedas, Arjun is declaring these attributes regarding him.
commentary_summary: Arjun declares Krishna as the Father of all creation and supreme Guru, incomparable and without equal in all the three worlds.
theme: Krishna as the supreme Father and Teacher of all existence

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायं
प्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् |
पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्यु:
प्रिय: प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् || 44||
transliteration:
tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṁ
prasādaye tvām aham īśham īḍyam
piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ
priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum
translation: Therefore, O adorable Lord, bowing deeply and prostrating before You, I implore You for Your grace. As a father tolerates his son, a friend forgives his friend, and a lover pardons the beloved, please forgive me for my offences.
commentary_full: Considering his behavior as transgressions toward God, Arjun is asking for pardon. While interacting with Shree Krishna—playing, eating, jesting, talking, and resting—he did not show the respect that is appropriate toward the Supreme Almighty. However, no one minds transgressions when they are made because of a high level of intimacy shared with the other person. No government officer has the privilege to joke with the President of a country, yet the President's personal friend teases him and jests with him. Similarly, Arjun's intimate dealings with Shree Krishna were not transgressions; they were gestures of the depth of his loving devotion in the sentiment of being a friend. Yet, a devotee is by nature humble, and so, out of humility, he feels that he may have committed transgressions, and hence he is asking for forgiveness.
commentary_summary: Arjun prostrates before Krishna and begs forgiveness for past disrespect, comparing the divine relationship to that of parent and child, friend and friend, or beloved and lover.
theme: Devotee's heartfelt plea for divine forgiveness and grace

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा
भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे |
तदेव मे दर्शय देवरूपं
प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास || 45||
transliteration:
adṛiṣhṭa-pūrvaṁ hṛiṣhito 'smi dṛiṣhṭvā
bhayena cha pravyathitaṁ mano me
tad eva me darśhaya deva rūpaṁ
prasīda deveśha jagan-nivāsa
translation: Having seen Your universal form that I had never seen before, I feel great joy. And yet, my mind trembles with fear. Please have mercy on me and again show me Your pleasing form, O God of gods, O Abode of the universe.
commentary_full: There are two kinds of bhakti — aishwarya bhakti and madhurya bhakti. Aishwarya bhakti is where the devotee is motivated by contemplating upon the almighty aspect of God, with awe and reverence as the dominant sentiment. Madhurya bhakti is where the devotee feels an intimate personal relationship with God. Arjun is a sakhya bhav devotee and relishes a fraternal relationship with the Lord. On seeing the universal form of God, Arjun experienced tremendous awe and reverence, and yet he longed for the sweetness of sakhya bhav that he was used to savoring. Hence, he prays to Shree Krishna to hide the almighty form and again show his human form.
commentary_summary: Arjun, simultaneously filled with joy and terror at the cosmic form, pleads with Krishna to return to His familiar, gentle divine form.
theme: The devotee's longing to return from cosmic awe to intimate devotion

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्त-
मिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव |
तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेन
सहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते || 46||
transliteration:
kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ chakra-hastam
ichchhāmi tvāṁ draṣhṭum ahaṁ tathaiva
tenaiva rūpeṇa chatur-bhujena
sahasra-bāho bhava viśhva-mūrte
translation: O Thousand-armed One, though You are the embodiment of all creation, I wish to see You in Your four-armed form, carrying the mace and disc, and wearing the crown.
commentary_full: By special grace, Arjun has been shown the cosmic form that is not easily seen by anyone. Arjun has realized that Shree Krishna is much more than merely his friend. His divine personality encompasses unlimited universes. Yet, Arjun is not attracted by the infinite opulences and is not interested in doing aishwarya bhakti of God Almighty. Rather, he prefers seeing that Almighty Lord in the human form, so that he can relate to him as before, like a friend. Addressing Lord Krishna as sahasra-bāho, meaning 'thousand-armed one,' Arjun is specifically requesting to see the chatur-bhuj rūp, or four-armed form of Lord Krishna.
commentary_summary: Arjun requests Krishna to withdraw the cosmic form and appear again in His familiar, gentle four-armed form adorned with crown, mace, and disc.
theme: Preference for the personal form of God over the formless cosmic vision

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मया प्रसन्नेन तवार्जुनेदं
रूपं परं दर्शितमात्मयोगात् |
तेजोमयं विश्वमनन्तमाद्यं
यन्मे त्वदन्येन न दृष्टपूर्वम् || 47||
transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṁ
rūpaṁ paraṁ darśhitam ātma-yogāt
tejo-mayaṁ viśhvam anantam ādyaṁ
yan me tvad anyena na dṛiṣhṭa-pūrvam
translation: The Lord said: Arjun, being pleased with you, by My Yogmaya power, I gave you a vision of My resplendent, unlimited, and primeval cosmic form. No one before you has ever seen it.
commentary_full: Since Arjun had become fearful and beseeched that the cosmic form be hidden, Shree Krishna now pacifies him by explaining that there is no need to be scared. He had bestowed a vision of his universal form by his grace, not as a form of punishment, but because he was very pleased with Arjun. He uses hyperbole to stress how rare it is to see the universal form, by saying that Arjun is the first one to see it. Although Duryodhan and Yashoda were also given a glimpse of the universal form, it was not to this intensity, depth, and magnitude. Shree Krishna bestowed this divine vision upon Arjun with the help of his Yogmaya energy — his divine all-powerful energy. It is by virtue of this Yogmaya energy that God can do the possible, the impossible, and the contradictory at the same time.
commentary_summary: Krishna explains that He showed Arjun the unprecedented cosmic form out of divine grace through Yogmaya — a vision never before seen by any mortal.
theme: The cosmic form as a rare gift of divine grace, not a fearful display

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
न वेदयज्ञाध्ययनैर्न दानै-
र्न च क्रियाभिर्न तपोभिरुग्रै: |
एवंरूप: शक्य अहं नृलोके
द्रष्टुं त्वदन्येन कुरुप्रवीर || 48||
transliteration:
na veda-yajñādhyayanair na dānair
na cha kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ
evaṁ-rūpaḥ śhakya ahaṁ nṛi-loke
draṣhṭuṁ tvad anyena kuru-pravīra
translation: Not by study of the Vedas, nor by the performance of sacrifice, rituals, or charity, nor even by practicing severe austerities, has any mortal ever seen what you have seen, O best of the Kuru warriors.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna declares that no amount of self-effort — the study of the Vedic texts, performance of ritualistic ceremonies, undertaking of severe austerities, abstinence from food, or generous acts of charity — is sufficient to bestow a vision of the cosmic form of God. This is only possible by his divine grace. The Vedas state: 'Without being anointed in the nectar of the grace of the Supreme Lord, nobody can see him.' Our physical eyes are made from matter, and hence all that we can see is also material. The Supreme Lord is non-material — he is divine. To have a vision of his divine form we need divine eyes, which God bestows through his grace.
commentary_summary: No Vedic study, sacrifice, charity, or austerity can grant the vision of God's cosmic form — only divine grace makes it possible.
theme: Divine grace as the sole means of beholding the cosmic form

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
मा ते व्यथा मा च विमूढभावो
दृष्ट्वा रूपं घोरमीदृङ्ममेदम् |
व्यपेतभी: प्रीतमना: पुनस्त्वं
तदेव मे रूपमिदं प्रपश्य || 49||
transliteration:
mā te vyathā mā cha vimūḍha-bhāvo
dṛiṣhṭvā rūpaṁ ghoram īdṛiṅ mamedam
vyapeta-bhīḥ prīta-manāḥ punas tvaṁ
tad eva me rūpam idaṁ prapaśhya
translation: Be neither afraid nor bewildered on seeing this terrible form of Mine. Be free from fear and with a cheerful heart, behold Me once again in My personal form.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna continues to pacify Arjun that rather than being scared, he should feel privileged to be blessed with a vision of the cosmic form. Further, he tells Arjun to behold his personal form again and shed his fear.
commentary_summary: Krishna reassures Arjun to cast aside fear and behold His gentle personal form once again with a joyful heart.
theme: Divine compassion in transitioning from cosmic awe to personal warmth

speaker: Sanjay
text_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच |
इत्यर्जुनं वासुदेवस्तथोक्त्वा
स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भूय: |
आश्वासयामास च भीतमेनं
भूत्वा पुन: सौम्यवपुर्महात्मा || 50||
transliteration:
sañjaya uvācha
ity arjunaṁ vāsudevas tathoktvā
svakaṁ rūpaṁ darśhayām āsa bhūyaḥ
āśhvāsayām āsa cha bhītam enaṁ
bhūtvā punaḥ saumya-vapur mahātmā
translation: Sanjay said: Having spoken thus, the compassionate son of Vasudev displayed His personal (four-armed) form again. Then, He further consoled the frightened Arjun by assuming His gentle (two-armed) form.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna hid the vision of his cosmic form, and manifested before Arjun in his four-armed form, which is adorned with a golden diadem, disc, mace, and lotus flower. The four-armed form of Shree Krishna evokes the sentiment of awe and reverence, much like the sentiments of the citizens of a kingdom toward their king. However, Arjun was a sakhā (friend) of Shree Krishna, and devotion dominated by the sentiment of awe and reverence would never satisfy him. Hence, to conform to Arjun's sentiment of sakhya bhāv devotion, Shree Krishna finally hid even his four-armed form and transformed into his original two-armed form.
commentary_summary: Sanjay narrates how Krishna, having spoken, first showed His four-armed form and then His familiar two-armed form to console the frightened Arjun.
theme: God's compassionate withdrawal of the cosmic form for the devotee's comfort

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
दृष्ट्वेदं मानुषं रूपं तव सौम्यं जनार्दन |
इदानीमस्मि संवृत्त: सचेता: प्रकृतिं गत: || 51||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
dṛiṣhṭvedaṁ mānuṣhaṁ rūpaṁ tava saumyaṁ janārdana
idānīm asmi saṁvṛittaḥ sa-chetāḥ prakṛitiṁ gataḥ
translation: Arjun said: O Shree Krishna, seeing Your gentle human form (two-armed), I have regained my composure and my mind is restored to normal.
commentary_full: Seeing Shree Krishna in his beautiful two-armed form reconfirmed and strengthened Arjun's sentiment of sakhya bhāv. Thus, Arjun says he has regained his composure and is back to normal. Seeing Shree Krishna's pastimes with the Pandavas, the celestial sage Narad had earlier told Arjun's elder brother, King Yudhishthir: 'Shree Krishna resides in your house and lives with you just like your brother.' Thus, Arjun was habituated to having the privilege of interacting with the Lord as a brother and friend.
commentary_summary: Arjun's mind is restored to calm and normalcy upon beholding Krishna's gentle two-armed human form again.
theme: The restorative power of the personal form of God for a loving devotee

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम |
देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिण: || 52||
नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया |
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा || 53||
transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
su-durdarśham idaṁ rūpaṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi yan mama
devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṁ darśhana-kāṅkṣhiṇaḥ
nāhaṁ vedair na tapasā na dānena na chejyayā
śhakya evaṁ-vidho draṣhṭuṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi māṁ yathā
translation: The Supreme Lord said: This form of Mine that you are seeing is exceedingly difficult to behold. Even the celestial gods are eager to see it. Neither by the study of the Vedas, nor by penance, charity, or fire sacrifices, can I be seen as you have seen Me.
commentary_full: Having shown Arjun the cosmic form and praised it as unavailable to anyone but him, Shree Krishna does not want Arjun to slacken his love for the personal form of God. Hence, Shree Krishna says that the way in which Arjun sees God is exceedingly rare. He emphasizes that even the celestial gods yearn to realize God in his two-armed personal form as he is standing before Arjun. This is not possible by any amount of Vedic studies, austerities, or fire sacrifices. The basic spiritual principle is that God cannot be known by the strength of one's efforts. However, those who engage in devotion to him become recipients of his grace. Then, by virtue of his grace, they are easily able to know him.
commentary_summary: Krishna declares that even the celestial gods long to see His personal form, which no amount of Vedic study, austerity, or sacrifice can reveal.
theme: The personal form of God as more precious and rare than even the cosmic vision

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्य अहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन |
ज्ञातुं द्रष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परन्तप || 54||
transliteration:
bhaktyā tv ananyayā śhakya aham evaṁ-vidho 'rjuna
jñātuṁ draṣhṭuṁ cha tattvena praveṣhṭuṁ cha parantapa
translation: O Arjun, by unalloyed devotion alone can I be known as I am, standing before you. Thereby, on receiving My divine vision, O scorcher of foes, one can enter into union with Me.
commentary_full: In this verse, Shree Krishna emphasizes bhakti as the means for attaining him. Earlier, in verse 11.48, he had stated that his universal form can be seen only by devotion. Now, Shree Krishna emphatically declares that his two-armed form can only be realized through bhakti. This has been repeatedly stated in the Vedic scriptures. The Mathar Shruti states: 'Devotion alone will unite us with God; devotion alone will help us see him; devotion alone will help us attain him; God is enslaved by true devotion, which is the best of all paths.' The Bhagavatam states: 'I am only attained through bhakti. Those who engage in my bhakti with faith are very dear to me.' The Ramayana states: 'Without devotion, one can never attain God, no matter how much one endeavors through the practice of ashtanga yoga, austerities, knowledge, and detachment.'
commentary_summary: Krishna declares that only pure, unalloyed devotion can enable one to truly know, see, and enter into union with God.
theme: Pure devotion (bhakti) as the only path to knowing and merging with God

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
मत्कर्मकृन्मत्परमो मद्भक्त: सङ्गवर्जित: |
निर्वैर: सर्वभूतेषु य: स मामेति पाण्डव || 55||
transliteration:
mat-karma-kṛin mat-paramo mad-bhaktaḥ saṅga-varjitaḥ
nirvairaḥ sarva-bhūteṣhu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava
translation: Those who perform all their duties for My sake, who depend upon Me and are devoted to Me, who are free from attachment, and are without malice toward all beings, such devotees certainly come to Me.
commentary_full: At the end of the ninth chapter, Shree Krishna had told Arjun to fix his mind upon him and be devoted to him. Now, he concludes this chapter by highlighting five characteristics of those who are engaged in exclusive devotion: They perform all their duties for God's sake, consecrating every act to him. They depend entirely upon God and not upon their own spiritual practices. They are devoted exclusively to God without feeling the need for other spiritual practices. They are free of attachment, since devotion requires the engagement of the mind which is only possible if the mind is detached from the world. And they are without malice toward all beings, since if the heart fills up with malice it will not remain exclusive toward God. Thus, exclusive devotees do not harbor any malice even toward those who have harmed them, seeing God residing in the heart of all beings.
commentary_summary: Krishna concludes Chapter 11 by defining the five marks of an exclusive devotee: acting for God, depending on God, devoted to God, free from attachment, and free from malice.
theme: The five pillars of exclusive devotion that lead to union with God

speaker: Arjuna
text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते |
ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमा: ||1||
transliteration: arjuna uvācha | evaṁ satata-yuktā ye bhaktās tvāṁ paryupāsate | ye chāpy akṣharam avyaktaṁ teṣhāṁ ke yoga-vittamāḥ ||
translation: Arjun inquired: Between those who are steadfastly devoted to Your personal form and those who worship the formless Brahman, whom do You consider to be more perfect in Yog?
commentary_full:
After witnessing the magnificent cosmic form of Shree Krishna in the previous chapter, Arjun’s devotion deepened further. Though overwhelmed by the universal vision, he found greater comfort and attraction in the personal form of God, endowed with attributes, qualities, and loving pastimes. This preference led him to raise an important philosophical question.

Arjun asks who is superior in Yog: those devotees who constantly worship the personal form of the Lord with devotion, or those who contemplate and worship the imperishable, formless Brahman. His inquiry highlights a long-standing spiritual discussion regarding the relative merit of devotion to a personal God versus meditation on the impersonal Absolute.

The question itself affirms a profound truth—that God possesses both aspects. The Supreme is simultaneously all-pervading and formless, as well as personal and accessible through divine forms. To deny either aspect is to impose limitations upon the Infinite. Just as individual souls are formless yet repeatedly assume bodies, the all-powerful God can manifest forms without compromising His formless nature.

Even Jagadguru Shankaracharya, a foremost exponent of jñāna-yog, acknowledged that Brahman is both personal and impersonal. However, he emphasized that worship of the formless aspect is far more difficult. Through this question, Arjun seeks clarity on the most effective and complete path to spiritual perfection.
commentary_summary: Arjun asks whether devotees of God’s personal form or worshippers of the formless Brahman are more perfect in Yog, highlighting the dual aspects of the Supreme and seeking clarity on the superior spiritual path.
theme: Comparison between devotion to the personal God and worship of the formless Brahman

speaker: Shri Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते |
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मता: ||2||
transliteration: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha | mayy āveśhya mano ye māṁ nitya-yuktā upāsate | śhraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ ||
translation: The Lord said: Those who fix their minds on Me and always engage in My devotion with steadfast faith, I consider them to be the best yogis.
commentary_full:
Shree Krishna directly answers Arjun’s question by explaining that God can be realized at different levels of closeness. Though the Supreme is one, realization varies based on the spiritual path followed. Using an analogy similar to observing a train from a distance, God explains that as one comes closer, deeper attributes and personal details become visible.

The Supreme Entity manifests in three primary ways—Brahman, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān. Brahman is the formless, all-pervading divine effulgence; Paramātmā is the localized aspect of God seated in the hearts of all living beings; and Bhagavān is the personal form of God, endowed with divine names, forms, qualities, pastimes, associates, and abodes. These are not separate Gods, but different manifestations of the same Supreme Reality, each revealing varying degrees of divine intimacy.

Those who follow the path of jñāna-yog worship the impersonal Brahman, which is a distant realization of God. Practitioners of aṣhṭāṅg-yog seek to realize the Paramātmā within the heart, which is a closer realization. However, devotees who engage in bhakti-yog worship God in His personal form as Bhagavān, attaining the most complete and intimate realization of the Divine.

By stating that those who fix their minds upon Him with unwavering faith and devotion are the highest yogis, Shree Krishna establishes bhakti as the supreme path. Devotion allows the soul to experience the full sweetness of God’s personality, which remains latent in other realizations. Thus, loving devotion leads to the closest union with the Supreme Truth.
commentary_summary: Shree Krishna explains that although God can be realized as Brahman, Paramātmā, and Bhagavān, devotees who worship Him in His personal form with steady faith attain the highest and closest realization, making them the best yogis.
theme: Supremacy of devotion to the personal form of God as the highest Yog

speaker: Shri Krishna
text_sanskrit:
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते |
