transliteration: kṣhetra-kṣhetrajñayor evam antaraṁ jñāna-chakṣhuṣhā bhūta-prakṛiti-mokṣhaṁ cha ye vidur yānti te param
translation: Those who perceive with the eyes of knowledge the difference between the body and the knower of the body, and the process of release from material nature, attain the supreme destination.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna concludes the exposition on the field (kṣhetra) and the knower of the field (kṣhetrajña) by emphasizing true knowledge. Discriminative wisdom involves recognizing the difference between the material body and the soul residing within. By identifying with their spiritual essence rather than the physical body, aspirants pursue liberation from material nature. Such enlightened individuals follow the path of spiritual realization and ultimately attain God-consciousness, the supreme destination.
commentary_summary: Understanding the distinction between body and soul, and pursuing liberation from material nature, leads to the supreme goal.
theme: Discriminative knowledge of body and soul leading to liberation

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
परं भूय: प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानानां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् |
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुनय: सर्वे परां सिद्धिमितो गता: || 1||
transliteration: shri-bhagavan uvacha param bhuyah pravakshyami jnananam jnanam uttamam yaj jnatva munayah sarve param siddhim ito gatah
translation: BG 14.1: The Divine Lord said: I shall once again explain to you the supreme wisdom, the best of all knowledge; by knowing which, all the great saints attained the highest perfection.
commentary_full: In the previous chapter, Shree Krishna had explained that all life forms are a combination of soul and matter. He had also elucidated that prakṛiti (material nature) is responsible for creating the field of activities for the puruṣh (soul). He added that this does not happen independently, but under the direction of the Supreme Lord, who is also seated within the body of the living being. In this chapter, he goes on to elaborate in detail about the three-fold qualities of material nature (the guṇas). By gaining this knowledge and imbibing it into our consciousness as realized wisdom, we can ascend to the highest perfection.
commentary_summary: Shree Krishna introduces the supreme wisdom of the guṇas, knowledge that leads saints to the highest perfection.
theme: Supreme wisdom leading to perfection

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
इदं ज्ञानमुपाश्रित्य मम साधर्म्यमागता: |
सर्गेऽपि नोपजायन्ते प्रलये न व्यथन्ति च || 2||
transliteration: idam jnanam upashritya mama sadharmyam agatah sarge ’pi nopajayante pralaye na vyathanti cha
translation: BG 14.2: Those who take refuge in this wisdom will be united with Me. They will not be reborn at the time of creation nor destroyed at the time of dissolution.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna assures Arjun that those who equip themselves with the knowledge he is about to bestow will no longer have to accept repeated confinement in a mother’s womb. They will also not be obliged to stay in a state of suspended animation in the womb of God at the time of the universal dissolution, or be reborn along with the next creation. The three guṇas (modes of material nature) are indeed the cause of bondage, and knowledge of them will illumine the path out of bondage. Shree Krishna repeatedly uses the strategy of proclaiming the results of what he is about to teach, to bring his student to rapt attention. The words na vyathanti mean 'they will not experience misery.' The word sādharmyam means they will acquire 'a similar divine nature' as God himself. When the soul is released from the bondage of the material energy, it comes under the dominion of God’s divine Yogmaya energy. The divine energy equips it with God’s divine knowledge, love, and bliss. As a result, the soul becomes of the nature of God—it acquires divine godlike qualities.
commentary_summary: Those who take refuge in this knowledge unite with God, escape rebirth, and acquire a divine nature.
theme: Refuge in supreme wisdom leading to liberation and divine nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
मम योनिर्महद् ब्रह्म तस्मिन्गर्भं दधाम्यहम् |
सम्भव: सर्वभूतानां ततो भवति भारत || 3||
सर्वयोनिषु कौन्तेय मूर्तय: सम्भवन्ति या: |
तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रद: पिता || 4||
transliteration:
mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbham dadhamy aham sambhavah sarva-bhutanam tato bhavati bharata
sarva-yonishu kaunteya murtayah sambhavanti yah tasam brahma mahad yonir aham bija-pradah pita
translation: BG 14.3-4: The total material substance, prakṛiti, is the womb. I impregnate it with the individual souls, and thus all living beings are born. O son of Kunti, for all species of life that are produced, the material nature is the womb, and I am the seed-giving Father.
commentary_full: As explained in chapters 7 and 8, the material creation follows cycles of creation, maintenance, and dissolution. During dissolution, souls who are vimukh (have turned away) from God remain in a state of suspended animation within the body of Maha Vishnu. The material energy, prakṛiti, also lies unmanifest in God’s mahodar (great womb). When He desires to initiate creation, He glances at prakṛiti. It then begins to unwind, creating entities such as mahān, ahankār, pañch-tanmātrās, and pañch-mahābhūta. With the help of the secondary creator Brahma, material energy produces various life forms, and God places the souls into appropriate bodies based on their past karmas. Thus, Shree Krishna states that prakṛiti is like the womb and the souls are like seeds. He implants the souls into the womb of Mother Nature to give birth to multitudes of living beings. Sage Ved Vyas also describes this in Śhrīmad Bhāgavatam: 'In the womb of the material energy the Supreme Lord impregnates the souls. Then, inspired by the karmas of the individual souls, the material nature gets to work to create suitable life forms for them.' Only those souls who are vimukh are placed into the material world; others remain with God.
commentary_summary: The material nature (prakṛiti) is the womb, and God, as the seed-giver, places souls into it, producing all living beings according to their past karmas.
theme: Material nature as womb and God as the seed-giver creating all life

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति गुणा: प्रकृतिसम्भवा: |
निबध्नन्ति महाबाहो देहे देहिनमव्ययम् || 5||
transliteration: sattvam rajas tama iti gunah prakriti-sambhavah nibadhnanti maha-baho dehe dehinam avyayam
translation: BG 14.5: O mighty-armed Arjun, the material energy consists of three guṇas (modes)—sattva (goodness), rajas (passion), and tamas (ignorance). These modes bind the eternal soul to the perishable body.
commentary_full: Having explained that all life-forms are born from puruṣh and prakṛiti, Shree Krishna now explains how prakṛiti binds the soul. Although divine, the soul's identification with the body ties it to material nature. Material energy possesses three guṇas—goodness, passion, and ignorance. The body, mind, and intellect, which arise from prakṛiti, also reflect these modes. Consider the example of three-color printing: if one color is applied in excess, it dominates the picture. Similarly, based on a person’s internal thoughts, circumstances, past sanskārs, and other factors, one of these guṇas predominates, influencing personality and behavior, and thereby binding the soul to material nature.
commentary_summary: The three guṇas of material nature—sattva, rajas, tamas—bind the eternal soul to the perishable body, influencing personality and actions.
theme: Three modes of material nature binding the soul

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
तत्र सत्त्वं निर्मलत्वात्प्रकाशकमनामयम् |
सुखसङ्गेन बध्नाति ज्ञानसङ्गेन चानघ || 6||
transliteration: tatra sattvam nirmalatvat prakashakam anamayam sukha-sangena badhnati jnana-sangena chanagha
translation: BG 14.6: Amongst these, sattva guṇa, the mode of goodness, being purer than the others, is illuminating and full of well-being. O sinless one, it binds the soul by creating attachment for a sense of happiness and knowledge.
commentary_full: The word prakāśhakam means “illuminating,” and anāmayam means “healthy and full of well-being,” or serene and free from misery. Sattva guṇa engenders virtue, illuminates the intellect, and makes one calm, satisfied, charitable, compassionate, and serene. While it creates happiness and knowledge, attachment to it binds the soul to material nature. Using the example of three robbers: tamo guṇa kills the soul by ignorance, rajo guṇa excites passions and binds through desires, while sattva guṇa eases vices and discomfort, guiding the soul toward virtue. Yet, sattva guṇa is still material; true transcendence is achieved through śhuddha sattva, the divine mode of goodness beyond material nature, granted by God to elevate the soul.
commentary_summary: Sattva guṇa, the mode of goodness, illuminates, promotes well-being, and binds the soul through attachment to happiness and knowledge; it guides toward virtue but remains part of material nature.
theme: Mode of goodness binding the soul while illuminating intellect and well-being

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् |
तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् || 7||
transliteration: rajo ragatmakam viddhi trishna-sanga-samudbhavam tan nibadhnati kaunteya karma-sangena dehinam
translation: BG 14.7: O Arjun, rajo guṇa is of the nature of passion. It arises from worldly desires and affections, and binds the soul through attachment to fruitive actions.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains the working of rajo guṇa, showing how it binds the soul to material existence. Rajo guṇa fuels lust for mental and physical pleasures, inflames desires, and promotes attachment to worldly things like status, career, family, and home. The desires and the mode of passion reinforce each other, trapping the soul in worldly life. The way to pacify rajo guṇa is through karm yog—offering the results of actions to God, creating detachment from material attachments.
commentary_summary: Rajo guṇa, the mode of passion, arises from desires and attachment, binding the soul to worldly activities; karm yog helps pacify its effects.
theme: Mode of passion binding the soul through desires and attachment to actions

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् |
प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत || 8||
transliteration: tamas tv ajnana-jam viddhi mohanam sarva-dehinam pramadalasya-nidrabhis tan nibadhnati bharata
translation: BG 14.8: O Arjun, tamo guṇa, which is born of ignorance, is the cause of illusion for the embodied souls. It deludes all living beings through negligence, laziness, and sleep.
commentary_full: Tamo guṇa is the antithesis of sattva guṇa. Persons influenced by it take pleasure in sleep, laziness, intoxication, violence, and gambling. They lose discrimination between right and wrong and do not hesitate to act immorally to fulfill selfish desires. Duty becomes burdensome, and they neglect it, becoming more inclined to sloth and sleep. This mode of ignorance deepens the soul's entanglement in material darkness, making it oblivious of its spiritual identity and its opportunity for progress in human life.
commentary_summary: Tamo guṇa, born of ignorance, deludes the soul through laziness, sleep, and negligence, leading it deeper into material darkness.
theme: Mode of ignorance deluding the soul through sloth and negligence

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रज: कर्मणि भारत |
ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तम: प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत || 9||
transliteration: sattvam sukhe sanjayati rajah karmani bharata jnanam avritya tu tamah pramade sanjayaty uta
translation: BG 14.9: Sattva binds one to material happiness; rajas conditions the soul toward actions; and tamas clouds wisdom and binds one to delusion.
commentary_full: In the mode of goodness, the miseries of material existence reduce, and worldly desires become subdued, giving contentment. Yet, it can lead to complacency or pride if knowledge is not spiritual. In the mode of passion, souls are impelled toward intense activity for pleasure, wealth, status, and desires, creating karmic bondage. The mode of ignorance clouds intellect, leading to foolish actions and attachment to perverse pleasures, binding the soul in delusion.
commentary_summary: Sattva binds through happiness, rajas through attachment to action, and tamas clouds wisdom, binding one in delusion.
theme: The three guṇas bind the soul differently: sattva through happiness, rajas through activity, tamas through delusion

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
रजस्तमश्चाभिभूय सत्त्वं भवति भारत |
रज: सत्त्वं तमश्चैव तम: सत्त्वं रजस्तथा || 10||
transliteration: rajas tamash chabhibhuya sattvam bhavati bharata rajah sattvam tamash chaiva tamah sattvam rajas tatha
translation: BG 14.10: Sometimes goodness (sattva) prevails over passion (rajas) and ignorance (tamas), O scion of Bharat. Sometimes passion (rajas) dominates goodness (sattva) and ignorance (tamas), and at other times ignorance (tamas) overcomes goodness (sattva) and passion (rajas).
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains how an individual's temperament oscillates among the three guṇas. The three guṇas are present in material energy, and since the mind is made from the same energy, all three are in the mind. They are like three wrestlers competing—sometimes one dominates, sometimes another. External environment, contemplation, and past tendencies determine which guṇa prevails. Sattva brings peace, contentment, kindness, and serenity; rajas brings passion, ambition, and desire for pleasures; tamas brings laziness, anger, and doubt. The mind constantly shifts among these modes.
commentary_summary: The three guṇas—sattva, rajas, tamas—oscillate in the mind, each dominating at different times, shaping temperament and behavior.
theme: The mind oscillates among the three guṇas, which influence behavior and disposition

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
सर्वद्वारेषु देहेऽस्मिन्प्रकाश उपजायते |
ज्ञानं यदा तदा विद्याद्विवृद्धं सत्त्वमित्युत || 11||
लोभ: प्रवृत्तिरारम्भ: कर्मणामशम: स्पृहा |
रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ || 12||
अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च |
तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन || 13||
transliteration: sarva-dvareshu dehe ’smin prakasha upajayate jnanam yada tada vidyad vivriddham sattvam ity uta lobhah pravrittir arambhah karmanam ashamah spriha rajasy etani jayante vivriddhe bharatarshabha aprakasho ’pravrittish cha pramado moha eva cha tamasy etani jayante vivriddhe kuru-nandana
translation: BG 14.11-13: When all the gates of the body are illumined by knowledge, know it to be a manifestation of the mode of goodness. When the mode of passion predominates, O Arjun, the symptoms of greed, exertion for worldly gain, restlessness, and craving develop. O Arjun, nescience, inertia, negligence, and delusion—these are the dominant signs of the mode of ignorance.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains how the three modes influence one’s thinking. Sattva guṇa leads to illumination and virtues. Rajo guṇa leads to greed, restlessness, and craving for worldly gain. Tamo guṇa results in delusion, laziness, and negligence. These modes also influence attitudes toward God and spiritual practice. The mind naturally oscillates due to the guṇas. Sādhanā is the effort to rise above these oscillations and maintain devotional consciousness toward God and Guru. Initially, this effort is difficult, but with practice, it becomes natural.
commentary_summary: Sattva illumines and brings virtue; rajas fuels greed and restlessness; tamas causes delusion and laziness. Understanding this helps transcend their influence through spiritual practice.
theme: The three guṇas manifest in thoughts, actions, and temperament, and spiritual practice helps transcend them

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
यदा सत्त्वे प्रवृद्धे तु प्रलयं याति देहभृत् |
तदोत्तमविदां लोकानमलान्प्रतिपद्यते || 14||
रजसि प्रलयं गत्वा कर्मसङ्गिषु जायते |
तथा प्रलीनस्तमसि मूढयोनिषु जायते || 15||
transliteration: yada sattve pravriddhe tu pralayam yati deha-bhrit tadottama-vidam lokan amalan pratipadyate rajasi pralayaṁ gatvā karma-saṅgiṣhu jāyate tatha pralīnas tamasi mūḍha-yonishu jāyate
translation: BG 14.14-15: Those who die with predominance of sattva reach the pure abodes (which are free from rajas and tamas) of the learned. Those who die with prevalence of the mode of passion are born among people driven by work, while those dying in the mode of ignorance take birth in the animal kingdom.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that the destiny awaiting souls is based upon the guṇas of their personalities. Sattva leads to virtuous, learned families or higher celestial abodes. Rajas leads to families engaged in worldly activity and intense material work. Tamas leads to sloth, violence, and ignorance, resulting in rebirth in lower species, including animals. The human form is not guaranteed; it can be lost if misused. The soul’s evolution—upward, steady, or downward—depends on the intensity and dominance of the guṇas in life.
commentary_summary: The predominance of the guṇas at death determines rebirth: sattva leads to pure abodes, rajas to active human life, and tamas to lower species, emphasizing the importance of cultivating virtuous qualities.
theme: The soul’s destination after death is determined by the dominant guṇa in life

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
कर्मण: सुकृतस्याहु: सात्त्विकं निर्मलं फलम् |
रजसस्तु फलं दु:खमज्ञानं तमस: फलम् || 16||
transliteration: karmanah sukritasyahuh sattvikam nirmalam phalam rajasas tu phalam duhkham ajnanam tamasah phalam
translation: BG 14.16: It is said the fruit of actions performed in the mode of goodness bestow pure results. Actions done in the mode of passion result in pain, while those performed in the mode of ignorance result in darkness.
commentary_full: Those influenced by sattva are equipped with purity, virtue, knowledge, and selflessness. Their actions are performed with pure intentions, yielding uplifting and satisfying results. Those under rajas are driven by desire and self-interest; their actions give temporary pleasure but increase attachment and suffering. Those dominated by tamas act in ignorance, neglecting moral and spiritual principles, and their actions produce darkness and delusion, further binding them to material existence.
commentary_summary: The result of actions depends on the dominant guṇa: sattva yields purity, rajas brings pain, and tamas leads to ignorance and darkness.
theme: The outcome of actions is determined by the prevailing guṇa at the time of action

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च |
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतोऽज्ञानमेव च || 17||
transliteration: sattvat sanjayate jnanam rajaso lobha eva cha pramada-mohau tamaso bhavato ’jnanam eva cha
translation: BG 14.17: From the mode of goodness arises knowledge, from the mode of passion arises greed, and from the mode of ignorance arise negligence and delusion.
commentary_full: Sattva guṇa gives rise to wisdom, pacifying sense desires and promoting contentment and virtuous actions. Rajo guṇa inflames ambition and desire, leading to greed and attachment. Tamo guṇa envelops the living being in inertia and ignorance, causing negligence, delusion, and impure actions.
commentary_summary: The three guṇas produce distinct mental qualities: sattva brings knowledge, rajas produces greed, and tamas generates negligence and delusion.
theme: The guṇas determine the arising mental qualities and tendencies of the soul

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति सत्त्वस्था मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति राजसा: |
जघन्यगुणवृत्तिस्था अधो गच्छन्ति तामसा: || 18||
transliteration: urdhvam gachchhanti sattva-stha madhye tishthanti rajasah jaghanya-guna-vritti-stha adho gachchhanti tamasah
translation: BG 14.18: Those situated in the mode of goodness rise upward; those in the mode of passion stay in the middle; and those in the mode of ignorance go downward.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that the reincarnation of souls depends on the guṇa predominating their personality. Souls in sattva ascend to higher realms, those in rajo remain on earth, and those in tamo descend to lower worlds. This is analogous to students gaining admission to colleges according to their merits. The transcendental soul beyond the three guṇas attains God.
commentary_summary: Soul's next birth corresponds to the dominant guṇa: sattva rises, rajas stays in the middle, tamas descends.
theme: The guṇas determine the soul’s destination after death

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
नान्यं गुणेभ्य: कर्तारं यदा द्रष्टानुपश्यति |
गुणेभ्यश्च परं वेत्ति मद्भावं सोऽधिगच्छति || 19||
transliteration: nanyam gunebhyah kartaram yada drashtanupashyati gunebhyash cha param vetti mad-bhavam so ’dhigachchhati
translation: BG 14.19: When wise persons see that in all work there is no agent of action other than the three guṇas, and they know Me to be transcendental to these guṇas, they attain My divine nature.
commentary_full: Having revealed the workings of the three guṇas, Shree Krishna shows the solution for transcending them. All beings are influenced by the guṇas, which are the active agents in worldly work, but the Supreme Lord is beyond them (tri-guṇātīt). Understanding this, one loosens attachment to worldly objects and strengthens attachment to God through bhakti, thereby transcending the guṇas and attaining the divine nature.
commentary_summary: By seeing all actions as governed by the three guṇas and recognizing God as beyond them, one attains the divine nature.
theme: Transcending the three guṇas through knowledge and devotion

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
गुणानेतानतीत्य त्रीन्देही देहसमुद्भवान् |
जन्ममृत्युजरादु:खैर्विमुक्तोऽमृतमश्रुते || 20||
transliteration: gunān etān atītya trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān janma-mṛityu-jarā-duḥkhair vimukto ’mṛitam aśhnute
translation: BG 14.20: By transcending the three modes of material nature associated with the body, one becomes free from birth, death, old age, and misery, and attains immortality.
commentary_full: The soul, while under the influence of the three guṇas, experiences repeated birth, disease, old age, and death. The modes of material nature bind it to this cycle. Codes of conduct (karm dharma) can elevate one to sattva guṇa, but even this is still within material bondage. By transcending the three guṇas, the soul is freed from Maya's influence, released from the cycle of life and death, and experiences immortality. The soul is inherently immortal, but identification with the body creates the illusion of birth and death. Transcending the guṇas restores awareness of its true eternal nature.
commentary_summary: Transcending the three guṇas liberates the soul from birth, death, old age, and misery, allowing it to attain its true immortal nature.
theme: Freedom from material bondage and attainment of immortality by transcending the three guṇas

speaker: Arjun
text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
कैर्लिङ्गैस्त्रीन्गुणानेतानतीतो भवति प्रभो |
किमाचार: कथं चैतांस्त्रीन्गुणानतिवर्तते || 21||
transliteration: arjuna uvācha kair liṅgais trīn guṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho kim āchāraḥ kathaṁ chaitāns trīn guṇān ativartate
translation: BG 14.21: Arjun inquired: What are the characteristics of those who have gone beyond the three guṇas, O Lord? How do they act? How do they go beyond the bondage of the guṇas?
commentary_full: After hearing from Shree Krishna about the three guṇas and their effects, Arjun asks about the transcendentalists who go beyond them. He wants to know their symptoms (liṅgais), how they behave in action (āchāraḥ), and the method by which they transcend the three modes (ativartate). This sets the stage for Shree Krishna to describe the qualities, conduct, and spiritual process of one who is beyond the guṇas.
commentary_summary: Arjun asks about the characteristics, behavior, and method of those who have transcended the three guṇas.
theme: Understanding the qualities and conduct of one who transcends the three guṇas

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
प्रकाशं च प्रवृत्तिं च मोहमेव च पाण्डव |
न द्वेष्टि सम्प्रवृत्तानि न निवृत्तानि काङ् क्षति || 22||
उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते |
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येवं योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते || 23||
transliteration: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha prakāśhaṁ cha pravṛittiṁ cha moham eva cha pāṇḍava na dveṣhṭi sampravṛittāni na nivṛittāni kāṅkṣhati udāsīna-vad āsīno guṇair yo na vichālyate guṇā vartanta ity evaṁ yo ’vatiṣhṭhati neṅgate
translation: BG 14.22-23: The Supreme Divine Personality said: O Arjun, The persons who are transcendental to the three guṇas neither hate illumination (which is born of sattva), nor activity (which is born of rajas), nor even delusion (which is born of tamas), when these are abundantly present, nor do they long for them when they are absent. They remain neutral to the modes of nature and are not disturbed by them. Knowing it is only the guṇas that act, they stay established in the self, without wavering.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains the traits of those who have transcended the three guṇas. They are not disturbed when the guṇas function in the world or manifest in people, objects, and situations. Such persons neither hate ignorance when it is present nor crave it when absent. They act naturally, performing their duties, but remain detached from the modes of nature. They understand that all actions are driven by the guṇas, and that the self is separate from the mind and body. By remaining established in the self, they avoid being influenced by the fluctuations of the guṇas and maintain spiritual equilibrium. This detachment allows them to do good in the world without being perturbed by external circumstances.
commentary_summary: Transcendental persons remain neutral to the modes of nature, perform duties without attachment, and stay established in the self.
theme: Equanimity and self-establishment beyond the three guṇas

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
समदु:खसुख: स्वस्थ: समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चन: |
तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुति: || 24||
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयो: |
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीत: स उच्यते || 25||
transliteration: sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ sva-sthaḥ sama-loṣhṭāśhma-kāñchanaḥ tulya-priyāpriyo dhīras tulya-nindātma-sanstutiḥ mānāpamānayośh tulyaḥ tulyaḥ mitrāripakṣayoḥ sarvārambha-parityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa uchyate
translation: BG 14.24-25: Those who are alike in happiness and distress; who are established in the self; who look upon a clod, a stone, and a piece of gold as of equal value; who remain the same amidst pleasant and unpleasant events; who are intelligent; who accept both blame and praise with equanimity; who remain the same in honor and dishonor; who treat both friend and foe alike; and who have abandoned all enterprises – they are said to have risen above the three guṇas.
commentary_full: Like God, the soul is beyond the three guṇas. In bodily consciousness, we identify with the pain and pleasures of the body, vacillating between elation and dejection. Those established on the transcendental platform of the self do not identify with bodily happiness or distress. Self-realized individuals perceive the dualities of the world but remain unaffected by them, achieving nirguṇa status. This gives them equal vision, seeing a stone, earth, gold, favorable and unfavorable situations, criticism and praise as all the same. They remain equanimous, treat friend and foe alike, and abandon all material enterprises, thus rising above the three guṇas.
commentary_summary: Self-realized souls see all dualities equally, remain equanimous, and transcend the three guṇas.
theme: Transcendence and equanimity beyond the three guṇas

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते |
स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते || 26||
transliteration: māṁ cha yo ’vyabhichāreṇa bhakti-yogena sevate sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahma-bhūyāya kalpate
translation: BG 14.26: Those who serve Me with unalloyed devotion rise above the three modes of material nature and come to the level of the Brahman.
commentary_full: Having explained the traits of those beyond the three guṇas, Shree Krishna reveals the sole method of transcending these modes: unalloyed devotion (bhakti-yoga). Mere self-knowledge is insufficient; the mind must be fixed on the Supreme Lord. Then it becomes nirguṇa, like Shree Krishna Himself. Even meditating on the personal form of God is sufficient, as divine qualities are beyond material guṇas. Transcendental meditation must be directed toward God, the entity beyond the three modes, to truly rise above them.
commentary_summary: Unalloyed devotion to God enables one to transcend the three guṇas and attain the level of Brahman.
theme: Rising above the three guṇas through unalloyed devotion to God

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च |
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च || 27||
transliteration: brahmaṇo hi pratiṣhṭhāham amṛitasyāvyayasya cha śhāśhvatasya cha dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya cha
translation: BG 14.27: I am the basis of the formless Brahman, the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of unending divine bliss.
commentary_full: The previous verse may raise questions about the relationship between Shree Krishna and the formless Brahman. Here, Shree Krishna clarifies that the Brahman worshipped by the jñānīs is the effulgence emanating from His personal form. Padma Purāṇ and Chaitanya Charitāmṛit explain that this transcendental light from the Lord’s body is Brahman. Thus, the verse confirms that devotion to the personal form of the Supreme Lord is the means to rise above the three guṇas and attain transcendence.
commentary_summary: Shree Krishna is the foundation of Brahman, immortal dharma, and unending bliss; devotion to Him transcends the three guṇas.
theme: Shree Krishna as the source of Brahman, dharma, and eternal bliss; devotion transcends the three guṇas

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ऊर्ध्वमूलमध:शाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् |
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् || 1||
transliteration: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha ūrdhva-mūlam adhaḥ-śhākham aśhvatthaṁ prāhur avyayam chhandānsi yasya parṇāni yas taṁ veda sa veda-vit
translation: BG 15.1: The Supreme Divine Personality said: They speak of an eternal aśhvatth tree with its roots above and branches below. Its leaves are the Vedic hymns, and one who knows the secret of this tree is the knower of the Vedas.
commentary_full: Lord Shree Krishna describes the eternal Aśhvatth (sacred fig) tree, whose roots are upward from God and branches downward representing the material world. Its leaves are Vedic hymns, which sustain material life through rituals and their results. Souls experience continuous cycles of birth and death through this tree. Knowing the secret of this tree—understanding the transient nature of the material world and transcending it—makes one a knower of the Vedas. The tree illustrates that while the world seems eternal, it is supported by God and eventually falls back to Him, highlighting the impermanence of worldly attachments.
commentary_summary: The Aśhvatth tree symbolizes the material world with roots in God and leaves as Vedic hymns. Knowing its secret—transcending worldly attachments—makes one a knower of the Vedas.
theme: The eternal aśhvatth tree symbolizes the material world; understanding its secret leads to transcendence and Vedic wisdom.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा
गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवाला: |
अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि
कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके || 2||
transliteration: adhaśh chordhvaṁ prasṛitās tasya śhākhā guṇa-pravṛiddhā viṣhaya-pravālāḥ adhaśh cha mūlāny anusantatāni karmānubandhīni manuṣhya-loke
translation: BG 15.2: The branches of the tree extend upward and downward, nourished by the three guṇas, with the objects of the senses as tender buds. The roots of the tree hang downward, causing the flow of karma in the human form. Below, its roots branch out causing (karmic) actions in the world of humans.
commentary_full: Lord Krishna explains that the human form is like the eternal Aśhvatth tree. The soul performs karmas (the trunk), and its branches extend upward (towards celestial abodes) and downward (towards lower births), depending on past and present deeds. The three guṇas (modes of material nature) irrigate the tree, while sense objects (viṣhaya-pravālāḥ) act as buds, sprouting desires. These desires produce karma, which functions like aerial roots, perpetually expanding the tree and entangling the soul further in material consciousness. Just as a banyan tree’s aerial roots grow into secondary trunks, desires and karma continue to multiply, sustaining the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth.
commentary_summary: The Aśhvatth tree represents the human life and karma, nourished by the three guṇas. Sense objects sprout desires, producing karma, which perpetuates the soul’s entanglement in material existence.
theme: The human form is like the Aśhvatth tree; the three guṇas and sense objects perpetuate karma, entangling the soul in the cycle of material existence.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते
नान्तो न चादिर्न च सम्प्रतिष्ठा |
अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल
मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा || 3||
तत: पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं
यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूय: |
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये
यत: प्रवृत्ति: प्रसृता पुराणी || 4||
transliteration: na rūpam asyeha tathopalabhyate nānto na chādir na cha sampratiṣhṭhā aśhvattham enaṁ su-virūḍha-mūlam asaṅga-śhastreṇa dṛiḍhena chhittvā tataḥ padam tat parimārgitavyaṁ yasmin gata na nivartanti bhūyaḥ tam eva chādyaṁ puruṣhaṁ prapadye yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛitā purāṇī
translation: BG 15.3-4: The real form of this tree is not perceived in this world, neither its beginning nor end, nor its continued existence. But this deep-rooted aśhvatth tree must be cut down with a strong axe of detachment. Then one must search out the base of the tree, which is the Supreme Lord, from whom streamed forth the activity of the universe a long time ago. Upon taking refuge in Him, one will not return to this world again.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that the aśhvatth tree represents the cycle of life and death, nourished by desires arising from the three guṇas. The buds (sense objects) produce desires, and karma acts like roots, entangling the soul. Ignorant souls keep accumulating merits and demerits, which move them upward to celestial abodes or downward to lower species. This process continues eternally. The way to cut down this tree is with the strong axe of detachment (asaṅga) developed through knowledge of the self: realizing that 'I am not this body, but an eternal soul.' Once desires are cut, the roots weaken. The next step is to seek the base of the tree, the Supreme Lord, from whom all creation proceeds. By surrendering fully to Him, the soul transcends the tree and will not return to the cycle of birth and death. Maya, consisting of the three modes, is difficult to overcome, but surrendering to the Lord enables one to cross it easily.
commentary_summary: The aśhvatth tree symbolizes samsara, nourished by desires and karma. Detachment and self-knowledge are the axe to cut it, and taking refuge in the Supreme Lord allows the soul to transcend the material world permanently.
theme: The aśhvatth tree of material existence can be cut by detachment and surrender to the Supreme Lord, liberating the soul from samsara.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा
अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामा: |
द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ता: सुखदु:खसंज्ञैर् गच्छन्त्यमूढा: पदमव्ययं तत ||5||
transliteration: nirmāna-mohā jita-saṅga-doṣhā adhyātma-nityā vinivṛitta-kāmāḥ dvandvair vimuktāḥ sukha-duḥkha-sanjñair gachchhanty amūḍhāḥ padam avyayaṁ tat
translation: BG 15.5: Those who are free from vanity and delusion, who have overcome the evil of attachment, who dwell constantly on the self and on God, who are free from the desire to enjoy the senses, and are beyond the dualities of pleasure and pain, such liberated personalities attain My eternal Abode.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains the requisites for complete surrender to the Supreme Lord, who is at the base of the aśhvatth tree. First, one must give up pride, which arises from ignorance and the illusion of being the enjoyer of all material wealth. By realizing that God alone is the owner of all creation, the soul surrenders and develops selfless service. As desires for worldly enjoyment fade, the heart is purified. Jagadguru Shree Kripaluji Maharaj emphasizes that devotion to Krishna and the desire to serve Him is the most powerful means of purification. Once perfected in God-realization, souls are freed from the cycle of birth and death and enter the eternal spiritual realm, which constitutes three-fourths of the universe, in contrast to the material realm, which is only one-fourth.
commentary_summary: Freedom from pride, attachment, and desires, along with constant focus on the self and God, liberates the soul to attain Krishna's eternal Abode beyond dualities and the cycle of birth and death.
theme: Surrender, detachment, and focus on God liberate the soul, allowing it to transcend material dualities and attain the eternal Abode.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावक: |
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम || 6||
transliteration: na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śhaśhāṅko na pāvakaḥ yat gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṁ mama
translation: BG 15.6: Neither the sun nor the moon, nor fire can illumine that Supreme Abode of Mine. Having gone There, one does not return to this material world again.
commentary_full: Lord Shree Krishna describes His Supreme Abode, which is self-luminous and requires no sun, moon, or fire for illumination. Unlike the material realm, which is full of defects and dualities, the spiritual realm is transcendental, perfect, and sat-chit-ānanda (eternal bliss and knowledge). The Paravyom, or spiritual sky, contains numerous abodes of various eternal forms of God such as Narayan, Ram, and Krishna, along with their devotees, where divine pastimes (Leelas) are eternally performed. Brahma in the Brahma Samhitā describes Goloka, the personal Abode of Krishna, filled with divine beauty, blissful associates, and artistic manifestations. Souls who attain this Abode reside there eternally with the Lord, completely freed from the cycle of birth and death.
commentary_summary: The Supreme Abode is self-luminous, perfect, and beyond material illumination. Souls who reach it are freed from samsara and reside eternally with Krishna.
theme: The Supreme Abode is beyond material light and dualities; devotees who reach it attain eternal residence with Krishna and liberation from material existence.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूत: सनातन: |
मन:षष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति || 7||
transliteration: mamaivānśho jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ manaḥ-ṣhaṣhṭānīndriyāṇi prakṛiti-sthāni karṣhati
translation: BG 15.7: The embodied souls in this material world are My eternal fragmental parts. But bound by material nature, they are struggling with the six senses including the mind.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that all souls in the material world are His Anśha (fragmental parts). While perfected souls who reach Him never return, the rest remain in the material realm, bound by maya. God manifests as Swānśh (direct, integrated parts, like His avatars) and Vibhinnānśh (fragmental souls). The vibhinnānśh souls are further divided into Nitya Siddha (always liberated), Sādhan Siddha (attained liberation through practice), and Nitya Baddha (bound eternally in material existence). The Nitya Baddha souls, bound by material nature, struggle with the mind and the five senses. As the Kaṭhopaniṣhad states, the senses are turned outward toward the world, causing entanglement in samsara. Thus, even though these souls are eternal parts of God, their material bondage leads to constant struggle.
commentary_summary: Embodied souls are fragmental parts of God. Bound by material nature, they struggle with mind and senses in samsara.
theme: Souls are eternal parts of God, but in the material world, their entanglement with mind and senses causes struggle.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वर: |
गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् || 8||
transliteration: śharīraṁ yad avāpnoti yach chāpy utkrāmatīśhvaraḥ gṛihītvaitāni sanyāti vāyurgandhān ivāśhayāt
translation: BG 15.8: As the air carries fragrance from place to place, so does the embodied soul carry the mind and senses with it, when it leaves an old body and enters a new one.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains the process of soul transmigration. Just as a breeze carries the fragrance of flowers from one place to another, the soul carries the subtle and causal bodies—including mind and senses—when it leaves a dead body and enters a new one. This is why a person’s past experiences can influence their new life. Dreams, for example, may reflect impressions stored in the subconscious from previous lives. Even someone born blind can have dreams influenced by past impressions. The subtle mind and senses are the instruments through which the soul continues to experience and act across lifetimes.
commentary_summary: The soul carries the mind and senses from one body to the next, like the air carrying fragrance.
theme: The soul carries the mind and senses from body to body, enabling continuity of experience across lifetimes.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
श्रोत्रं चक्षु: स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च |
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते || 9||
transliteration: śhrotraṁ chakṣhuḥ sparśhanaṁ cha rasanaṁ ghrāṇam eva cha adhiṣhṭhāya manaśh chāyaṁ viṣhayān upasevate
translation: BG 15.9: Using the sense perceptions of the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose, which are grouped around the mind, the embodied soul savors the objects of the senses.
commentary_full: The soul is divine, yet it experiences the material world through the mind and senses. The senses and mind, though lifeless by themselves, become instruments of consciousness through the soul. This allows the soul to perceive pleasure and pain from objects, thoughts, and experiences. However, material pleasures cannot fully satisfy the soul, which continually searches for the ultimate source of bliss in God. Historical examples, like Tulsidas, illustrate how intense attachment to worldly desires can mislead the mind, and how redirecting the senses and mind toward devotion to God frees the soul from the cycle of birth and death.
commentary_summary: The soul experiences sense objects via the mind and senses, but true satisfaction is found only in God.
theme: The embodied soul interacts with the world through the mind and senses, but ultimate fulfillment comes from turning them toward God.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् |
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुष: || 10||
transliteration: utkrāmantaṁ sthitaṁ vāpi bhuñjānaṁ vā guṇānvitam vimūḍhā nānupaśhyanti paśhyanti jñāna-chakṣhuṣhaḥ
translation: BG 15.10: The ignorant do not perceive the soul as it resides in the body, and as it enjoys sense objects; nor do they perceive it when it departs. But those who possess the eyes of knowledge can behold it.
commentary_full: The soul experiences the world through the mind and senses while residing in a body, but this subtle spiritual entity is imperceptible to material senses. Ignorant people assume the body itself is the self. This is similar to a novice mechanic trying to understand how a car moves by only looking at its parts; he misses the driver who controls it. Likewise, scientists may see bodily functions but miss the soul, which animates the body. Consciousness signals the presence of the soul. When the soul departs at death, the body ceases to function. Only those with spiritual knowledge, possessing the 'eyes of knowledge' (jñāna-chakṣhu), can perceive the soul and understand its actions.
commentary_summary: The soul cannot be perceived by material senses; only the spiritually enlightened can see it.
theme: The soul is imperceptible to the ignorant but visible to those with spiritual vision.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् |
यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतस: || 11||
transliteration: yatanto yoginaśh chainaṁ paśhyanty ātmany avasthitam yatanto ‘py akṛitātmāno nainaṁ paśhyanty achetasaḥ
translation: BG 15.11: Striving yogis too are able to realize the soul enshrined in the body. However, those whose minds are not purified cannot cognize it, even though they strive to do so.
commentary_full: Merely striving or seeking knowledge is not enough; it must be directed properly. Material senses and intellect alone cannot perceive the soul. Human minds often reject what cannot fit their current scientific or philosophical framework, as Alexis Carrel noted in 'Man the Unknown'. Nyāya Darśhan calls this kūpa-maṇḍūka-nyāya, the logic of a well-frog, which cannot comprehend the vastness outside its well. Likewise, those attached to materialistic thinking cannot perceive the eternal soul. Only those who purify their minds through spiritual practice, humility, and devotion can perceive the soul. With a cleansed mind, the scriptures and spiritual truths become clear. Similarly, the existence of God cannot be perceived by the senses; it requires the 'eyes of knowledge'.
commentary_summary: Only yogis with purified minds perceive the soul; others, despite effort, remain unaware.
theme: Purified mind and spiritual practice enable perception of the soul; materialistic intellect alone cannot.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् |
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् || 12||
transliteration: yad āditya-gataṁ tejo jagad bhāsayate ’khilam yach chandramasi yach chāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam
translation: BG 15.12: Know that I am like the brilliance of the sun that illuminates the entire solar system. The radiance of the moon and the brightness of the fire also come from Me.
commentary_full: In human life, we often forget our origin and eternal self, identifying solely with the physical body and material attachments. Shree Krishna explains that the entire creation is a manifestation of His energy. The brilliance of the Sun, Moon, and fire all originate from Him. The Sun’s uninterrupted energy, moonlight, celestial arrangements, and elements are all divine manifestations (vibhūtis). Kenopanishad recounts a story where Indra and other gods fail to recognize God’s supreme power, illustrating that even celestial beings derive their strength from Him. The lesson is that all luminescence and cosmic forces ultimately come from God, emphasizing His omnipresence and role as the supreme source of all energy and power.
commentary_summary: The Sun, Moon, and fire are manifestations of God's energy; all brilliance comes from Him.
theme: All cosmic radiance and power originate from the Supreme Lord.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा |
पुष्णामि चौषधी: सर्वा: सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मक: || 13||
transliteration: gām āviśhya cha bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā puṣhṇāmi chauṣhadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ
translation: BG 15.13: Permeating the earth, I nourish all living beings with My energy. Becoming the moon, I nourish all plants with the juice of life.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that it is His energy that makes life possible on Earth. By permeating the earth, He sustains all living beings (gām āviśhya dhārayāmy aham ojasā). The energy (ojasā) of God ensures that the physical conditions of the planet allow for life. For example, the saltiness of ocean water protects against harmful microbes, enabling life to flourish. Similarly, God as the moon (somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ) provides the nourishing moonlight that sustains plant life, including grains, fruits, vegetables, and herbs. This shows that both the living beings and plant life receive life-sustaining energy directly from God.
commentary_summary: God sustains all life on Earth through His energy and nourishes plants via the moon's ambrosial juice.
theme: God is the source of all life-sustaining energy for living beings and plants.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रित: |
प्राणापानसमायुक्त: पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् || 14||
transliteration: ahaṁ vaiśhvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṁ deham āśhritaḥ prāṇāpāna-samāyuktaḥ pachāmy annaṁ chatur-vidham
translation: BG 15.14: It is I who take the form of the fire of digestion in the stomachs of all living beings, and combine with the incoming and outgoing breaths, to digest and assimilate the four kinds of foods.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that God manifests inside all living beings as vaiśhvānara, the digestive fire, which is energized by Him. The Bṛihadāraṇyak Upaniṣhad states: 'ayam agnir vaiśhvānaro yo ’yam antaḥ puruṣhe yenedam annaṁ achyate,' meaning God is the fire inside the stomach that enables digestion. While science attributes digestion to organs like the stomach, liver, and pancreas, this verse emphasizes that God’s energy activates the process. 'Chaturvidham annam' refers to four types of food: 1) Bhojya – chewed foods like bread; 2) Peya – liquids like milk or juice; 3) Kośhya – sucked foods like sugarcane; 4) Lehya – licked foods like honey. God’s energy makes digestion possible, highlighting His support for every aspect of life, from sustaining life on Earth to nourishing plants and enabling our digestion.
commentary_summary: God is the divine digestive fire in all beings, working with the breath to assimilate the four types of foods.
theme: God sustains life by energizing the digestive process and assimilating food in all beings.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो
मत्त: स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च |
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो
वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् || 15||
transliteration: sarvasya chāhaṁ hṛidi sanniviṣhṭo mattaḥ smṛitir jñānam apohanaṁ cha vedaiśh cha sarvair aham eva vedyo vedānta-kṛid veda-vid eva chāham
translation: BG 15.15: I am seated in the hearts of all living beings, and from Me come memory, knowledge, as well as forgetfulness. I alone am to be known by all the Vedas, am the author of the Vedant, and the knower of the meaning of the Vedas.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna reveals that He grants memory, knowledge, and the ability to forget, functioning like the ultimate programmer of the mind and intellect. The mind and senses are instruments, but the consciousness behind them comes from God. Forgetting prevents overload, similar to deleting unnecessary data. He is also the source, knower, and author of the Vedas; Ved Vyas is considered His incarnation for manifesting Vedanta. All Vedic teachings ultimately point to knowing God, and rituals, mantras, and meditation are aids to guide the soul toward Him. Jagadguru Shree Kripaluji Maharaj emphasizes that the essence of all scriptures is loving devotion to God and Guru.
commentary_summary: God resides in the hearts of all beings, granting memory, knowledge, and forgetfulness, and He alone is the ultimate authority and knower of the Vedas.
theme: God as the inner guide and ultimate source of knowledge, memory, and spiritual understanding.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च |
क्षर: सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते || 16||
transliteration: dvāv imau puruṣhau loke kṣharaśh chākṣhara eva cha kṣharaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭa-stho ’kṣhara uchyate
translation: BG 15.16: There are two kinds of beings in creation, the kṣhar (perishable) and the akṣhar (imperishable). The perishable are all beings in the material realm. The imperishable are the liberated beings.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that creation contains two types of beings: the kṣhar (perishable) and the akṣhar (imperishable). While the soul itself is eternal, in the material realm, Maya binds it to a body, making it perishable. From insects to gods, all embodied living entities in the material world are kṣhar, subject to birth and death. The akṣhar beings are liberated, immortal, and reside in the divine realm, free from material cycles.
commentary_summary: All beings in the material world are perishable (kṣhar), while liberated souls are imperishable (akṣhar), residing eternally in the divine realm.
theme: Distinction between material (perishable) beings and liberated (imperishable) beings.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
उत्तम: पुरुषस्त्वन्य: परमात्मेत्युदाहृत: |
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वर: || 17||
transliteration: uttamaḥ puruṣhas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛitaḥ yo loka-trayam āviśhya bibharty avyaya īśhvaraḥ
translation: BG 15.17: Besides these, is the Supreme Divine Personality, who is the indestructible Supreme Soul. He enters the three worlds as the unchanging Controller and supports all living beings.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna now describes the Supreme Divine Personality, the Paramātma, the Supreme Soul. Unlike individual souls (ātma), Paramātma is the indestructible, unchanging, and all-pervading Supreme Soul. He is present within every living being, observing and supporting them, delivering results according to their karma. This Supreme Soul controls both perishable and imperishable realms, and accompanies souls across different births and species. The personal form of Paramātma is represented as the four-armed Kshirodakshayi Vishnu, the divine protector of all creation.
commentary_summary: The Supreme Soul (Paramātma) is distinct from individual souls, indestructible, present in all beings, controls the three worlds, and delivers results of karma. He manifests personally as Kshirodakshayi Vishnu.
theme: Paramātma as the Supreme, all-pervading, and indestructible Controller distinct from individual souls.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तम: |
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथित: पुरुषोत्तम: || 18||
transliteration: yasmāt kṣharam atīto ’ham akṣharād api chottamaḥ ato ’smi loke vede cha prathitaḥ puruṣhottamah
translation: BG 15.18: I am transcendental to the perishable world of matter, and even to the imperishable soul; hence I am celebrated, both in the Vedas and the Smṛitis, as the Supreme Divine Personality.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna declares Himself as Puruṣhottam, the Supreme Divine Personality who transcends both the perishable (kṣhar) material world and the imperishable (akṣhar) souls. The term aham (I) emphasizes that the Puruṣhottam is none other than Krishna Himself. All Vedic and Smṛiti texts celebrate Him as the Supreme Being. While other deities like Lord Ram, Vishnu, and Shiva are worshipped, they are manifestations of the same Supreme Personality, not separate entities. This verse underscores Krishna’s position as the ultimate, beyond both matter and individual souls.
commentary_summary: Puruṣhottam (Supreme Divine Personality) is Krishna Himself, transcending both the perishable material world and imperishable souls, celebrated in all Vedic and Smṛiti texts.
theme: Krishna as Puruṣhottam, the Supreme Personality transcending all material and spiritual entities.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् |
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत || 19||
transliteration: yo mām evam asammūḍho jānāti puruṣhottamam sa sarva-vid bhajati māṁ sarva-bhāvena bhārata
translation: BG 15.19: Those who know Me without doubt as the Supreme Divine Personality truly have complete knowledge. O Arjun, they worship Me with their whole being.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna explains that knowing Him as the Supreme Divine Personality, or Bhagavān, is the highest form of knowledge. God manifests in three forms—Brahman (formless, omnipresent), Paramātmā (Supersoul residing in all beings), and Bhagavān (personal, with Leelas, Names, Forms, and Associates). While Brahman and Paramātmā show partial realization, Bhagavān manifests all His energies and pastimes, making this the most complete realization. Those who worship Him as Bhagavān with full devotion possess perfect knowledge.
commentary_summary: Complete knowledge is attained by knowing and worshipping Krishna as Bhagavān, the Supreme Divine Personality, beyond His manifestations as Brahman and Paramātmā.
theme: Highest realization of God is recognizing Him as Bhagavān and worshipping Him wholeheartedly.

speaker: Shree Krishna
text_sanskrit:
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ |
एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत || 20||
transliteration: iti guhyatamaṁ śhāstram idam uktaṁ mayānagha etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛita-kṛityaśh cha bhārata
translation: BG 15.20: I have shared this most secret principle of the Vedic scriptures with you, O sinless Arjun. By understanding this, a person becomes enlightened, and fulfills all that is to be accomplished.
commentary_full: Shree Krishna concludes Chapter 15 by affirming that He has revealed the essence of all secret Vedic knowledge to Arjun. This includes understanding the nature of the material and spiritual worlds, the distinction between the perishable and imperishable, and the Supreme Divine Personality. Grasping this knowledge leads to enlightenment, equips the seeker to perform all necessary duties effectively, and guides them toward the ultimate goal of God-realization.
commentary_summary: Understanding this most secret knowledge grants enlightenment and ensures fulfillment of all righteous duties, leading one toward God-realization.
theme: The culmination of Vedic wisdom—realizing the Supreme, achieving enlightenment, and fulfilling one’s duties.

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः |
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम् || 1||
Transliteration:
abhayaṁ sattva-saṁśhuddhir jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ |
dānaṁ damaśh cha yajñaśh cha svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam ||
Translation: Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and yoga, charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity, and straightforwardness.
commentary_full: Krishna begins by listing divine qualities essential for liberation.
commentary_summary: Divine qualities begin with purity and fearlessness.
theme: Divine qualities

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् |
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् || 2||
Transliteration:
ahiṁsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śhāntir apaiśhunam |
dayā bhūteṣhv aloluptvaṁ mārdavaṁ hrīr achāpalam ||
Translation: Non-violence, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, peace, compassion, gentleness.
commentary_full: These qualities promote harmony and spiritual growth.
commentary_summary: Compassion and truth define divine nature.
theme: Virtues

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता |
भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत || 3||
Transliteration: tejaḥ kṣhamā dhṛitiḥ śhaucham adroho nātimānitā |
Translation: Energy, forgiveness, purity, absence of pride.
commentary_full: These traits belong to divine personalities.
commentary_summary: Humility completes divine qualities.
theme: Divine nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च |
अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम् || 4||
Transliteration: dambho darpo ’bhimānaśh cha krodhaḥ pāruṣhyam eva cha |
Translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, harshness and ignorance are demonic qualities.
commentary_full: Krishna contrasts divine traits with demonic nature.
commentary_summary: Demonic nature is rooted in ego.
theme: Demonic qualities

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता |
मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव || 5||
Transliteration: daivī sampad vimokṣhāya nibandhāyāsurī matā |
Translation: Divine qualities lead to liberation, demonic to bondage.
commentary_full: Krishna reassures Arjuna of his divine nature.
commentary_summary: Divine leads to freedom.
theme: Liberation vs bondage

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च |
Transliteration: dvau bhūta-sargau loke ’smin daiva āsura eva cha |
Translation: There are two types of beings: divine and demonic.
commentary_full: Human nature is divided into two paths.
commentary_summary: Two natures exist.
theme: Human nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः |
Transliteration: pravṛittiṁ cha nivṛittiṁ cha janā na vidur āsurāḥ |
Translation: Demonic people do not know what to do or avoid.
commentary_full: Lack of moral clarity defines demonic nature.
commentary_summary: No moral direction.
theme: Moral ignorance

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् |
Transliteration: asatyam apratiṣhṭhaṁ te jagad āhur anīśhvaram |
Translation: They say the world is without truth or God.
commentary_full: Demonic mindset rejects divine order.
commentary_summary: Denial of God.
theme: Materialism

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः |
Transliteration: etāṁ dṛiṣhṭim avaṣhṭabhya naṣhṭātmāno ’lpa-buddhayaḥ |
Translation: Holding such views, they act destructively.
commentary_full: Wrong beliefs lead to harmful actions.
commentary_summary: False views destroy.
theme: Consequences

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Driven by desire and pride, they act wrongly.
commentary_summary: Desire controls them

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They are bound by endless worries.
commentary_summary: Attachment creates anxiety

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They are trapped by desires and greed.
commentary_summary: Greed binds

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They think wealth is everything.
commentary_summary: Material obsession

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They boast about their power.
commentary_summary: Ego dominance

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They think they are superior.
commentary_summary: False pride

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They are confused and lost.
commentary_summary: Mental disturbance

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They perform fake rituals.
commentary_summary: Hypocrisy

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They are driven by ego and anger.
commentary_summary: Ego + anger

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: God casts them into negative births.
commentary_summary: Spiritual downfall

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They fall into lower states repeatedly.
commentary_summary: Cycle of downfall

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Lust, anger, greed are gates to hell.
commentary_summary: Three gates to hell

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Avoid these to attain good.
commentary_summary: Avoid negativity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Ignoring scripture leads to failure.
commentary_summary: Scripture is important

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Follow scriptures to know right action.
commentary_summary: Follow dharma

speaker: Arjuna
Sanskrit text:
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः |
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः || 1||
Transliteration:
ye śhāstra-vidhim utsṛijya yajante śhraddhayānvitāḥ |
teṣhāṁ niṣhṭhā tu kā kṛiṣhṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ ||
Translation: What is the condition of those who worship with faith but ignore scriptures?
commentary_full: Arjuna asks about people who have faith but do not follow scriptural guidance. He wants to understand whether such faith is pure, passionate, or ignorant.
commentary_summary: Question about faith without scripture.
theme: Nature of faith

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा |
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु || 2||
Transliteration: trividhā bhavati śhraddhā dehināṁ sā svabhāva-jā |
Translation: Faith is of three types: sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic.
commentary_full: Krishna explains that faith depends on one's nature and is categorized into three gunas.
commentary_summary: Three types of faith.
theme: Three gunas

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत |
Transliteration: sattvānurūpā sarvasya śhraddhā bhavati bhārata |
Translation: A person is defined by their faith.
commentary_full: Faith shapes one's identity and actions.
commentary_summary: Faith defines personality.
theme: Identity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Different people worship according to their nature.
commentary_full: Worship reflects inner qualities.
commentary_summary: Nature decides worship.
theme: Faith expression

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Ego-driven austerities are harmful.
commentary_full: People performing extreme austerities without wisdom harm themselves.
commentary_summary: Wrong austerity.
theme: Misguided practice

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: They torture themselves and the divine within.
commentary_full: Such practices are considered demonic.
commentary_summary: Self-harm is ignorance.
theme: Demonic practice

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Food, sacrifice, austerity and charity are of three types.
commentary_full: All actions are influenced by the three gunas.
commentary_summary: Everything has three types.
theme: Threefold division

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Sattvic food increases health and happiness.
commentary_full: Pure food supports physical and mental well-being.
commentary_summary: Healthy food is sattvic.
theme: Sattvic food

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Rajasic food is spicy and causes pain.
commentary_full: Such food leads to restlessness.
commentary_summary: Stimulating food.
theme: Rajasic food

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Tamasic food is stale and impure.
commentary_full: Impure food leads to dullness.
commentary_summary: Unhealthy food.
theme: Tamasic food

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते |
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः || 11||
Transliteration: aphalākāṅkṣhibhir yajño vidhi-dṛiṣhṭo ya ijyate |
Translation: Sacrifice done without expectation of reward is sattvic.
commentary_full: A true sacrifice is performed as duty, without desire for results. Such action purifies the mind and aligns with dharma.
commentary_summary: Selfless sacrifice is sattvic.
theme: Sattvic sacrifice

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् |
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् || 12||
Transliteration: abhisandhāya tu phalaṁ dambhārtham api chaiva yat |
Translation: Sacrifice done for reward or show is rajasic.
commentary_full: When actions are motivated by ego or desire for recognition, they fall into the rajasic category.
commentary_summary: Desire-driven sacrifice.
theme: Rajasic sacrifice

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् |
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते || 13||
Transliteration: vidhi-hīnam asṛiṣhṭānnaṁ mantra-hīnam adakṣiṇam |
Translation: Sacrifice without faith or rules is tamasic.
commentary_full: Ignoring proper method and lacking devotion leads to ineffective and ignorant action.
commentary_summary: Ignorant sacrifice.
theme: Tamasic sacrifice

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् |
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते || 14||
Transliteration: deva-dvija-guru-prājña-pūjanaṁ śhaucham ārjavam |
Translation: Respect, purity, simplicity, and non-violence are austerities of the body.
commentary_full: Physical discipline includes honoring elders, maintaining cleanliness, and practicing non-violence.
commentary_summary: Body discipline.
theme: Austerity of body

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् |
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते || 15||
Transliteration: anudvega-karaṁ vākyaṁ satyaṁ priya-hitaṁ cha yat |
Translation: Truthful, kind, and beneficial speech is austerity of speech.
commentary_full: Words should not hurt others; they must be truthful and pleasant.
commentary_summary: Speech discipline.
theme: Austerity of speech

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
मनः प्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः |
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते || 16||
Transliteration: manaḥ-prasādaḥ saumyatvaṁ maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ |
Translation: Calmness, silence, self-control are austerities of the mind.
commentary_full: Mental discipline is essential for inner peace and clarity.
commentary_summary: Mind discipline.
theme: Austerity of mind

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः |
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते || 17||
Transliteration: śhraddhayā parayā taptaṁ tapas tat tri-vidhaṁ naraiḥ |
Translation: Austerity done with faith and no expectation is sattvic.
commentary_full: True discipline is practiced sincerely without seeking rewards.
commentary_summary: Pure austerity.
theme: Sattvic austerity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् |
Transliteration: satkāra-māna-pūjārthaṁ tapo dambhena chaiva yat |
Translation: Austerity done for respect is rajasic.
commentary_full: Actions driven by pride are unstable and temporary.
commentary_summary: Show-off austerity.
theme: Rajasic austerity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः |
Transliteration: mūḍha-grāheṇātmano yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
Translation: Self-torturing austerity is tamasic.
commentary_full: Such practices harm the body and mind and lack wisdom.
commentary_summary: Harmful austerity.
theme: Tamasic austerity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे |
Transliteration: dātavyam iti yad dānaṁ dīyate ’nupakāriṇe |
Translation: Charity given without expectation is sattvic.
commentary_full: True charity is given out of duty and compassion.
commentary_summary: Pure charity.
theme: Sattvic charity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः |
Transliteration: yat tu pratyupakārārthaṁ phalam uddiśhya vā punaḥ |
Translation: Charity expecting return is rajasic.
commentary_full: Giving with expectation reduces spiritual value.
commentary_summary: Selfish charity.
theme: Rajasic charity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते |
Transliteration: adeśha-kāle yad dānam apātrebhyaśh cha dīyate |
Translation: Charity given improperly is tamasic.
commentary_full: Giving without respect or awareness is ineffective.
commentary_summary: Wrong charity.
theme: Tamasic charity

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: ॐ तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः |
Transliteration: om tat sat iti nirdeśho brahmaṇas tri-vidhaḥ smṛitaḥ |
Translation: Om Tat Sat represents the Absolute Truth.
commentary_full: These sacred sounds symbolize divine reality.
commentary_summary: Divine symbols.
theme: Sacred symbols

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः |
Transliteration: tasmād om ity udāhṛitya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ |
Translation: Sacrifice begins with Om.
commentary_full: Spiritual acts are sanctified by divine remembrance.
commentary_summary: Sacred beginning.
theme: Spiritual practice

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: तदित्यनभिसंधाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः |
Transliteration: tat ity anabhisandhāya phalaṁ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ |
Translation: Tat signifies action without desire for results.
commentary_full: Actions should be done for higher purpose.
commentary_summary: Detachment.
theme: Selfless action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते |
Transliteration: sad-bhāve sādhu-bhāve cha sad ity etat prayujyate |
Translation: Sat represents truth and goodness.
commentary_full: It signifies positive and righteous action.
commentary_summary: Truth and goodness.
theme: Truth

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते |
Transliteration: yajñe tapasi dāne cha sthitiḥ sad iti chochyate |
Translation: Sat also means dedication in actions.
commentary_full: Consistency in good actions is considered Sat.
commentary_summary: Spiritual dedication.
theme: Consistency

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् |
Transliteration: aśhraddhayā hutaṁ dattaṁ tapas taptaṁ kṛitaṁ cha yat |
Translation: Actions without faith are useless.
commentary_full: Without faith, even good actions lose value.
commentary_summary: Faith is essential.
theme: Importance of faith

speaker: Arjuna
Sanskrit text:
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् |
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक् केशिनिषूदन || 1||
Transliteration:
sannyāsasya mahā-bāho tattvam icchāmi veditum |
tyāgasya cha hṛṣīkeśa pṛthak keśi-niṣūdana ||
Translation: Arjuna said: O Krishna, I wish to understand renunciation and sacrifice separately.
commentary_full: Arjuna begins the final chapter by asking the difference between renouncing actions and renouncing their results. This question sets the foundation for understanding true detachment.
commentary_summary: Arjuna asks about renunciation.
theme: Renunciation inquiry

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः |
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः || 2||
Transliteration:
kāmyānāṁ karmaṇāṁ nyāsaṁ sannyāsaṁ kavayo viduḥ |
sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṁ prāhus tyāgaṁ vicakṣhaṇāḥ ||
Translation: Renouncing desires is called sannyasa, and giving up results is tyaga.
commentary_full: Krishna clarifies that sannyasa is giving up desire-driven actions, while tyaga is renouncing attachment to results.
commentary_summary: Difference between sannyasa and tyaga.
theme: Definition of renunciation

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः |
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे || 3||
Transliteration: tyājyaṁ doṣha-vad ity eke karma prāhur manīṣhiṇaḥ |
Translation: Some say all actions should be renounced, others say sacrifice and charity should not be.
commentary_full: Different philosophies exist regarding renunciation, but Krishna resolves this confusion.
commentary_summary: Confusion about renunciation.
theme: Philosophical debate

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम |
त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः || 4||
Transliteration: niśhchayaṁ śhṛiṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama |
Translation: Listen to My conclusion: renunciation is of three types.
commentary_full: Krishna introduces the threefold nature of renunciation based on gunas.
commentary_summary: Three types of renunciation.
theme: Threefold tyaga

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् |
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम् || 5||
Transliteration: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyaṁ kāryam eva tat |
Translation: Sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not be given up.
commentary_full: These actions purify the soul and must be performed.
commentary_summary: Important duties must continue.
theme: Essential actions

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Perform duties without attachment.
commentary_summary: Detached action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Avoid giving up duties out of ignorance.
commentary_summary: Ignorant renunciation

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Renunciation due to fear is rajasic.
commentary_summary: Fear-based action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Duty without attachment is sattvic.
commentary_summary: True renunciation

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: The wise are free from doubt.
commentary_summary: Clarity of mind

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: One cannot completely renounce action.
commentary_summary: Action is unavoidable

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Results affect those attached, not the detached.
commentary_summary: Attachment causes results

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Five factors cause action.
commentary_summary: Causes of action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Body, doer, senses, effort and divine are factors.
commentary_summary: Five components

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: All actions arise from these factors.
commentary_summary: Source of action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Ignorance sees self as sole doer.
commentary_summary: False ego

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Detached person is not bound by actions.
commentary_summary: Freedom from karma

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Knowledge, action, and doer are threefold.
commentary_summary: Threefold nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: These are divided by gunas.
commentary_summary: Guna classification

speaker: Shree Krishna
Translation: Seeing unity in all beings is sattvic knowledge.
commentary_summary: Unity is wisdom

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् |
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम् || 21||
Transliteration: pṛithaktvena tu yaj jñānaṁ nānā-bhāvān pṛithag-vidhān |
Translation: Knowledge that sees diversity and separateness in all beings is rajasic.
commentary_full: Rajasic knowledge perceives division and multiplicity instead of unity. It focuses on differences, leading to attachment, competition, and conflict.
commentary_summary: Seeing diversity as separate is rajasic knowledge.
theme: Rajasic knowledge

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् |
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम् || 22||
Transliteration: yat tu kṛitsnavad ekasmin kārye saktam ahaitukam |
Translation: Knowledge that is narrow, irrational, and clings to one idea is tamasic.
commentary_full: Tamasic knowledge is limited and irrational. It lacks understanding of truth and is driven by ignorance and blind attachment.
commentary_summary: Narrow and irrational thinking is tamasic knowledge.
theme: Tamasic knowledge

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् |
अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते || 23||
Transliteration: niyataṁ saṅga-rahitam arāga-dveṣhataḥ kṛitam |
Translation: Action done without attachment and without desire is sattvic.
commentary_full: Sattvic action is performed as duty, free from likes and dislikes, and without expectation of results.
commentary_summary: Selfless action is sattvic.
theme: Sattvic action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहंकारेण वा पुनः |
क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम् || 24||
Transliteration: yat tu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ |
Translation: Action done with desire and ego is rajasic.
commentary_full: Rajasic action is driven by personal gain and pride. It leads to stress and attachment.
commentary_summary: Desire-driven action is rajasic.
theme: Rajasic action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् |
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते || 25||
Transliteration: anubandhaṁ kṣhayaṁ hiṁsām anapekṣhya cha pauruṣham |
Translation: Action performed in ignorance, without considering consequences, is tamasic.
commentary_full: Tamasic action is careless and harmful. It ignores consequences and arises from delusion.
commentary_summary: Ignorant action is tamasic.
theme: Tamasic action

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः |
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते || 26||
Transliteration: mukta-saṅgo ’nahaṁ-vādī dhṛity-utsāha-samanvitaḥ |
Translation: The doer who is free from attachment and ego is sattvic.
commentary_full: A sattvic doer performs duties with dedication and without ego, remaining steady in success and failure.
commentary_summary: Egoless doer is sattvic.
theme: Sattvic doer

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः |
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः || 27||
Transliteration: rāgī karma-phala-prepsur lubdho hiṁsātmako ’śhuchiḥ |
Translation: The doer who is attached, greedy, and emotional is rajasic.
