commentary_full: Rajasic doers are driven by results, emotions, and selfish desires.
commentary_summary: Emotional and greedy doer is rajasic.
theme: Rajasic doer

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः |
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते || 28||
Transliteration: ayuktaḥ prākṛitaḥ stabdhaḥ śhaṭho naiṣhkṛitiko ’lasaḥ |
Translation: The doer who is lazy, stubborn, and careless is tamasic.
commentary_full: Tamasic doers lack discipline and awareness, acting irresponsibly and without clarity.
commentary_summary: Lazy and ignorant doer is tamasic.
theme: Tamasic doer

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु |
Transliteration: buddher bhedaṁ dhṛiteśh chaiva guṇatas tri-vidhaṁ śhṛiṇu |
Translation: Now hear about three types of intellect and determination.
commentary_full: Krishna explains that intellect and determination are also influenced by the three gunas.
commentary_summary: Three types of intellect.
theme: Threefold intellect

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये |
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी || 30||
Transliteration: pravṛittiṁ cha nivṛittiṁ cha kāryākārye bhayābhaye |
Translation: Intellect that knows right and wrong is sattvic.
commentary_full: Sattvic intellect clearly distinguishes between duty and non-duty.
commentary_summary: Right understanding is sattvic.
theme: Sattvic intellect

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च |
Transliteration: yayā dharmam adharmam cha kāryaṁ chākāryam eva cha |
Translation: Confused intellect is rajasic.
commentary_full: Rajasic intellect struggles to differentiate between right and wrong.
commentary_summary: Confused intellect.
theme: Rajasic intellect

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता |
Transliteration: adharmaṁ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasā-vṛitā |
Translation: Deluded intellect is tamasic.
commentary_full: Tamasic intellect mistakes wrong for right due to ignorance.
commentary_summary: Wrong perception.
theme: Tamasic intellect

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः |
Transliteration: dhṛityā yayā dhārayate manaḥ-prāṇendriya-kriyāḥ |
Translation: Determination with discipline is sattvic.
commentary_full: Sattvic determination maintains control over mind and senses.
commentary_summary: Disciplined determination.
theme: Sattvic determination

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन |
Transliteration: yayā tu dharma-kāmārthān dhṛityā dhārayate ’rjuna |
Translation: Determination driven by desire is rajasic.
commentary_full: Rajasic determination is based on goals of pleasure and success.
commentary_summary: Goal-driven determination.
theme: Rajasic determination

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यया स्वप्नं भयṁ शोकं विषादं मदमेव च |
Transliteration: yayā svapnaṁ bhayaṁ śhokaṁ viṣhādaṁ madam eva cha |
Translation: Determination rooted in fear and laziness is tamasic.
commentary_full: Tamasic determination clings to negative states and avoids growth.
commentary_summary: Negative determination.
theme: Tamasic determination

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ |
Transliteration: sukhaṁ tv idānīṁ tri-vidhaṁ śhṛiṇu me bharatarṣhabha |
Translation: Now hear about three types of happiness.
commentary_full: Krishna introduces the classification of happiness based on gunas.
commentary_summary: Three types of happiness.
theme: Threefold happiness

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् |
Transliteration: yat tad agre viṣham iva pariṇāme ’mṛitopamam |
Translation: Happiness that begins like poison but ends like nectar is sattvic.
commentary_full: Sattvic happiness comes from discipline and leads to lasting joy.
commentary_summary: Long-term happiness.
theme: Sattvic happiness

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् |
Transliteration: viṣhayendriya-sanyogād yat tad agre ’mṛitopamam |
Translation: Pleasure from senses is rajasic happiness.
commentary_full: It feels good initially but leads to suffering later.
commentary_summary: Short-term pleasure.
theme: Rajasic happiness

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः |
Transliteration: yad agre chānubandhe cha sukhaṁ mohanam ātmanaḥ |
Translation: Happiness based on laziness and sleep is tamasic.
commentary_full: Tamasic happiness comes from ignorance and leads to delusion.
commentary_summary: Ignorant pleasure.
theme: Tamasic happiness

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः |
Transliteration: na tad asti pṛithivyāṁ vā divi deveṣhu vā punaḥ |
Translation: No being is free from the three gunas.
commentary_full: All beings are influenced by sattva, rajas, and tamas.
commentary_summary: Gunas are universal.
theme: Universal nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप |
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः || 41||
Transliteration: brāhmaṇa-kṣhatriya-viśhāṁ śhūdrāṇāṁ cha parantapa |
Translation: Duties of different groups are determined by their nature.
commentary_full: Krishna explains that social duties arise from one's inherent qualities (gunas), not birth. Each person has a natural role to play.
commentary_summary: Duties based on nature.
theme: Division of duties

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च |
Transliteration: śhamo damas tapaḥ śhauchaṁ kṣhāntir ārjavam eva cha |
Translation: Peace, self-control, purity and wisdom are qualities of a Brahmin.
commentary_full: Brahmin qualities reflect knowledge, discipline, and inner purity.
commentary_summary: Qualities of Brahmin.
theme: Brahmin nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् |
Transliteration: śhauryaṁ tejo dhṛitir dākṣhyaṁ yuddhe chāpy apalāyanam |
Translation: Courage and leadership are qualities of a Kshatriya.
commentary_full: Kshatriyas are responsible for protection, leadership, and courage.
commentary_summary: Warrior qualities.
theme: Kshatriya nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् |
Transliteration: kṛiṣi-go-rakṣhya-vāṇijyaṁ vaiśhya-karma svabhāva-jam |
Translation: Farming, trade and business are duties of Vaishyas.
commentary_full: Vaishyas contribute through economic activities and resource management.
commentary_summary: Business duties.
theme: Vaishya nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः |
Transliteration: sve sve karmaṇy abhirataḥ saṁsiddhiṁ labhate naraḥ |
Translation: By doing one's duty, one attains perfection.
commentary_full: Following one's own path sincerely leads to spiritual growth.
commentary_summary: Duty leads to perfection.
theme: Path to perfection

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् |
Transliteration: yataḥ pravṛittir bhūtānāṁ yena sarvam idaṁ tatam |
Translation: Worship through one's duty leads to the Divine.
commentary_full: All work can become spiritual when done as an offering to God.
commentary_summary: Work becomes worship.
theme: Karma as worship

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् |
Transliteration: śhreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt |
Translation: Better to follow one's own duty imperfectly.
commentary_full: Doing another's duty perfectly is inferior to doing one's own duty imperfectly.
commentary_summary: Follow your own path.
theme: Swadharma

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् |
Transliteration: sahajaṁ karma kaunteya sa-doṣham api na tyajet |
Translation: Do not abandon your natural duty.
commentary_full: Every duty has imperfections, but it should not be abandoned.
commentary_summary: Do not avoid duty.
theme: Duty with flaws

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः |
Transliteration: asakta-buddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigata-spṛihaḥ |
Translation: Detached mind leads to liberation.
commentary_full: Freedom from desire and attachment brings peace.
commentary_summary: Detachment leads to freedom.
theme: Liberation

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे |
Transliteration: siddhiṁ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me |
Translation: Learn how one reaches Brahman.
commentary_full: Krishna explains the path to ultimate realization.
commentary_summary: Path to Brahman.
theme: Spiritual goal

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च |
Transliteration: buddhyā viśhuddhayā yukto dhṛityātmānaṁ niyamya cha |
Translation: Purify intellect and control mind.
commentary_full: Spiritual growth requires discipline and inner control.
commentary_summary: Self-control.
theme: Spiritual discipline

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः |
Transliteration: vivikta-sevī laghv-āśhī yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ |
Translation: Practice solitude, control and simplicity.
commentary_full: A disciplined life supports spiritual realization.
commentary_summary: Simple living.
theme: Spiritual lifestyle

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् |
Transliteration: ahaṅkāraṁ balaṁ darpaṁ kāmaṁ krodhaṁ parigraham |
Translation: Give up ego, anger and desire.
commentary_full: Letting go of negative qualities leads to liberation.
commentary_summary: Let go of ego.
theme: Inner purification

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति |
Transliteration: brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śhochati na kāṅkṣhati |
Translation: One who realizes Brahman is peaceful.
commentary_full: Such a person is free from sorrow and desire.
commentary_summary: Peaceful state.
theme: Realization

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः |
Transliteration: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaśh chāsmi tattvataḥ |
Translation: Through devotion one truly knows God.
commentary_full: Bhakti leads to true realization of the Divine.
commentary_summary: Devotion reveals truth.
theme: Bhakti path

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः |
Transliteration: sarva-karmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo mad-vyapāśhrayaḥ |
Translation: Perform all actions with devotion.
commentary_full: Surrendering actions to God leads to liberation.
commentary_summary: Offer actions to God.
theme: Karma yoga

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः |
Transliteration: chetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-paraḥ |
Translation: Mentally surrender all actions to Me.
commentary_full: Inner surrender removes stress and ego.
commentary_summary: Mental surrender.
theme: Inner surrender

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: मच्चित्तः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि |
Transliteration: mach-chittaḥ sarva-durgāṇi mat-prasādāt tariṣhyasi |
Translation: With devotion, you overcome obstacles.
commentary_full: Faith in God helps overcome life's challenges.
commentary_summary: Faith removes obstacles.
theme: Divine support

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: यदहंकारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे |
Transliteration: yad ahaṅkāram āśhritya na yotsya iti manyase |
Translation: If you act from ego, you will fail.
commentary_full: Ego leads to wrong decisions and suffering.
commentary_summary: Ego misleads.
theme: Ego danger

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा |
Transliteration: svabhāva-jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā |
Translation: Your nature will compel you to act.
commentary_full: One cannot escape one's nature; it drives actions inevitably.
commentary_summary: Nature controls action.
theme: Power of nature

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति |
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया || 61||
Transliteration: īśhvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṁ hṛid-deśhe ’rjuna tiṣhṭhati |
Translation: God resides in the hearts of all beings and directs their movements.
commentary_full: Krishna reveals that the Supreme Lord dwells within every being as the inner controller. Though individuals feel independent, divine will subtly guides their journey.
commentary_summary: God resides in all hearts.
theme: Divine presence

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत |
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् || 62||
Transliteration: tam eva śharaṇaṁ gachchha sarva-bhāvena bhārata |
Translation: Surrender to Him completely; you will attain peace.
commentary_full: Krishna advises total surrender to the Divine. Through surrender, one attains lasting peace and liberation.
commentary_summary: Surrender brings peace.
theme: Surrender to God

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया |
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु || 63||
Transliteration: iti te jñānam ākhyātaṁ guhyād guhyataraṁ mayā |
Translation: Reflect on this knowledge and act as you wish.
commentary_full: Krishna gives Arjuna freedom of choice after explaining the highest wisdom.
commentary_summary: Act with understanding.
theme: Free will

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः |
Transliteration: sarva-guhyatamaṁ bhūyaḥ śhṛiṇu me paramaṁ vachaḥ |
Translation: Hear My supreme instruction again.
commentary_full: Krishna prepares to reveal the ultimate teaching of the Gita.
commentary_summary: Final instruction begins.
theme: Ultimate teaching

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु |
Transliteration: man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru |
Translation: Think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me.
commentary_full: Krishna emphasizes devotion as the simplest path to reach Him.
commentary_summary: Devotion leads to God.
theme: Bhakti yoga

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज |
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः || 66||
Transliteration: sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śharaṇaṁ vraja |
Translation: Abandon all duties and surrender to Me; I will free you from sin.
commentary_full: This is the ultimate teaching of the Gita. Surrender to God brings liberation from all karmic bondage.
commentary_summary: Ultimate surrender.
theme: Supreme teaching

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन |
Transliteration: idaṁ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadāchana |
Translation: Do not share this teaching with the unworthy.
commentary_full: Sacred knowledge must be shared only with sincere seekers.
commentary_summary: Protect sacred knowledge.
theme: Eligibility

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति |
Transliteration: ya idaṁ paramaṁ guhyaṁ mad-bhakteṣhv abhidhāsyati |
Translation: One who teaches this to devotees attains Me.
commentary_full: Sharing spiritual knowledge with devotion is a sacred act.
commentary_summary: Teaching leads to God.
theme: Spiritual sharing

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः |
Transliteration: na cha tasmān manuṣhyeṣhu kaśhchin me priya-kṛittamaḥ |
Translation: No one is dearer to Me than such a teacher.
commentary_full: Krishna values those who spread divine wisdom.
commentary_summary: Teachers are most प्रिय.
theme: Value of teaching

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः |
Transliteration: adhyeṣhyate cha ya imaṁ dharmyaṁ saṁvādam āvayoḥ |
Translation: One who studies this dialogue worships Me.
commentary_full: Studying the Gita itself is a form of devotion.
commentary_summary: Study is worship.
theme: Sacred study

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः |
Transliteration: śhraddhāvān anasūyaśh cha śhṛiṇuyād api yo naraḥ |
Translation: Even hearing with faith leads to liberation.
commentary_full: Sincere listening itself brings spiritual merit.
commentary_summary: Listening with faith liberates.
theme: Power of listening

speaker: Shree Krishna
Sanskrit text: कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा |
Transliteration: kachchid etach chrutaṁ pārtha tvayāikāgreṇa chetasā |
Translation: Have you understood this fully?
commentary_full: Krishna checks if Arjuna has grasped the teaching.
commentary_summary: Final check.
theme: Reflection

speaker: Arjuna
Sanskrit text: नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत |
Transliteration: naṣhṭo mohaḥ smṛitir labdhā tvat-prasādān mayāchyuta |
Translation: My confusion is gone; I will act as You say.
commentary_full: Arjuna regains clarity and is ready to act according to dharma.
commentary_summary: Clarity achieved.
theme: Transformation

speaker: Sanjaya
Sanskrit text: इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः |
Transliteration: ity ahaṁ vāsudevasya pārthasya cha mahātmanaḥ |
Translation: Sanjaya narrates the divine conversation.
commentary_full: Sanjaya reflects on the sacred dialogue.
commentary_summary: Narration.
theme: Divine dialogue

speaker: Sanjaya
Sanskrit text: व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम् |
Transliteration: vyāsa-prasādāch chrutavān etad guhyam ahaṁ param |
Translation: By grace, I heard this wisdom.
commentary_full: Divine grace allows one to access higher knowledge.
commentary_summary: Grace reveals truth.
theme: Divine grace

speaker: Sanjaya
Sanskrit text: राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् |
Transliteration: rājan saṁsmṛitya saṁsmṛitya saṁvādam imam adbhutam |
Translation: Remembering this brings joy again and again.
commentary_full: Reflecting on divine wisdom brings repeated joy.
commentary_summary: Joy in remembrance.
theme: Reflection joy

speaker: Sanjaya
Sanskrit text: तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः |
Transliteration: tach cha saṁsmṛitya saṁsmṛitya rūpam atyadbhutaṁ hareḥ |
Translation: Remembering the divine form amazes me.
commentary_full: The vision of Krishna fills Sanjaya with wonder.
commentary_summary: Divine vision amazes.
theme: Divine form

speaker: Sanjaya
Sanskrit text: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः |
Transliteration: yatra yogeśhvaraḥ kṛiṣhṇo yatra pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ |
Translation: Where Krishna and Arjuna are, there is victory.
commentary_full: Sanjaya concludes that wherever divine guidance and righteous action unite, success and prosperity follow.
commentary_summary: Victory with dharma.
theme: Final conclusion

speaker: Shri Krishna
sanskrit:
पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान्गुणान् |
कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु || 22||
transliteration:
puruṣhaḥ prakṛiti-stho hi bhuṅkte prakṛiti-jān guṇān
kāraṇaṁ guṇa-saṅgo ’sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu
translation: When the puruṣh (individual soul), seated in prakṛiti (material energy), desires to enjoy the three guṇas, attachment to these guṇas becomes the cause of its birth in superior and inferior wombs.

commentary.full:
Shri Krishna explains the mechanism behind the soul’s experience of pleasure and pain. Identifying the body as the self, the soul directs the body toward enjoyment of material pleasures. Since the body is composed of material energy governed by the three guṇas—goodness, passion, and ignorance—the soul becomes entangled with these modes.

Due to ego, the soul assumes the role of doer and enjoyer, even though actions are performed by the body, mind, and intellect. Just as a driver is held responsible for a vehicle’s accident, the soul is accountable for the activities carried out through the body it animates. Consequently, the soul accumulates karmas over countless lifetimes. Attachment to the guṇas stored in this karmic stock leads to repeated births in higher and lower forms of life.
commentary.summary: Attachment of the soul to the three guṇas causes karmic accumulation, which results in repeated births across superior and inferior life forms.

theme: Bondage of the soul through attachment to material nature

speaker: Shri Krishna
sanskrit:
उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः |
परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन्पुरुषः परः || 23||
transliteration:
upadraṣhṭānumantā cha bhartā bhoktā maheśhvaraḥ
paramātmeti chāpy ukto dehe ’smin puruṣhaḥ paraḥ
translation: Within the body also resides the Supreme Lord. He is said to be the Witness, the Permitter, the Supporter, the Transcendental Enjoyer, the ultimate Controller, and the Paramātmā (Supreme Soul).

commentary.full:
After explaining the position of the jīvātmā (individual soul), Shri Krishna now reveals the role of the Paramātmā (Supreme Soul), who also resides within the same body. While the jīvātmā is the knower of one body, the Paramātmā is the knower of all bodies. He exists simultaneously as the all-pervading Supreme and as the indwelling presence in every living being.

The Paramātmā acts as the witness of all actions, the permitter who sanctions activities, the supporter who sustains life, and the supreme controller who governs the universe. Though He accompanies the jīvātmā through all forms of life—human, animal, or insect—He remains unattached and neutral, merely observing and administering karmic results.

The Upaniṣhads describe the jīvātmā and Paramātmā as two birds sitting on the same tree (the body). One bird (the jīvātmā) enjoys the fruits of actions, experiencing pleasure and pain, while the other (the Paramātmā) simply watches as a compassionate friend. When the jīvātmā turns its attention toward the Paramātmā, it transcends sorrow and attains liberation. Bondage or freedom depends on how the soul exercises its free will—turning away from or toward the Supreme.
commentary.summary: The Paramātmā resides in every body as the witness, controller, and giver of karmic results; turning toward Him frees the soul from bondage.

theme: Presence and role of the Supreme Soul within all beings

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तं तु दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् | सुग्रीवः सहसा भीतः प्रविवेश महागिरिम् ||
transliteration: taṁ tu dṛṣṭvā mahā-bāhuṁ rāmaṁ satya-parākramam | sugrīvaḥ sahasā bhītaḥ praviveśa mahā-girim ||
translation: Seeing the mighty-armed Rama, known for his true valor, Sugriva became afraid and quickly entered the great mountain.
commentary_full: Sugriva, who was living in fear of his brother Vali, mistook Rama for a potential threat. Even though Rama radiated divine strength and righteousness, Sugriva’s past trauma caused him to react with fear. This verse highlights how fear can cloud judgment and prevent recognition of truth.
commentary_summary: Sugriva fears Rama due to past trauma and misunderstanding.
theme: Fear and misjudgment

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा भयसंविग्नं सुग्रीवं प्लवगर्षभम् | हनुमान् मन्त्रमध्ये तु स्थितः प्राज्ञो व्यतिष्ठत ||
transliteration: taṁ dṛṣṭvā bhaya-saṁvignaṁ sugrīvaṁ plava-garṣabham | hanumān mantra-madhye tu sthitaḥ prājño vyatiṣṭhata ||
translation: Seeing Sugriva distressed with fear, Hanuman, the wise among the vanaras, stood calmly to assess the situation.
commentary_full: Hanuman represents intelligence and calmness. While Sugriva panics, Hanuman observes and thinks before acting. This shows the importance of wisdom over impulsive fear.
commentary_summary: Hanuman remains calm and observes wisely.
theme: Wisdom over fear

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: स तु दृष्ट्वा हनुमन्तं सुग्रीवः प्लवगर्षभः | उवाच भीतः संत्रस्तो वानराणां हितैषिणम् ||
transliteration: sa tu dṛṣṭvā hanumantaṁ sugrīvaḥ plava-garṣabhaḥ | uvāca bhītaḥ saṁtrastō vānarāṇāṁ hitaiṣiṇam ||
translation: Sugriva, frightened and disturbed, spoke to Hanuman, the well-wisher of the vanaras.
commentary_full: Sugriva turns to Hanuman for guidance, showing trust in wisdom. Even in fear, seeking wise counsel is a sign of good leadership.
commentary_summary: Sugriva seeks guidance from Hanuman.
theme: Seeking wisdom

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः | हनुमान् बुद्धिसम्पन्नः प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ||
transliteration: tasya tad-vacanaṁ śrutvā sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ | hanumān buddhi-sampannaḥ prahṛṣṭo vākyam abravīt ||
translation: Hearing the words of the noble Sugriva, Hanuman, endowed with wisdom, cheerfully replied.
commentary_full: Hanuman listens carefully before responding, showing emotional intelligence and respect. His cheerful yet composed response reflects confidence and readiness to handle the situation wisely. This verse highlights the importance of calm communication and thoughtful response in leadership.
commentary_summary: Hanuman responds wisely and calmly to Sugriva.
theme: Wise response and communication

speaker: Hanuman
text_sanskrit: न भीतुमर्हसे राजन् नायं वै वालिनः प्रियः | लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्राता रामो दशरथात्मजः ||
transliteration: na bhītum arhase rājan nāyaṁ vai vālināḥ priyaḥ | lakṣhmaṇena saha bhrātā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ ||
translation: O King, you need not fear. This is Rama, son of Dasharatha, accompanied by his brother Lakshmana, and he is not an ally of Vali.
commentary_full: Hanuman reassures Sugriva by identifying Rama and clarifying that he is not associated with Vali. This removes Sugriva’s fear and builds trust. Hanuman’s role as a mediator begins here, bridging misunderstanding through clarity.
commentary_summary: Hanuman removes Sugriva’s fear by revealing Rama’s identity.
theme: Building trust through clarity

speaker: Hanuman
text_sanskrit: तौ तु वीरौ महात्मानौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ | सीतायाः मार्गणार्थाय वनमेतदुपागतौ ||
transliteration: tau tu vīrau mahātmānau bhrātarau rāma-lakṣhmaṇau | sītāyāḥ mārgaṇārthāya vanam etad upāgatau ||
translation: These two noble brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, have come to the forest in search of Sita.
commentary_full: Hanuman explains the purpose of Rama’s arrival—searching for Sita. This reveals the emotional depth of Rama’s journey and establishes a shared ground for alliance, as Sugriva also seeks help against Vali.
commentary_summary: Hanuman explains Rama’s mission to find Sita.
theme: Shared purpose

speaker: Hanuman
text_sanskrit: तयोः सहायं कर्तुं त्वं मित्रभावेन वर्तसे | त्वत्सहायेन रामोऽपि वधिष्यति रणे रिपुम् ||
transliteration: tayoḥ sahāyaṁ kartuṁ tvaṁ mitra-bhāvena vartase | tvat-sahāyena rāmo ’pi vadhiṣhyati raṇe ripum ||
translation: You should befriend them and offer your help; with your support, Rama will defeat his enemies.
commentary_full: Hanuman suggests forming an alliance between Rama and Sugriva. This marks the beginning of a strategic partnership based on mutual benefit—Rama helps Sugriva regain his kingdom, and Sugriva helps find Sita.
commentary_summary: Hanuman proposes alliance between Rama and Sugriva.
theme: Strategic friendship

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा हनुमान् तु सुग्रीवस्य हितं वचः | रूपं संत्यज्य विप्रस्य वानरं रूपमास्थितः ||
transliteration: evam uktvā hanumān tu sugrīvasya hitaṁ vachaḥ | rūpaṁ santyajya viprasya vānaraṁ rūpam āsthitaḥ ||
translation: After speaking these beneficial words, Hanuman discarded his Brahmin disguise and assumed his vanara form.
commentary_full: Hanuman reveals his true identity after establishing trust. This shows that strategy and intelligence may require disguise, but honesty must follow once trust is built.
commentary_summary: Hanuman reveals his true form after gaining trust.
theme: Truth after strategy

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महात्मानौ रामलक्ष्मणौ हरीश्वरः | हर्षेण महता युक्तः समीपं प्रत्यपद्यत ||
transliteration: tau tu dṛṣṭvā mahātmānau rāma-lakṣhmaṇau harīśhvaraḥ | harṣheṇa mahatā yuktaḥ samīpaṁ pratyapadyata ||
translation: Seeing Rama and Lakshmana, Sugriva approached them with great joy.
commentary_full: Sugriva’s fear transforms into joy after understanding Rama’s true nature. This shows how knowledge replaces fear and opens the door to meaningful relationships.
commentary_summary: Sugriva approaches Rama with joy after clarity.
theme: From fear to friendship

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: हनुमान् तु ततः शीघ्रं रामं लक्ष्मणमेव च | आहूय सुग्रीवं चापि मिलयामास धर्मवित् ||
transliteration: hanumān tu tataḥ śīghraṁ rāmaṁ lakṣhmaṇam eva cha | āhūya sugrīvaṁ chāpi milayāmāsa dharma-vit ||
translation: Hanuman quickly brought Rama, Lakshmana, and Sugriva together, uniting them wisely.
commentary_full: Hanuman acts as the bridge that unites Rama and Sugriva. His role as a mediator highlights the importance of communication, wisdom, and timing in forming strong alliances.
commentary_summary: Hanuman unites Rama and Sugriva.
theme: Power of connection

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततो रामः प्रसन्नात्मा सुग्रीवेण समागतः | हनूमता समानीय सौहृदं कर्तुमिच्छति ||
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ prasannātmā sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ | hanūmatā samānīya sauhṛdaṁ kartum icchati ||
translation: Then Rama, with a joyful heart, met Sugriva, brought together by Hanuman, and desired to establish friendship.
commentary_full: Rama’s willingness to form friendship reflects his compassionate and diplomatic nature. Even in personal grief, he recognizes the value of alliances. This moment marks the beginning of a divine partnership rooted in mutual trust and shared goals.
commentary_summary: Rama meets Sugriva and initiates friendship.
theme: Beginning of alliance

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सुग्रीवोऽपि महातेजा रामेण सह सङ्गतः | प्रहृष्टमनसः सर्वे वानरा हर्षमाययुः ||
transliteration: sugrīvo ’pi mahā-tejā rāmeṇa saha saṅgataḥ | prahṛiṣhṭa-manasaḥ sarve vānarā harṣham āyayuḥ ||
translation: Sugriva too, filled with great energy, met Rama, and all the vanaras became joyful.
commentary_full: Sugriva’s meeting with Rama brings hope not only to him but also to the entire vanara community. Leadership decisions impact collective morale, and this alliance marks a turning point for Sugriva’s followers.
commentary_summary: Sugriva and vanaras feel joy after meeting Rama.
theme: Collective hope

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: हनुमान् तु ततः प्रीतः अग्निं साक्षिणमास्थितः | रामस्य सुग्रीवस्य च मैत्रीं समुपकल्पयत् ||
transliteration: hanumān tu tataḥ prītaḥ agniṁ sākṣhiṇam āsthitaḥ | rāmasya sugrīvasya cha maitriṁ samupakalpayat ||
translation: Hanuman, pleased, established the friendship between Rama and Sugriva, taking fire as witness.
commentary_full: Fire is considered a sacred witness in Vedic tradition. By invoking Agni, Hanuman ensures that the alliance is not just political but sacred and binding. This emphasizes dharma in relationships.
commentary_summary: Hanuman formalizes their friendship with sacred ritual.
theme: Sacred alliance

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततोऽग्निं प्रदक्षिण्य तौ मित्रत्वं उपागतौ | परस्परं च तौ वीरौ सन्तुष्टौ समलङ्कृतौ ||
transliteration: tato ’gniṁ pradakṣiṇya tau mitratvaṁ upāgatau | parasparaṁ cha tau vīrau santuṣhṭau samalaṅkṛitau ||
translation: After circumambulating the fire, the two heroes entered into friendship and felt mutually satisfied.
commentary_full: Circumambulation of fire signifies commitment and sacred bonding. Rama and Sugriva’s friendship is not temporary but grounded in dharma, ensuring loyalty and trust.
commentary_summary: Rama and Sugriva seal their friendship through ritual.
theme: Commitment and bonding

speaker: Sugriva
text_sanskrit: दुःखितोऽहं महाबाहो वालिना भ्रातृरूपिणा | हृतदारो भयत्रस्तो वनमेतदुपागतः ||
transliteration: duḥkhito ’haṁ mahā-bāho vālinā bhrātṛ-rūpiṇā | hṛita-dāro bhaya-trasto vanam etad upāgataḥ ||
translation: O mighty Rama, I am distressed. My brother Vali has taken my wife, and out of fear, I have come to this forest.
commentary_full: Sugriva shares his suffering openly, which builds emotional trust. Vulnerability in leadership can strengthen alliances when shared with sincerity.
commentary_summary: Sugriva reveals his suffering caused by Vali.
theme: Expression of suffering

speaker: Sugriva
text_sanskrit: स मे भ्राता महाराजो बलवान् अतिदुर्जयः | तेनाहं जीवितं त्यक्त्वा भीतः प्राणान् धराम्यहम् ||
transliteration: sa me bhrātā mahārājo balavān ati-durjayaḥ | tenāhaṁ jīvitaṁ tyaktvā bhītaḥ prāṇān dharāmy aham ||
translation: My brother is extremely powerful and invincible; I live in constant fear because of him.
commentary_full: Sugriva emphasizes Vali’s strength to explain his helplessness. This shows how fear can suppress even capable individuals.
commentary_summary: Sugriva explains Vali’s strength and his fear.
theme: Power imbalance

speaker: Sugriva
text_sanskrit: त्वं तु धर्मज्ञ रामोऽसि सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः | सहायं कुरु मे वीर वालिनं हन्तुमर्हसि ||
transliteration: tvaṁ tu dharma-jña rāmo ’si satya-vākyo dṛiḍha-vrataḥ | sahāyaṁ kuru me vīra vālinam hantum arhasi ||
translation: You are righteous, truthful, and firm in vows. Help me defeat Vali.
commentary_full: Sugriva recognizes Rama’s virtues and seeks his help. Trust is built on recognition of character and righteousness.
commentary_summary: Sugriva seeks Rama’s help based on his dharma.
theme: Appeal for justice

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: करिष्यामि वचस्तव मित्रभावेन ते स्थितः | वालिनं निहनिष्यामि सत्यं एतद् ब्रवीमि ते ||
transliteration: kariṣhyāmi vachas tava mitra-bhāvena te sthitaḥ | vālinam nihaniṣhyāmi satyaṁ etad bravīmi te ||
translation: I will fulfill your request as your friend. I promise to kill Vali.
commentary_full: Rama’s promise reflects his commitment to dharma and friendship. His words are not mere assurance but a vow rooted in righteousness.
commentary_summary: Rama promises to help Sugriva.
theme: Promise and duty

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः | सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतः प्रणनाम कृताञ्जलिः ||
transliteration: śhrutvā tu vachanaṁ tasya rāmasyākliṣhṭa-karmaṇaḥ | sugrīvaḥ paramaprītaḥ praṇanāma kṛitāñjaliḥ ||
translation: Hearing Rama’s words, Sugriva became extremely pleased and bowed with folded hands.
commentary_full: Sugriva expresses gratitude and respect, showing how trust and assurance can transform fear into devotion.
commentary_summary: Sugriva feels gratitude and respect toward Rama.
theme: Gratitude

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एवं तयोः समुत्पन्ना मैत्री धर्मसमन्विता | भविष्यति महाबाहो सीतायाः अन्वेषणे ध्रुवा ||
transliteration: evaṁ tayoḥ samutpannā maitri dharma-samanvitā | bhaviṣhyati mahā-bāho sītāyāḥ anveṣhaṇe dhruvā ||
translation: Thus began their righteous friendship, which would certainly aid in the search for Sita.
commentary_full: This alliance becomes the turning point in the Ramayana. It is not just a friendship but a dharmic partnership that drives the mission forward.
commentary_summary: Rama-Sugriva alliance begins for Sita’s search.
theme: Mission partnership

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः कथयामास सुग्रीवो राममग्रतः | वालिनः सर्वमाख्यानं दुःखितो हृदयेन च ||
transliteration: tataḥ kathayāmāsa sugrīvo rāmam agrataḥ | vālinah sarvam ākhyānaṁ duḥkhito hṛidayena cha ||
translation: Then Sugriva narrated the entire story of Vali to Rama, with a sorrowful heart.
commentary_full: Sugriva openly shares his painful past, showing complete trust in Rama. This transparency strengthens their bond and prepares Rama to take action with full understanding of the situation.
commentary_summary: Sugriva shares his story of suffering with Rama.
theme: Sharing truth

speaker: Sugriva
text_sanskrit: मया तु सह वैरं तत् जातं भ्रातुः दुरात्मनः | राज्यं च हृतमेव अस्मात् भार्या चापि हृता मम ||
transliteration: mayā tu saha vairaṁ tat jātaṁ bhrātuḥ durātmanaḥ | rājyaṁ cha hṛitam evāsmāt bhāryā chāpi hṛitā mama ||
translation: My wicked brother developed enmity with me, took away my kingdom and even my wife.
commentary_full: Sugriva explains the injustice done by Vali. This highlights betrayal within close relationships and sets the moral ground for Rama’s intervention.
commentary_summary: Sugriva describes Vali’s betrayal.
theme: Injustice and betrayal

speaker: Sugriva
text_sanskrit: तस्य मे दुःखमत्यर्थं जीविते नास्ति मे सुखम् | त्वत्सहायेन राम त्वं शत्रुं हन्तुमिहार्हसि ||
transliteration: tasya me duḥkham atyarthaṁ jīvite nāsti me sukham | tvat-sahāyena rāma tvaṁ śhatruṁ hantum ihārhasi ||
translation: I am deeply miserable and find no happiness in life. With your help, Rama, you should destroy my enemy.
commentary_full: Sugriva expresses his complete despair and dependence on Rama. This reflects how faith in a righteous leader can restore hope in difficult times.
commentary_summary: Sugriva seeks Rama’s help to end his suffering.
theme: Seeking justice

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः | रामो धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठः प्रत्युवाच कृताञ्जलिम् ||
transliteration: śhrutvā tu vachanaṁ tasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ | rāmo dharma-bhṛitāṁ śhreṣhṭhaḥ pratyuvācha kṛitāñjalim ||
translation: Hearing Sugriva’s words, Rama, the upholder of dharma, replied respectfully.
commentary_full: Rama listens attentively and responds with compassion and dignity. His leadership reflects patience and understanding before action.
commentary_summary: Rama listens and responds with compassion.
theme: Compassionate leadership

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: सखा त्वं मे महाप्राज्ञ न मे संशयः क्वचित् | करिष्यामि प्रियं तव वालिनं निहनिष्यामि ||
transliteration: sakhā tvaṁ me mahā-prājña na me saṁśhayaḥ kvachit | kariṣhyāmi priyaṁ tava vālinam nihaniṣhyāmi ||
translation: You are my friend, O wise one. I will surely do what is dear to you and kill Vali.
commentary_full: Rama reaffirms his commitment to friendship and justice. His words strengthen Sugriva’s confidence and reflect unwavering integrity.
commentary_summary: Rama promises to fulfill Sugriva’s wish.
theme: Loyalty in friendship

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो हर्षमाययौ | विश्वासं परमं प्राप्तो रामे धर्मभृतां वरे ||
transliteration: tasya tad-vachanaṁ śhrutvā sugrīvo harṣham āyayau | viśhvāsaṁ paramaṁ prāpto rāme dharma-bhṛitāṁ vare ||
translation: Hearing Rama’s words, Sugriva felt great joy and developed complete trust in him.
commentary_full: Rama’s assurance removes Sugriva’s fear entirely. Trust is built when words align with character and intention.
commentary_summary: Sugriva gains complete trust in Rama.
theme: Building trust

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततो रामः सुग्रीवं समाश्वास्य पुनः पुनः | सौहृदं दृढमासाद्य स्थितौ तौ हरिराघवौ ||
transliteration: tato rāmaḥ sugrīvaṁ samāśhvāsya punaḥ punaḥ | sauhṛidaṁ dṛiḍham āsādya sthitau tau hari-rāghavau ||
translation: Rama repeatedly comforted Sugriva, strengthening their friendship.
commentary_full: Reassurance is key in strengthening relationships. Rama’s repeated assurance shows emotional support and commitment.
commentary_summary: Rama strengthens Sugriva’s confidence.
theme: Emotional support

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: लक्ष्मणोऽपि महातेजा रामस्य प्रियकारकः | तयोः सख्यं समासाद्य हर्षेण समनन्दत ||
transliteration: lakṣhmaṇo ’pi mahā-tejā rāmasya priya-kārakaḥ | tayoḥ sakhyaṁ samāsādya harṣheṇa samanandata ||
translation: Lakshmana too rejoiced greatly at the friendship between Rama and Sugriva.
commentary_full: Lakshmana’s joy reflects loyalty and support for Rama’s decisions. A strong support system reinforces leadership.
commentary_summary: Lakshmana feels joy at their alliance.
theme: Supportive companionship

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: हनुमान् अपि धर्मज्ञः तयोः सख्यं सुदुर्लभम् | दृष्ट्वा प्रमुदितो भूत्वा प्रणनाम कृताञ्जलिः ||
transliteration: hanumān api dharma-jñaḥ tayoḥ sakhyaṁ sudurlabham | dṛiṣhṭvā pramudito bhūtvā praṇanāma kṛitāñjaliḥ ||
translation: Hanuman, knower of dharma, rejoiced and bowed seeing their rare friendship.
commentary_full: Hanuman recognizes the divine significance of this alliance. His humility and devotion highlight his greatness.
commentary_summary: Hanuman rejoices at the sacred friendship.
theme: Divine recognition

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एवं सख्यं समुत्पन्नं रामसुग्रीवयोस्तदा | जगतः हितकार्यार्थं भविष्यति न संशयः ||
transliteration: evaṁ sakhyaṁ samutpannaṁ rāma-sugrīvayos tadā | jagataḥ hita-kāryārthaṁ bhaviṣhyati na saṁśhayaḥ ||
translation: Thus was formed the friendship between Rama and Sugriva, which would serve the welfare of the world.
commentary_full: This alliance is not just personal but cosmic in purpose. It leads to the defeat of evil and restoration of dharma.
commentary_summary: Rama-Sugriva alliance serves universal good.
theme: Divine purpose

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्शनः |
इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि ||
transliteration: tato rāvaṇa-nītāyāḥ sītāyāḥ śatrukarśanaḥ | iyeṣa padam anveṣṭuṁ cāraṇācarite pathi ||
translation: Then Hanuman, the destroyer of enemies, decided to search for Sita, who had been abducted by Ravana.
commentary_full: This marks the beginning of Sundara Kanda. Hanuman takes responsibility for the mission to find Sita. His determination reflects courage, devotion, and unwavering focus on dharma.
commentary_summary: Hanuman begins mission to find Sita.
theme: Start of divine mission

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
दुष्करं निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वं चिकीर्षन् कर्म वानरः |
समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवो गवां पतिरिवाभभौ ||
transliteration: duṣkaraṁ niṣpratidvandvaṁ cikīrṣan karma vānaraḥ | samudagra-śiro-grīvo gavāṁ patir ivābabhau ||
translation: The vanara prepared to perform a difficult and unmatched task, appearing like a mighty bull.
commentary_full: Hanuman’s strength and confidence are compared to a powerful bull. This highlights readiness before action and belief in one’s capability.
commentary_summary: Hanuman prepares for a difficult mission.
theme: Preparation for action

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
अथ वैडूर्यवर्णेषु शाद्वलेषु महाबलः |
धीरो विचचार सुखं सलिलकल्पेषु मारुतिः ||
transliteration: atha vaiḍūrya-varṇeṣu śādvaleṣu mahā-balaḥ | dhīro vicacāra sukhaṁ salila-kalpeṣu mārutiḥ ||
translation: The mighty Hanuman walked calmly over grassy lands shining like gems.
commentary_full: Before taking the leap, Hanuman remains calm and composed. This shows inner balance before undertaking great tasks.
commentary_summary: Hanuman stays calm before action.
theme: Inner stability

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: स समुद्रं महावेगो लङ्घयिष्यति मारुतिः |
transliteration: sa samudraṁ mahā-vego laṅghayiṣyati mārutiḥ |
translation: Hanuman prepared to leap across the ocean with great speed.
commentary_full: The ocean symbolizes challenges in life. Hanuman’s leap represents courage to overcome seemingly impossible obstacles.
commentary_summary: Hanuman prepares to cross the ocean.
theme: Overcoming obstacles

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सागरस्य तटे स्थित्वा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः |
transliteration: sāgarasya taṭe sthitvā hanumān mārutātmajaḥ |
translation: Standing at the shore of the ocean, Hanuman gathered his energy.
commentary_full: Before great actions, preparation and focus are essential. Hanuman collects his strength, showing discipline and awareness.
commentary_summary: Hanuman prepares mentally and physically.
theme: Preparation

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: स तु संहर्य मनसा वायुवेगसमन्वितः | बभूव पर्वताकारः क्षणेन हरिसत्तमः ||
transliteration: sa tu saṁharya manasā vāyu-vega-samanvitaḥ | babhūva parvatākāraḥ kṣaṇena hari-sattamaḥ ||
translation: Gathering his mind and energy, Hanuman quickly assumed a gigantic form like a mountain.
commentary_full: Hanuman concentrates his mind and expands his body, symbolizing inner power manifesting outwardly. This verse emphasizes that mental focus is the foundation of great physical achievements.
commentary_summary: Hanuman gathers strength and grows विशाल.
theme: Awakening inner power

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तस्य बृहत्स्वनं घोरं पर्वतस्येव दीर्घतः | निर्घोषमकरोद्भीमं दिशः सर्वाः समाकुलाः ||
transliteration: tasya bṛihat-svanaṁ ghoraṁ parvatasyeva dīrghataḥ | nirghoṣam akarod bhīmaṁ diśaḥ sarvāḥ samākulāḥ ||
translation: A loud and terrifying sound arose from him, like that of a great mountain, shaking all directions.
commentary_full: Hanuman’s expansion generates a powerful sound that echoes through all directions. This symbolizes the impact of true strength—it is felt universally. His presence itself becomes a force of nature.
commentary_summary: Hanuman’s power shakes all directions.
theme: Power manifestation

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: निपेतुश्च ततः वृक्षा वायुना सम्प्रकम्पिताः | गिरयश्च विचुक्रुशुः कम्पिताः सह भूमिना ||
transliteration: nipetuśh cha tataḥ vṛikṣhā vāyunā samprakampitāḥ | girayaśh cha vicukruśhuḥ kampitāḥ saha bhūminā ||
translation: Trees fell and mountains trembled due to the force of Hanuman’s movement.
commentary_full: Nature itself responds to Hanuman’s immense energy. The falling trees and shaking mountains symbolize how great actions create visible transformation in the environment.
commentary_summary: Nature reacts to Hanuman’s शक्ति.
theme: Impact on nature

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सिंहाश्च व्यथिताः सर्वे मृगाश्चैव वनालयाः | पक्षिणः पतिता भूमौ भीता व्याकुलचेतसः ||
transliteration: siṁhāśh cha vyathitāḥ sarve mṛigāśh chaiva vanālayāḥ | pakṣiṇaḥ patitā bhūmau bhītā vyākula-chetasāḥ ||
translation: Lions, animals, and birds became frightened and disturbed, falling to the ground in fear.
commentary_full: The reaction of animals shows the intensity of Hanuman’s power. Fear spreads among weaker beings when faced with overwhelming force, reflecting the natural response to extraordinary events.
commentary_summary: Animals डर जाते हैं Hanuman की शक्ति से.
theme: Effect of शक्ति

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: उत्पपात ततः श्रीमान् हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः | नभः समभिपद्याशु गरुडो वायुसंनिभः ||
transliteration: utpapāta tataḥ śhrīmān hanumān mārutātmajaḥ | nabhaḥ samabhipadyāśhu garuḍo vāyu-sannibhaḥ ||
translation: Then Hanuman, the son of the wind, leapt into the sky like Garuda, moving with great speed.
commentary_full: This is the iconic leap of Hanuman. His flight symbolizes transcending limitations. Like Garuda, he moves with divine speed and purpose, representing courage and faith combined.
commentary_summary: Hanuman takes the महान leap into the sky.
theme: Transcending limits

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: स तु वेगेन महता प्लवमानो महाकपिः | बभौ मेघ इवाकाशे विद्युद्गर्भो महाबलः ||
transliteration: sa tu vegena mahatā plavamāno mahākapiḥ | babhau megha ivākāśe vidyud-garbho mahā-balaḥ ||
translation: Leaping with great speed, the mighty Hanuman shone in the sky like a cloud filled with lightning.
commentary_full: Hanuman’s flight is compared to a thundercloud, symbolizing both power and divine energy. His movement is not just physical but cosmic in significance.
commentary_summary: Hanuman shines like a powerful cloud in the sky.
theme: Divine शक्ति in motion

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तस्य वेगसमुत्क्षिप्तं सलिलं सागरस्य हि | अभवन्मेघसंकाशं पतद्गिरिशिलोपमम् ||
transliteration: tasya vega-samutkṣhiptaṁ salilaṁ sāgarasya hi | abhavan megha-saṅkāśaṁ patad-giri-śilopamam ||
translation: The ocean water, thrown up by his speed, appeared like clouds and falling mountains.
commentary_full: Hanuman’s गति is so immense that it disturbs the ocean. This reflects how great effort influences even vast systems.
commentary_summary: Ocean reacts to Hanuman’s गति.
theme: Impact of effort

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: उद्गतानि च तोयानि तस्य वेगेन मारुतेः | अम्बरं समलङ्कुर्वन् मेघानिव महाबलः ||
transliteration: udgatāni cha toyāni tasya vegena māruteḥ | ambaraṁ samalaṅkurvan meghān iva mahā-balaḥ ||
translation: Water rose into the sky due to his speed, decorating it like clouds.
commentary_full: The imagery shows transformation—Hanuman turns the ocean into sky-like clouds. It symbolizes converting challenges into opportunities.
commentary_summary: Hanuman transforms surroundings with शक्ति.
theme: Transformation through effort

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: दृश्यन्ते विविधाकाराः सागरस्य तले स्थिताḥ | जलचराः महाकायाः तेन वेगेन चोद्धृताः ||
transliteration: dṛiśhyante vividhākārāḥ sāgarasya tale sthitāḥ | jalacharāḥ mahākāyāḥ tena vegena choddhṛitāḥ ||
translation: Various sea creatures were lifted and became visible due to his speed.
commentary_full: Hidden elements emerge under powerful force. This represents how intense action reveals hidden truths.
commentary_summary: Hidden things become visible due to शक्ति.
theme: Revealing truth

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तं दृष्ट्वा देवगन्धर्वा सिद्धचारणसङ्घशः | विस्मयं परमं जग्मुः हनुमन्तं प्लवङ्गमम् ||
transliteration: taṁ dṛiṣhṭvā deva-gandharvā siddha-chāraṇa-saṅghaśhaḥ | vismayaṁ paramaṁ jagmuḥ hanumantaṁ plavaṅgamam ||
translation: Gods, Gandharvas, and celestial beings were amazed seeing Hanuman.
commentary_full: Hanuman’s act is so महान that even divine beings admire him. True greatness earns universal respect.
commentary_summary: Even gods admire Hanuman’s शक्ति.
theme: Recognition of greatness

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तं पर्वतरुहः श्रीमान् मैनेकः प्रत्युपस्थितः | विश्रान्तिं ते ददाम्यद्य इति वाक्यमुवाच ह ||
transliteration: taṁ parvata-ruhaḥ śhrīmān mainakaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ | viśhrāntiṁ te dadāmy adya iti vākyam uvācha ha ||
translation: The golden mountain Mainaka appeared and offered Hanuman rest.
commentary_full: Mainaka represents support offered during a journey. Even in difficult missions, help appears, but one must decide whether to accept it.
commentary_summary: Mainaka offers help to Hanuman.
theme: Help on the path

speaker: Hanuman
text_sanskrit: नाहं विश्रामहेतुं त्वां स्प्रष्टुमिच्छामि पर्वत | कार्यं हि महदस्त्यद्य गन्तव्यं शीघ्रमेव मे ||
transliteration: nāhaṁ viśhrāma-hetuṁ tvāṁ spraṣhṭum icchāmi parvata | kāryaṁ hi mahad asty adya gantavyaṁ śhīghram eva me ||
translation: I cannot rest now; I have an important task to complete quickly.
commentary_full: Hanuman respectfully declines rest, showing focus and discipline. This teaches prioritizing duty over comfort.
commentary_summary: Hanuman stays focused on mission.
theme: Commitment to goal

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा स महावेगो गच्छत्येव नभस्तलम् | मैनेकः पूजितस्तेन पुनः स्वस्थानमागमत् ||
transliteration: ity uktvā sa mahā-vego gacchaty eva nabhas-talam | mainakaḥ pūjitas tena punaḥ sva-sthānam āgamat ||
translation: After honoring Mainaka, Hanuman continued his journey, and the mountain returned.
commentary_full: Hanuman balances humility and determination—he respects help but continues his mission.
commentary_summary: Hanuman respects but continues journey.
theme: Balance of respect and duty

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः सुरसा नाम नागमाता समुत्थिता | मार्गे हनुमतः स्थिता तमुवाच महाबलम् ||
transliteration: tataḥ surasā nāma nāga-mātā samutthitā | mārge hanumataḥ sthitā tam uvācha mahā-balam ||
translation: Then Surasa, mother of serpents, appeared in his path and spoke to him.
commentary_full: Surasa represents divine testing. Challenges often come to test readiness, not to stop progress.
commentary_summary: Surasa appears as a test.
theme: Divine testing

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तां दृष्ट्वा हनुमान् धीमान् बुद्ध्या युक्तः समाधानम् | लीलया प्रविवेशास्याः वक्त्रं निर्गत्य च पुनः ||
transliteration: tāṁ dṛiṣhṭvā hanumān dhīmān buddhyā yuktaḥ samādhānam | līlayā praviveśāsyāḥ vaktraṁ nirgaty cha punaḥ ||
translation: Hanuman cleverly entered Surasa’s mouth and came out, solving the challenge with intelligence.
commentary_full: Hanuman uses बुद्धि instead of force. Intelligence is often more powerful than strength.
commentary_summary: Hanuman uses intelligence to pass the test.
theme: Wisdom over force

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः सिंहिका नाम राक्षसी कामरूपिणी | छायाग्राहिणी तं वीरं आकाशे समपद्यत ||
transliteration: tataḥ siṁhikā nāma rākṣhasī kāma-rūpiṇī | chāyā-grāhiṇī taṁ vīraṁ ākāśe samapadyata ||
translation: Then a demoness named Simhika, capable of changing forms and seizing shadows, confronted Hanuman in the sky.
commentary_full: Simhika represents hidden obstacles that attack indirectly—like doubts or negativity. She captures shadows, symbolizing how unseen weaknesses can hinder progress.
commentary_summary: Simhika appears as a hidden obstacle.
theme: Hidden challenges

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सा तु छायां समाकृष्य हनूमन्तं महाबलम् | आकाशात् पातयामास ततो युद्धमुपस्थितम् ||
transliteration: sā tu chāyāṁ samākṛiṣhya hanūmantaṁ mahā-balam | ākāśāt pātayāmāsa tato yuddham upasthitam ||
translation: She seized Hanuman’s shadow and tried to pull him down, leading to a confrontation.
commentary_full: The pulling of shadow signifies attempts to weaken confidence. Hanuman must confront this internal and external obstacle directly.
commentary_summary: Simhika attacks Hanuman by पकड़ shadow.
theme: Facing obstacles

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तां दृष्ट्वा हनुमान् धीरः बुद्धिमान् समुपस्थितः | विवृद्धं रूपमास्थाय तस्या मुखमुपागमत् ||
transliteration: tāṁ dṛiṣhṭvā hanumān dhīraḥ buddhimān samupasthitaḥ | vivṛiddhaṁ rūpam āsthāya tasyā mukham upāgamat ||
translation: Seeing her, the wise Hanuman enlarged his form and approached her mouth.
commentary_full: Hanuman adapts strategy based on situation. Growth (expansion) represents rising above challenges instead of avoiding them.
commentary_summary: Hanuman expands to face Simhika.
theme: Adaptive strategy

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तस्याः कण्ठं समुत्पत्य भित्त्वा हृदयमात्मनः | निःसृत्य स पुनर्वेगात् आकाशे समपद्यत ||
transliteration: tasyāḥ kaṇṭhaṁ samutpatya bhittvā hṛidayam ātmanaḥ | niḥsṛitya sa punar vegāt ākāśe samapadyata ||
translation: Entering her body, Hanuman destroyed her heart and emerged again into the sky.
commentary_full: Hanuman eliminates the obstacle completely. This shows that some challenges must be removed at the root rather than avoided.
commentary_summary: Hanuman destroys Simhika completely.
theme: Eliminating obstacles

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः सिद्धाश्च चारणाः हनूमन्तं प्रशंसितुम् | दृष्ट्वा तस्य पराक्रमं हर्षमाययुः ||
transliteration: tataḥ siddhāśh cha chāraṇāḥ hanūmantaṁ praśhaṁsitum | dṛiṣhṭvā tasya parākramaṁ harṣham āyayuḥ ||
translation: Seeing his valor, celestial beings praised Hanuman with joy.
commentary_full: Success achieved through courage earns recognition. Divine approval symbolizes alignment with dharma.
commentary_summary: Hanuman is praised by celestial beings.
theme: Recognition of courage

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: स तु वेगेन महता लङ्कां दृष्ट्वा महाबलः | चिन्तयामास बुद्ध्या तु प्रवेष्टुं नगरं शुभम् ||
transliteration: sa tu vegena mahatā laṅkāṁ dṛiṣhṭvā mahā-balaḥ | chintayāmāsa buddhyā tu praveṣhṭuṁ nagaraṁ śhubham ||
translation: Seeing Lanka, Hanuman thought carefully about how to enter the city.
commentary_full: Before action, Hanuman uses बुद्धि. Planning is as important as strength.
commentary_summary: Hanuman plans entry into Lanka.
theme: Strategic thinking

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: स लघुरूपधारी तु निशि लङ्कां प्रविष्टवान् | न दृष्टो राक्षसैः कैश्चित् यथाच्छन्नः शुभेक्षणः ||
transliteration: sa laghu-rūpa-dhārī tu niśi laṅkāṁ praviṣhṭavān | na dṛiṣhṭo rākṣhasaiḥ kaiśhchit yathā chhannaḥ śubhekṣhaṇaḥ ||
translation: Taking a small form, Hanuman entered Lanka at night unnoticed by the demons.
commentary_full: Adaptability is key. Hanuman changes form based on need, showing intelligence over brute force.
commentary_summary: Hanuman enters Lanka in small form.
theme: Smart execution

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सा पुरी लङ्का रम्या स्वर्णप्राकारशोभिता | दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमापन्नो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः ||
transliteration: sā purī laṅkā ramyā svarṇa-prākāra-śobhitā | dṛiṣhṭvā vismayam āpanno hanumān mārutātmajaḥ ||
translation: Hanuman saw the beautiful city of Lanka, shining with golden walls, and was amazed.
commentary_full: Even enemies may possess beauty and grandeur. Hanuman observes without distraction, staying focused on mission.
commentary_summary: Hanuman observes Lanka’s beauty.
theme: Observation

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: रात्रौ तु विचरन् धीमान् हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः | निरीक्षते पुरीं सर्वां सीतां चान्वेषते कपिः ||
transliteration: rātrau tu vicharan dhīmān hanumān mārutātmajaḥ | nirīkṣhate purīṁ sarvāṁ sītāṁ chānveṣhate kapiḥ ||
translation: Moving through the city at night, Hanuman carefully observed everything while searching for Sita.
commentary_full: Patience and observation are key in missions. Hanuman does not rush but analyzes surroundings.
commentary_summary: Hanuman searches carefully in Lanka.
theme: Focused search

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एवं स कपिशार्दूलो लङ्कायां विचरन् निशि | सीतायाः दर्शनार्थाय प्रयत्नं परमं कृतः ||
transliteration: evaṁ sa kapi-śhārdūlo laṅkāyāṁ vicharan niśi | sītāyāḥ darśhanārthāya prayatnaṁ paramaṁ kṛitaḥ ||
translation: Thus Hanuman, moving through Lanka at night, made his greatest effort to find Sita.
commentary_full: This verse concludes the initial mission phase. Hanuman’s unwavering dedication symbolizes persistence and devotion in achieving goals.
commentary_summary: Hanuman continues mission with full effort.
theme: Perseverance

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः कपिमुख्येन हनूमता महात्मना | सीताया दर्शनं श्रुत्वा रामो हर्षमवाप्तवान् ||
transliteration: tataḥ kapi-mukhyena hanūmatā mahātmanā | sītāyā darśhanaṁ śhrutvā rāmo harṣham avāptavān ||
translation: Hearing from the noble Hanuman about Sita’s sighting, Rama became filled with joy.
commentary_full: This verse marks the emotional turning point. Rama, who was in deep sorrow, finally receives confirmation that Sita is alive. Hanuman becomes the bridge between despair and hope.
commentary_summary: Rama feels joy after hearing about Sita.
theme: Hope after despair

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य हनूमतः महात्मनः | प्रहृष्टो राघवो वाक्यमुवाच मधुरं तदा ||
transliteration: śhrutvā tu vachanaṁ tasya hanūmataḥ mahātmanaḥ | prahṛiṣhṭo rāghavo vākyam uvācha madhuraṁ tadā ||
translation: Hearing Hanuman’s words, Rama joyfully spoke sweet words.
commentary_full: Rama expresses gratitude and happiness. This reflects how good news changes emotional state instantly.
commentary_summary: Rama responds happily.
theme: Expression of joy

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: न हि मे प्रियतरं किंचित् हनूमान् त्वत्समं कपे |
transliteration: na hi me priyataraṁ kiñchit hanūmān tvat-samaṁ kape |
translation: O Hanuman, nothing is dearer to me than you.
commentary_full: Rama acknowledges Hanuman’s devotion and service. This shows that true service earns the highest recognition.
commentary_summary: Rama praises Hanuman.
theme: Recognition of devotion

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: कृतं कार्यं महद् वीर त्वया हनुमता शुभम् |
transliteration: kṛitaṁ kāryaṁ mahad vīra tvayā hanumatā śhubham |
translation: O brave Hanuman, you have accomplished a great task.
commentary_full: Rama highlights the importance of Hanuman’s mission. It was not just a task, but a turning point in the war.
commentary_summary: Hanuman’s work is appreciated.
theme: Achievement

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः परिष्वज्य हनूमन्तं रामो वचनमब्रवीत् |
transliteration: tataḥ pariṣhvajya hanūmantaṁ rāmo vachanam abravīt |
translation: Then Rama embraced Hanuman and spoke to him.
commentary_full: The embrace symbolizes divine appreciation. Physical gestures often express emotions more deeply than words.
commentary_summary: Rama hugs Hanuman.
theme: Emotional connection

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एष मे जीवितस्यार्थः सिद्धः कपिवर त्वया |
transliteration: eṣha me jīvitasya arthaḥ siddhaḥ kapi-vara tvayā |
translation: O best of vanaras, my life’s purpose has been fulfilled by you.
commentary_full: Rama equates Hanuman’s success with his life’s purpose. This shows the depth of Sita’s importance.
commentary_summary: Hanuman fulfills Rama’s purpose.
theme: Fulfillment

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततो लक्ष्मणसुग्रीवौ हर्षं जग्मतुरुत्तमम् |
transliteration: tato lakṣhmaṇa-sugrīvau harṣhaṁ jagmatur uttamam |
translation: Lakshmana and Sugriva also felt immense joy.
commentary_full: Joy spreads collectively. When the leader is happy, the entire group feels uplifted.
commentary_summary: Lakshmana and Sugriva rejoice.
theme: Shared happiness

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सुग्रीवोऽपि हरिश्रेष्ठः हृष्टः वचनमब्रवीत् |
transliteration: sugrīvo ’pi hari-śhreṣhṭhaḥ hṛiṣhṭaḥ vachanam abravīt |
translation: Sugriva, delighted, also spoke words of joy.
commentary_full: Sugriva’s reaction reflects strong leadership alignment with Rama’s mission.
commentary_summary: Sugriva expresses happiness.
theme: Supportive leadership

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सर्वे वानरमुख्याश्च हर्षं परममागताः |
transliteration: sarve vānar-mukhyāśh cha harṣhaṁ paramam āgatāḥ |
translation: All the vanara leaders were filled with great joy.
commentary_full: Collective morale rises when success is achieved. Hanuman’s success inspires the entire army.
commentary_summary: Vanara army rejoices.
theme: Collective morale

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः रामो महातेजाः चिन्तयामास राघवः | लङ्कां प्रति गमनाय उपायं मनसा शुभम् ||
transliteration: tataḥ rāmo mahā-tejāḥ chintayāmāsa rāghavaḥ | laṅkāṁ prati gamanāya upāyaṁ manasā śhubham ||
translation: Then Rama began to think about how to proceed towards Lanka.
commentary_full: After joy comes action. Rama shifts focus from emotion to strategy, marking the beginning of the war phase.
commentary_summary: Rama plans next step towards Lanka.
theme: Transition to action

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: कथं नु खलु लङ्कां तां दुर्गां राक्षससेविताम् | प्राप्स्यामो वानरैः सार्धं सीतां द्रष्टुं प्रियामहम् ||
transliteration: kathaṁ nu khalu laṅkāṁ tāṁ durgāṁ rākṣhasa-sevitām | prāpsyāmo vānaraiḥ sārdhaṁ sītāṁ draṣhṭuṁ priyām aham ||
translation: How shall we reach Lanka, which is well-fortified and filled with demons, so that I may see my beloved Sita?
commentary_full: Rama begins strategic thinking. Despite his strength, he carefully considers the challenge ahead. This shows that even great leaders rely on planning before action.
commentary_summary: Rama questions how to reach Lanka.
theme: Strategic thinking

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: सागरश्च महावेगः कथं लङ्घ्यः प्लवङ्गमैः | इति चिन्तापरो रामो बभूव मनुजर्षभः ||
transliteration: sāgaraśh cha mahā-vegaḥ kathaṁ laṅghyaḥ plavaṅgamaiḥ | iti chintā-paro rāmo babhūva manujarṣhabhaḥ ||
translation: How can this vast ocean be crossed by the vanaras? Thinking thus, Rama became deeply contemplative.
commentary_full: The ocean represents a major obstacle. Rama acknowledges the difficulty rather than ignoring it. Recognizing challenges is the first step toward solving them.
commentary_summary: Rama worries about crossing the ocean.
theme: Recognizing obstacles

speaker: Sugriva
text_sanskrit: मा चिन्तां कुरु राम त्वं लङ्घयिष्यामहे वयम् | न हि ते कपयो हीनाः विक्रमेण बलान्विताः ||
transliteration: mā chintāṁ kuru rāma tvaṁ laṅghayiṣhyāmahe vayam | na hi te kapayo hīnāḥ vikrameṇa balānvitāḥ ||
translation: Do not worry, O Rama. We will cross the ocean; the vanaras are strong and capable.
commentary_full: Sugriva boosts Rama’s confidence. A good leader not only plans but also motivates others during uncertainty.
commentary_summary: Sugriva reassures Rama.
theme: Motivation

speaker: Sugriva
text_sanskrit: महाबलाः प्लवङ्गास्ते सर्वे युद्धविशारदाः | तेषां नास्ति परं कार्यं यत् न सिद्ध्यति राघव ||
transliteration: mahā-balāḥ plavaṅgās te sarve yuddha-viśhāradāḥ | teṣhāṁ nāsti paraṁ kāryaṁ yat na siddhyati rāghava ||
translation: These vanaras are mighty and skilled in battle; nothing is impossible for them.
commentary_full: Sugriva emphasizes the capability of his army. Belief in team strength is essential for success.
commentary_summary: Vanaras are capable of great feats.
theme: Team strength

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवो रामं समभिपूजयत् | वानराणां च सर्वेषां उत्साहं समवर्धयत् ||
transliteration: evam uktvā tu sugrīvo rāmaṁ samabhipūjayat | vānarāṇāṁ cha sarveṣhāṁ utsāhaṁ samavardhayat ||
translation: Having spoken thus, Sugriva honored Rama and encouraged all the vanaras.
commentary_full: Sugriva plays a dual role—respecting Rama and motivating his army. Leadership requires balancing humility and inspiration.
commentary_summary: Sugriva motivates the army.
theme: Leadership

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः प्लवङ्गमा सर्वे हृष्टाः परमवीर्यवन्तः | सिंहनादं प्रचक्रुस्ते युद्धाय समुपस्थिताः ||
transliteration: tataḥ plavaṅgamā sarve hṛiṣhṭāḥ parama-vīryavantaḥ | siṁha-nādaṁ prachakrus te yuddhāya samupasthitāḥ ||
translation: Then all the vanaras, filled with joy and strength, roared like lions, ready for battle.
commentary_full: The army’s enthusiasm reflects collective confidence. Energy and unity are powerful forces in achieving goals.
commentary_summary: Vanaras roar with enthusiasm.
theme: Collective energy

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: रामोऽपि तान् समालोक्य हृष्टो वानरसत्तमान् | लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्राता चिन्तयामास तद्गतम् ||
transliteration: rāmo ’pi tān samālokya hṛiṣhṭo vānarasattamān | lakṣhmaṇena saha bhrātā chintayāmāsa tad-gatam ||
translation: Rama, seeing the enthusiastic vanaras, felt encouraged and discussed the plan with Lakshmana.
commentary_full: Rama gains confidence from his team and begins planning collaboratively. Leadership thrives on teamwork.
commentary_summary: Rama discusses strategy with Lakshmana.
theme: Collaborative planning

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सागरं प्रति गन्तव्यं इति निश्चयमास्थितः | रामो युद्धाय सज्जोऽभूत् लङ्कां प्रति दृढव्रतः ||
transliteration: sāgaraṁ prati gantavyaṁ iti niśhchayam āsthitaḥ | rāmo yuddhāya sajjo ’bhūt laṅkāṁ prati dṛiḍha-vrataḥ ||
translation: Rama resolved to approach the ocean and prepared firmly for the war against Lanka.
commentary_full: Decision-making is crucial. Once a leader decides, clarity replaces doubt.
commentary_summary: Rama decides to proceed towards ocean.
theme: Decisive action

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ते सर्वे हरिशार्दूलाः रामस्याज्ञां प्रतीक्ष्यते | लङ्कायाः अभिगमनाय सज्जाः संन्यवर्तन्त ||
transliteration: te sarve hari-śhārdūlāḥ rāmasyājñāṁ pratīkṣhyate | laṅkāyāḥ abhigamanāya sajjāḥ saṁnyavartanta ||
translation: All the vanaras awaited Rama’s command, ready to march toward Lanka.
commentary_full: Discipline in the army reflects respect for leadership. Timing and coordination are key in execution.
commentary_summary: Vanaras wait for Rama’s command.
theme: Readiness

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एवं तेषां महान् उत्साहः समुत्पन्नो महाबलः | लङ्कायाः अभिगमनाय सर्वेषां दृढनिश्चयः ||
transliteration: evaṁ teṣhāṁ mahān utsāhaḥ samutpanno mahā-balaḥ | laṅkāyāḥ abhigamanāya sarveṣhāṁ dṛiḍha-niśhchayaḥ ||
translation: Thus, great enthusiasm and firm determination arose among them to proceed toward Lanka.
commentary_full: The army reaches peak motivation. Collective determination becomes unstoppable force.
commentary_summary: Army gains strong determination.
theme: Collective determination

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः कपिवराः सर्वे रामस्याज्ञां प्रचक्षिरे | गन्तुं लङ्कां महासत्त्वाः उत्साहं समुपागताः ||
transliteration: tataḥ kapi-varāḥ sarve rāmasyājñāṁ prachakṣhire | gantuṁ laṅkāṁ mahā-sattvāḥ utsāhaṁ samupāgatāḥ ||
translation: Then all the great vanaras, filled with enthusiasm, awaited Rama’s command to proceed to Lanka.
commentary_full: The vanara army stands united and ready. Their discipline and readiness highlight the importance of organized effort in achieving great missions.
commentary_summary: Vanaras ready for Rama’s command.
theme: Preparedness

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: रामोऽपि महातेजाः दृष्ट्वा तेषां पराक्रमम् | प्रहृष्टो वचनं प्राह वानराणां हितं तदा ||
transliteration: rāmo ’pi mahā-tejāḥ dṛiṣhṭvā teṣhāṁ parākramam | prahṛiṣhṭo vachanaṁ prāha vānarāṇāṁ hitaṁ tadā ||
translation: Rama, seeing their valor, spoke words of encouragement to the vanaras.
commentary_full: Rama inspires his army with motivating words. Leadership involves recognizing and encouraging team strength.
commentary_summary: Rama encourages the army.
theme: Motivation

speaker: Rama
text_sanskrit: गच्छामः शीघ्रमेवैतत् सागरं वानरैः सह | तत्र उपायं विचार्यैव लङ्कां गन्तुं प्रयास्यते ||
transliteration: gacchāmaḥ śhīghram evaitat sāgaraṁ vānaraiḥ saha | tatra upāyaṁ vichāryaiva laṅkāṁ gantuṁ prayāsyate ||
translation: Let us quickly proceed to the ocean with the vanaras and decide how to reach Lanka.
commentary_full: Rama moves from planning to execution. He emphasizes teamwork and strategic thinking before action.
commentary_summary: Rama decides to move towards ocean.
theme: Action planning

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः सर्वे समुत्साहाः कपयो रामचोदिताः | प्रस्थिताः सागरं प्रति लङ्कायाः अभिगमनाय ||
transliteration: tataḥ sarve samutsāhāḥ kapayo rāma-choditāḥ | prasthitāḥ sāgaraṁ prati laṅkāyāḥ abhigamanāya ||
translation: Encouraged by Rama, all the vanaras set out toward the ocean to reach Lanka.
commentary_full: Once leadership gives direction, collective movement begins. Unity and shared purpose drive progress.
commentary_summary: Vanaras march towards ocean.
theme: Collective action

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: तेषां निनादो महानासीद् गगनं समपूरयन् | पर्वताः कम्पिताः सर्वे भूमिश्चापि प्रचालिताः ||
transliteration: teṣhāṁ ninādo mahān āsīd gaganaṁ samapūrayān | parvatāḥ kampitāḥ sarve bhūmiśh chāpi prachālitāḥ ||
translation: Their loud roar filled the sky, shaking mountains and the earth.
commentary_full: The energy of the united army becomes a powerful force. Collective enthusiasm creates massive impact.
commentary_summary: Army’s roar shakes nature.
theme: Power of unity

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: गच्छन्तो वानराः सर्वे वेगेन महता युताः | द्रुतं सागरतीरं ते जग्मुः रामपुरःसराः ||
transliteration: gacchanto vānarāḥ sarve vegena mahatā yutāḥ | drutaṁ sāgara-tīraṁ te jagmuḥ rāma-puraḥsarāḥ ||
translation: The vanaras, moving swiftly, reached the seashore with Rama leading them.
commentary_full: Rama leads from the front, showing ideal leadership. The army follows with trust and speed.
commentary_summary: Army reaches ocean under Rama’s leadership.
theme: Leading from front

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: सागरं तु समासाद्य रामो वानरसत्तमः | ददर्श विस्तीर्णतरं जलराशिं भयावहम् ||
transliteration: sāgaraṁ tu samāsādya rāmo vānarasattamaḥ | dadarśha vistīrṇa-taraṁ jala-rāśhiṁ bhayāvaham ||
translation: Reaching the ocean, Rama saw its vast and भयावह expanse.
commentary_full: The ocean represents the final barrier. Even great leaders face intimidating challenges.
commentary_summary: Rama observes vast ocean.
theme: Facing reality

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: ततः सागरमासाद्य रामः चिन्तापरोऽभवत् | उपायं चिन्तयामास कथं लङ्कां गमिष्यति ||
transliteration: tataḥ sāgaram āsādya rāmaḥ chintā-paro ’bhavat | upāyaṁ chintayāmāsa kathaṁ laṅkāṁ gamiṣhyati ||
translation: Reaching the ocean, Rama again thought deeply about how to cross it.
commentary_full: Even after reaching the goal’s boundary, planning continues. Success requires continuous thinking and adaptation.
commentary_summary: Rama thinks about crossing ocean.
theme: Continuous strategy

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: लक्ष्मणः सह रामेण सुग्रीवश्च महाबलः | समासीनाः समुद्रस्य तटे मन्त्रं समाचरन् ||
transliteration: lakṣhmaṇaḥ saha rāmeṇa sugrīvaśh cha mahā-balaḥ | samāsīnāḥ samudrasya taṭe mantraṁ samācharan ||
translation: Rama, Lakshmana, and Sugriva sat together near the ocean, discussing strategy.
commentary_full: Collaboration and discussion lead to better decisions. Great leaders consult before acting.
commentary_summary: Leaders discuss plan together.
theme: Strategic discussion

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit: एवं तु मन्त्रयामासुः लङ्कायाः अभिगमनम् | रामलक्ष्मणसुग्रीवा वानरैः सह संयुताः ||
transliteration: evaṁ tu mantrayāmāsuḥ laṅkāyāḥ abhigamanam | rāma-lakṣhmaṇa-sugrīvā vānaraiḥ saha saṁyutāḥ ||
translation: Thus Rama, Lakshmana, and Sugriva, along with the vanaras, discussed how to reach Lanka.
commentary_full: This verse concludes the preparation phase. Strategy, unity, and determination set the stage for the महान युद्ध ahead.
commentary_summary: Team plans Lanka mission.
theme: Preparation for war

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
गच्छता मातुलकुलं भरतेन तदाऽनघः |
शत्रुघ्नो नित्यशत्रुघ्नो नीतः प्रीतिपुरस्कृतः || २-१-१
transliteration:
gacchatā mātulakulaṃ bharatena tadā.anaghaḥ |
śatrughno nityaśatrughno nītaḥ prītipuraskṛtaḥ || 2-1-1
translation: Bharata, while going to his maternal uncle's house, took along with him his brother Satrughna — he who has no sins and who always vanquishes his enemies — with great love.
commentary_full: The first sarga of Ayodhya Kanda opens not with Rama but with Bharata and Satrughna's absence from Ayodhya — a narrative device that explains why the two younger brothers were away when the critical events unfolded. Bharata had gone to the kingdom of his maternal grandfather Ashvapati, king of Kekaya. This sarga is primarily devoted to a magnificent enumeration of Rama's virtues — physical, intellectual, moral, and administrative — establishing him as the ideal prince deserving of coronation. Dasaratha observes signs of aging in himself, the appearance of comets, and other ill omens in the sky, prompting him to accelerate his plan to crown Rama as Yuvaraja. He convenes an assembly of kings, ministers, and citizens from across the realm (notably excluding Janaka and the Kekaya king, as they would hear the good news later). The assembly unanimously endorses Rama's coronation. The sarga thus sets up the joyful anticipation that will be cruelly overturned in subsequent chapters.
commentary_summary: Rama's virtues are extolled as Dasaratha plans his coronation, convening a grand assembly that joyfully endorses Rama as crown prince.
theme: The ideal prince and the joyful preparations for his coronation

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
दुन्दुभिस्वनकल्पेन गम्भीरेणानुनादिना |
स्वरेण महता राजा जीमूत इव नादयन् || २-२-२
transliteration:
dundhubhisvanakalpena gambhīreṇānunādinā |
svareṇa mahatā rājā jīmūta iva nādayan || 2-2-2
translation: In a loud voice resembling that of a kettle-drum, resounding the air like a thundering cloud, King Dasaratha addressed the gathered assembly.
commentary_full: In this sarga, Dasaratha addresses the assembled kings and citizens in his great hall with a voice deep as a kettledrum. He expresses his long-held desire to see Rama crowned as Yuvaraja (crown prince) before his own strength diminishes with old age. He speaks of Rama's unparalleled virtues and asks for the assembly's approval. The assembled kings, brahmanas, and citizens respond with enthusiastic approval, comparing their delight to that of peacocks welcoming rain clouds. They describe Rama's qualities — his wisdom, valor, truth, compassion — and declare him supremely worthy of the throne. The assembly's unanimous joy fills the air and causes the very walls of the hall to tremble. Vasishtha, the royal preceptor, is then dispatched to summon Rama.
commentary_summary: Dasaratha announces his desire to crown Rama as Yuvaraja before the grand assembly, which unanimously and joyfully endorses the plan.
theme: The unanimous approval of Rama's coronation by people, kings, and sages

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
वसिष्ठस्तु ततः श्रुत्वा राजो वचनमादृतः |
प्रेषयामास रामाय दूतान् शीघ्रजवान् हयान् || २-३-१
transliteration:
vasiṣṭhastu tataḥ śrutvā rājño vacanam ādṛtaḥ |
preṣayāmāsa rāmāya dūtān śīghrajavān hayān || 2-3-1
translation: Vasishtha, hearing the king's command respectfully, sent swift messengers on fleet horses to bring Rama.
commentary_full: Sage Vasishtha, acting on Dasaratha's command, sends fleet-footed messengers to summon Rama from his own palace. The messengers find Rama and bring him joyfully. This sarga also describes Vasishtha giving instructions to have the city of Ayodhya decorated for the coronation — the streets are swept and sprinkled, banners and flags are hoisted, fragrant flowers are strewn, and oil lamps are lit everywhere. The city is filled with festive joy. Rama arrives and pays his respects to Vasishtha. The sage then informs Rama of his father's wish to crown him as Yuvaraja the very next day, on the auspicious Pushyami asterism. Rama is instructed to fast through the night with Sita in preparation for the sacred ceremony.
commentary_summary: Vasishtha summons Rama and prepares Ayodhya for the coronation, instructing Rama to fast overnight with Sita before the sacred ceremony at dawn.
theme: Sacred preparations and divine auspiciousness on the eve of Rama's coronation

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
श्रुत्वा राजो वचः प्रीतः सुमन्त्रः त्वरितो ययौ |
रामस्याभिमुखः श्रीमान् विनयात् प्रणतोऽभवत् || २-४-१
transliteration:
śrutvā rājño vacaḥ prītaḥ sumantraḥ tvarito yayau |
rāmasyābhimukhaḥ śrīmān vinayāt praṇato'bhavat || 2-4-1
translation: Sumantra, delighted on hearing the king's command, went swiftly and stood before the glorious Rama, bowing in humility.
commentary_full: Sumantra, the royal minister and charioteer, is sent to bring Rama before Dasaratha. He finds Rama at his palace and describes the splendid scene: Rama's doorway is thronged with attendants, and the prince is surrounded by devoted citizens who love him. Sumantra conveys the king's wish, and Rama immediately prepares to go. This sarga contains a tender description of how the citizens of Ayodhya feel about Rama — they regard him as their very own spirit (prāṇa) moving outside. When Rama mounts his chariot and rides through the streets, the people gaze at him with eyes full of love and blessings. Rama arrives at Dasaratha's palace and stands before his father. The sarga establishes the extraordinary bond between Rama and the people of Ayodhya.
commentary_summary: Sumantra brings Rama to Dasaratha; the citizens gaze lovingly at Rama as he rides through Ayodhya, revealing the depth of the people's adoration for him.
theme: The beloved prince as the living soul of his people

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
रामं दशरथो राजा पूजयामास धार्मिकः |
पुत्रं ज्येष्ठं महाप्राज्ञमाशीर्भिरभिनन्द्य च || २-५-१
transliteration:
rāmaṃ daśaratho rājā pūjayāmāsa dhārmikaḥ |
putraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ mahāprājñam āśīrbhirabhinadya ca || 2-5-1
translation: The righteous king Dasaratha honored Rama, his eldest son of great wisdom, with blessings and words of affection.
commentary_full: In this emotional sarga, Dasaratha formally communicates to Rama his intention to crown him as Yuvaraja. He speaks to Rama privately, with deep paternal love and a sense of urgency, citing the omens of old age and the ominous portents in the sky. He counsels Rama about the duties of a crown prince — to be humble, disciplined, and ever mindful of the people's welfare. Dasaratha asks Rama to spend the night fasting with Sita in pure devotion. Rama accepts his father's words with complete and joyful submission. He then immediately goes to inform his mother Kausalya and the sage Vasishtha. Kausalya, moved by joy, blesses Rama lovingly. The sarga is a portrait of ideal familial love and dharmic transmission from father to son.
commentary_summary: Dasaratha privately tells Rama of his coronation, counseling him on duties of kingship, while Rama accepts with joyful and humble submission.
theme: The sacred transmission of dharmic kingship from father to son

speaker: Narrator
text_sanskrit:
रामः प्रीतमनाश्चैव मातुः पादावुपस्पृशन् |
आपृच्छ्य कौसल्यामेव जगाम स्वं निवेशनम् || २-६-१
transliteration:
rāmaḥ prītamanāścaiva mātuḥ pādāvupaspṛśan |
āpṛcchya kausalyāmeva jagāma svaṃ niveśanam || 2-6-1
translation: Rama, with a joyful heart, touched his mother Kausalya's feet in reverence, took her leave, and went to his own dwelling.
commentary_full: Rama visits his mother Kausalya after receiving the coronation news. Kausalya is overjoyed and blesses him with all her heart. She performs prayers for his welfare and offers him food, for he will fast from this point. This sarga also describes Rama going to Sita to inform her of the next day's ceremony. Sita is told to observe a fast as well. The couple spends the night in prayer and meditation before the sacred ceremony. The joy of Kausalya, the tenderness of Sita, and Rama's composed piety paint a picture of domestic dharma at its finest.
